1.1.1: आ, ऐ, औ are the **वृद्धि** vowels.
1.1.2: अ, ए, ओ are the **गुण** vowels.
1.1.3: When a rule asks for **गुण** or **वृद्धि** but doesn't specify where, it changes the **इक्** vowel (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ).
1.1.4: Before an **आर्धधातुक** affix that drops part of the root, **गुण** and **वृद्धि** changes don't happen.
1.1.6: दीधी, वेवी, and the augment **इट्** never take **गुण** or **वृद्धि**.
1.1.7: Neighboring consonants (with no vowel between them) are **संयोग**.
1.1.8: A sound made through the nose along with the mouth is **अनुनासिक**.
1.1.9: Two sounds with the same place and the same effort of articulation are **सवर्ण**.
1.1.10: A vowel and a consonant are never **सवर्ण**, even with the same place and effort.
1.1.11: A dual ending in ई, ऊ, or ए is **प्रगृह्य** — it takes no सन्धि.
1.1.12: After the म् of अदस्, an ई, ऊ, or ए is **प्रगृह्य**.
1.1.13: The affix शे (its real form is ए) is **प्रगृह्य**.
1.1.14: A single-vowel **निपात**, other than आङ्, is **प्रगृह्य**.
1.1.16: A vocative singular ending in ओ before इति is optionally **प्रगृह्य**, by शाकल्य, outside Vedic texts.
1.1.17: उञ् before इति is optionally **प्रगृह्य**, by शाकल्य.
1.1.18: Outside Vedic texts, उञ् before इति optionally becomes ऊँ (long and nasal), which is **प्रगृह्य**, by शाकल्य.
1.1.19: A word ending in ई or ऊ that carries a locative sense is **प्रगृह्य**.
1.1.20: The roots shaped like दा and धा are **घु** — except दाप् and दैप्.
1.1.21: A rule for an initial or a final sound applies to a single sound that is both at once.
1.1.22: The affixes तरप् and तमप् are **घ**.
1.1.23: बहु, गण, and words ending in वतु or डति are **संख्या**.
1.1.24: A **संख्या** ending in ष् or न् is **षट्**.
1.1.25: A **संख्या** ending in डति is also **षट्**.
1.1.26: The affixes क्त and क्तवतु are **निष्ठा**.
1.1.27: सर्व and the rest of its list are **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.28: In a direction-naming **बहुव्रीहि**, सर्व and the rest are optionally **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.29: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, सर्व and the rest are not **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.30: In an instrumental **तत्पुरुष**, सर्व and the rest are not **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.31: In a **द्वन्द्व** compound, **सर्व** and the rest are not **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.32: Before the nominative plural **जस्**, a **द्वन्द्व** of these words is optionally **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.33: Before **जस्**, the words प्रथम, चरम, a word ending in **तय**, अल्प, अर्ध, कतिपय, and नेम are optionally **सर्वनाम**.
1.1.34: Before **जस्**, the words पूर्व, पर, अवर, दक्षिण, उत्तर, अपर, अधर are optionally **सर्वनाम** when they mark relative position — not when they are names.
1.1.35: Before **जस्**, स्व is optionally **सर्वनाम** when it does not mean a kinsman or wealth.
1.1.36: Before **जस्**, अन्तर is optionally **सर्वनाम** when it means 'outer' or 'an under-garment'.
1.1.37: The words स्वर् and the rest, and the **निपात** particles, are **अव्यय**.
1.1.38: A word ending in a **तद्धित** affix that does not take all the cases is **अव्यय**.
1.1.39: A word ending in a **कृत्** affix that ends in म् or in an **एच्** vowel (ए, ओ, ऐ, औ) is **अव्यय**.
1.1.40: A word ending in **क्त्वा**, **तोसुन्**, or **कसुन्** is **अव्यय**.
1.1.43: The first five case affixes of the **सुट्** (सु, औ, जस्, अम्, औट्) are **सर्वनामस्थान** — but not in the neuter.
1.1.45: An **इक्** vowel that replaces a **यण्** semivowel is **सम्प्रसारण**.
1.1.46: An **आगम** marked with ट् goes at the front of what it augments; one marked with क् goes at the end.
1.1.47: An **आगम** marked with म् goes right after the last vowel, becoming the final letter there.
1.1.48: When an **एच्** vowel (ए, ओ, ऐ, औ) is to be shortened, its short form is the matching **इक्** — ए, ऐ→इ; ओ, औ→उ.
1.1.49: A genitive in a rule means 'in place of'.
1.1.50: When a substitute could be one of several letters, the one closest to what it replaces is the **आदेश**.
1.1.51: When an **अण्** vowel (अ, इ, उ) replaces ऋ, it is followed by र्.
1.1.52: A substitute replaces only the final letter of what the genitive marks.
1.1.53: A substitute marked with ङ् replaces only the final letter, even when it has more than one letter.
1.1.54: When a substitute is given for what follows (marked by the ablative), it replaces only the first letter.
1.1.55: A substitute of more than one letter, or one marked with श्, replaces the whole of what the genitive marks.
1.1.56: An **आदेश** counts as its **स्थानिन्** — except for rules that look at the स्थानिन्'s actual letters.
1.1.57: An **आदेश** that replaces a vowel because of something following counts as its **स्थानिन्** for any rule acting on what comes before it.
1.1.58: That counting-as-the-स्थानिन् does not hold for rules about word-finals, doubling, the affix **वरच्**, **यलोप**, accent, **सवर्ण**, **अनुस्वार**, lengthening, or **जश्**/**चर्** substitution.
1.1.59: Before a vowel affix that triggers doubling, a vowel's **आदेश** counts as its **स्थानिन्** — keeping the original's very form — only for the doubling, then it reverts.
1.1.60: **लोप** is disappearance — not heard, not spoken, not written.
1.1.61: When a rule drops a **प्रत्यय** using the word **लुक्**, **श्लु**, or **लुप्**, that dropping takes the matching name — **लुक्**, **श्लु**, or **लुप्**.
1.1.62: After a **प्रत्यय** is dropped by **लोप**, rules still act as if it were there. (The dropped affix keeps causing whatever it would have caused.)
1.1.63: But a **प्रत्यय** dropped by a **लु**-word — **लुक्**, **श्लु**, or **लुप्** — leaves no trace, so it causes nothing on the **अङ्ग**.
1.1.64: The tail of a word, starting at its last vowel, is **टि**.
1.1.65: The letter just before the last letter is the **उपधा**.
1.1.66: A locative in a rule marks what comes just before the named thing — that is where the change lands.
1.1.67: An ablative in a rule marks what comes just after the named thing — that is where the change lands.
1.1.68: A word in a rule stands for its own form, not its meaning — except when the word is a **संज्ञा**, which stands for the things it names.
1.1.69: An **अण्** letter (a vowel or semivowel) and any term marked with **उ** stand for their **सवर्ण** letters too, as well as their own form — but not when they are a **प्रत्यय**.
1.1.70: A letter with **त्** next to it stands only for **सवर्ण** letters of its own length, plus its own form.
1.1.71: A **प्रत्याहार** is its first letter plus a final **इत्** letter, and it stands for itself and every letter between them.
1.1.72: When a rule acts on something by naming a feature, it acts on whatever ends in that feature too, as well as on the feature itself.
1.1.73: A word whose first vowel is a **वृद्धि** vowel is **वृद्ध**.
1.1.75: In a name for an eastern region, a word whose first vowel is **एङ्** (ए, ओ) is also **वृद्ध**.
1.2.1: After **गाङ्** and the **कुट्**-series roots, every **प्रत्यय** counts as **ङित्** — except a **ञित्** or **णित्** one.
1.2.2: After **विज्**, a **प्रत्यय** that starts with the augment **इट्** counts as **ङित्**.
1.2.3: After **ऊर्णु**, a **प्रत्यय** that starts with the augment **इट्** optionally counts as **ङित्**.
1.2.4: A **सार्वधातुक** affix that is not **पित्** counts as **ङित्**.
1.2.5: After a root not ending in a conjunct, a **लिट्** affix that is not **पित्** counts as **कित्**.
1.2.6: After **इन्ध्** and **भू**, the **लिट्** affixes count as **कित्**.
1.2.8: After **रुद्**, **विद्**, **मुष्**, **ग्रह्**, **स्वप्**, and **प्रच्छ्**, the affixes **क्त्वा** and **सन्** are **कित्**.
1.2.9: After a root ending in an **इक्** vowel (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ), a **सन्** that starts with a **झल्** consonant counts as **कित्**.
1.2.10: After a root ending in a consonant preceded by an **इक्** vowel, a **सन्** that starts with a **झल्** consonant counts as **कित्**.
1.2.11: After a root ending in a consonant preceded by an **इक्** vowel, the **लिङ्** and **सिच्** substitutes count as **कित्** when they start with a **झल्** consonant and an **आत्मनेपद** affix follows.
1.2.12: After a root ending in ऋ, the **लिङ्** and **सिच्** substitutes count as **कित्** when they start with a **झल्** consonant and an **आत्मनेपद** affix follows.
1.2.13: After **गम्**, the **लिङ्** and **सिच्** substitutes optionally count as **कित्** when they start with a **झल्** consonant and an **आत्मनेपद** affix follows.
1.2.14: After **हन्**, the **सिच्** counts as **कित्** before an **आत्मनेपद** affix.
1.2.15: After **यम्** meaning 'to divulge', the **सिच्** counts as **कित्** before an **आत्मनेपद** affix.
1.2.16: After यम् meaning 'to espouse', **सिच्** is optionally **कित्** before **आत्मनेपद** endings.
1.2.17: After स्था and the **घु** roots (दा, धा and the rest), **सिच्** is **कित्** before **आत्मनेपद** endings, and the root's आ becomes इ.
1.2.18: **क्त्वा** with the **इट्** augment (when it is **सेट्**) is not **कित्**.
1.2.19: After शीङ्, स्विद्, मिद्, क्ष्विद् and धृष्, a **सेट्** **निष्ठा** affix is not **कित्**.
1.2.20: After मृष् meaning 'to forbear', a **सेट्** **निष्ठा** affix is not **कित्**.
1.2.21: After a root with penultimate उ, a **सेट्** **निष्ठा** affix is optionally not **कित्** when it marks impersonal action or the start of an action.
1.2.22: After पूङ् 'to purify', a **सेट्** **निष्ठा** affix and **सेट्** **क्त्वा** are not **कित्**.
1.2.23: After a root with penultimate न् ending in थ् or फ्, **सेट्** **क्त्वा** is optionally not **कित्** (so the nasal may drop or stay).
1.2.24: After वञ्च्, लुञ्च् and ऋत्, **सेट्** **क्त्वा** is optionally not **कित्**.
1.2.25: After तृष्, मृष् and कृश्, **सेट्** **क्त्वा** is optionally not **कित्** — so holds काश्यप.
1.2.26: After a root that begins with a consonant, ends in a **रल्** letter (any consonant but य् or व्), and has इ/ई or उ/ऊ as its penultimate, **सेट्** **क्त्वा** and **सन्** are optionally **कित्**.
1.2.27: A vowel lasting as long as short उ is **ह्रस्व**, as long as ऊ is **दीर्घ**, and as long as the prolated ऊ३ is **प्लुत**.
1.2.28: When a rule says **ह्रस्व**, **दीर्घ** or **प्लुत** by name, it replaces a vowel only.
1.2.29: A vowel said with a high tone is **उदात्त**.
1.2.30: A vowel said with a low tone is **अनुदात्त**.
1.2.31: A vowel that combines the **उदात्त** and **अनुदात्त** tones is **स्वरित**.
1.2.32: In a **स्वरित** vowel, the first half-measure (a half short vowel's length) is **उदात्त**; the rest is **अनुदात्त**.
1.2.33: In calling out to someone far off, the tone is **एकश्रुति** — one flat pitch, no accents.
1.2.34: In sacrificial work the **मन्त्र**s are said in **एकश्रुति**, except for **जप**, the **न्यूङ्ख** vowels and the **सामन्**s.
1.2.35: In sacrificial work the **वषट्** may instead be said in a still higher tone, or in **एकश्रुति**.
1.2.36: In the **छन्दस्** the **एकश्रुति** is optional — otherwise the three accents stand.
1.2.37: In the **सुब्रह्मण्या** there is no **एकश्रुति**, and a vowel that would be **स्वरित** becomes **उदात्त** instead.
1.2.38: In the **सुब्रह्मण्या**, देव and ब्राह्मण keep their **अनुदात्त** (the **स्वरित** there becomes **अनुदात्त**, not **उदात्त**).
1.2.40: An **अनुदात्त** vowel that comes right before an **उदात्त** or **स्वरित** becomes **सन्नतर** (lower still than **अनुदात्त**).
1.2.41: A **प्रत्यय** of a single letter is **अपृक्त**.
1.2.42: A **तत्पुरुष** whose members share one case is a **कर्मधारय**.
1.2.43: In the compound rules, the word stated in the nominative is the **उपसर्जन**.
1.2.44: A word fixed in one case (while its partner's case varies) is also **उपसर्जन** — but not for the rule that puts the **उपसर्जन** first.
1.2.45: A meaningful word-form that is neither a **धातु** nor a **प्रत्यय** is a **प्रातिपदिक**.
1.2.46: Words ending in a **कृत्** affix, words ending in a **तद्धित** affix, and **समास** compounds are also **प्रातिपदिक**.
1.2.47: In the neuter, a **प्रातिपदिक**'s final vowel shortens.
1.2.48: When गो or a feminine-affix ending sits as an **उपसर्जन** at the end of a **प्रातिपदिक**, its final vowel shortens.
1.2.49: When a **तद्धित** affix drops by **लुक्**, the feminine affix of the **उपसर्जन** drops by **लुक्** too.
1.2.50: When a **तद्धित** drops by **लुक्** after गोणी, its final ई becomes इ (instead of dropping).
1.2.51: When a **तद्धित** drops by **लुप्**, the word keeps the gender and number of the base it came from.
1.2.52: After a **लुप्**-drop, adjectives qualifying the word also take its gender and number — unless the word names a **जाति**.
1.2.53: None of this gender-and-number matching needs stating: these are fixed names (**संज्ञा**), and their gender and number come built in.
1.2.54: The rules that teach **लुप्**-elision need not be stated either, since the base's meaning never shows through anyway.
1.2.55: And if you did make the base's meaning the test, the word ought to vanish whenever that meaning is absent — which it doesn't.
1.2.56: No rule need tie a word's meaning to its principal member (**प्रधान**) or to its affix (**प्रत्यय**): meaning comes from elsewhere — ordinary usage.
1.2.57: The same goes for rules fixing the sense of tense (**काल**) and of **उपसर्जन**: no need to state them, since usage settles them.
1.2.58: A **जाति** name for one thing optionally takes the plural.
1.2.59: अस्मद् optionally takes the plural even for one or two.
1.2.60: The asterisms फल्गुनी and प्रोष्ठपदा, being dual, optionally take the plural.
1.2.61: In the Vedas, the dual asterism पुनर्वसू optionally takes the singular.
1.2.62: In the Vedas, the dual asterism विशाखा optionally takes the singular.
1.2.63: In a **द्वन्द्व** of the asterisms तिष्य and पुनर्वसु, the plural always becomes dual.
1.2.64: Of identical word-forms with the same case ending standing together, only the last stays; the rest drop (**एकशेष**).
1.2.65: A **वृद्ध** (गोत्र) word and a **युवन्** word that differ only by their affixes — only the **वृद्ध** stays.
1.2.66: Likewise a feminine **वृद्ध** word with its **युवन्** word — only the feminine stays, and it acts masculine.
1.2.67: A masculine word and its feminine counterpart, differing only by the gender affix — only the masculine stays.
1.2.68: भ्रातृ with स्वसृ, and पुत्र with दुहितृ — only भ्रातृ, only पुत्र stay.
1.2.69: A neuter word with its non-neuter counterpart, differing only by affix — the neuter optionally stays, and it acts singular.
1.2.70: पितृ with मातृ — only पितृ optionally stays.
1.2.71: श्वशुर with श्वश्रू — only श्वशुर optionally stays.
1.2.72: A त्यद्-series pronoun with any other word — the त्यद्-word always stays.
1.2.73: For a herd of grown domestic animals, the feminine word stays.
1.3.1: The action-words starting with भू are the **धातु** (verbal roots).
1.3.2: In **उपदेश**, a nasalized vowel is **इत्** (a marker, not part of the form).
1.3.4: In a **विभक्ति** affix, a final त-class consonant, स्, or म् is not **इत्**.
1.3.5: At the start of a root, ञि, टु, or डु is **इत्**.
1.3.6: The first letter of a **प्रत्यय**, if ष्, is **इत्**.
1.3.7: The first letter of a **प्रत्यय**, if a palatal (च्, छ्, ज्, झ्, ञ्) or a retroflex (ट्, ठ्, ड्, ढ्, ण्), is **इत्**.
1.3.8: The first letter of a **प्रत्यय** that is not a **तद्धित**, if ल्, श्, or a guttural (क्, ख्, ग्, घ्, ङ्), is **इत्**.
1.3.9: An **इत्** drops — the whole of it, not just its last letter.
1.3.10: When a rule lists equal numbers of things and their replacements, match them up in order — first to first, second to second.
1.3.11: A word marked with a **स्वरित** accent governs the rules that follow it (an **अधिकार**).
1.3.14: For the agent, when the action is reciprocal (each does to the other), the root takes **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.15: But a root meaning motion or injury does not take **आत्मनेपद** for reciprocal action.
1.3.16: And a root with इतरेतर or अन्योन्य as its **उपपद** does not take **आत्मनेपद**, even for reciprocal action.
1.3.18: After परि, वि, or अव, क्री takes **आत्मनेपद** — even when the fruit of the action does not go to the agent.
1.3.19: After वि or परा, जि takes **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.20: After आङ्, दा takes **आत्मनेपद** when it does not mean opening the mouth — even when the fruit does not go to the agent.
1.3.21: After अनु, सम्, परि, or आङ्, क्रीड् takes **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.22: After सम्, अव, प्र, or वि, स्था takes **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.23: स्था takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means making one's intentions known, or acting as an arbitrator.
1.3.24: After उत्, स्था takes **आत्मनेपद** when it does not mean rising up.
1.3.25: After उप, स्था takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means worship with hymns.
1.3.26: After उप, स्था takes **आत्मनेपद** when it is intransitive.
1.3.27: After उत् or वि, तप् takes **आत्मनेपद** when it is intransitive.
1.3.28: After आङ्, यम् and हन् take **आत्मनेपद** when intransitive.
1.3.29: After सम्, the roots गम्, ऋच्छ्, प्रच्छ्, स्वर्, ऋ, श्रु, and विद् take **आत्मनेपद** when intransitive.
1.3.30: After नि, सम्, उप, or वि, ह्वे takes **आत्मनेपद** — even when the fruit does not go to the agent.
1.3.31: After आङ्, ह्वे takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means challenging a rival — even when the fruit does not go to the agent.
1.3.32: कृ takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means informing maliciously, reviling, serving, acting with violence, altering a thing, reciting, or putting to use — even when the fruit does not go to the agent.
1.3.33: After **कृ** with **अधि**, when it means to overcome or stay undefeated, use **आत्मनेपद** — even when the action's fruit doesn't go to the agent.
1.3.34: After **कृ** with **वि**, when its object is a sound, use **आत्मनेपद** — even when the fruit doesn't go to the agent.
1.3.35: After **कृ** with **वि**, when it takes no object, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.36: After **नी** (**णीञ्**), use **आत्मनेपद** when it means: to honor, to lift up, to make someone a teacher, to settle a meaning, to hire for wages, to pay off, or to give away — even when the fruit doesn't go to the agent.
1.3.37: After **नी**, when its object is bodiless and sits in the agent, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.38: After **क्रम्**, when it means steady flow, drive, or growth, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.39: After **क्रम्** with **उप** or **पर**, when it means steady flow, drive, or growth, use **आत्मनेपद** — and only after these two prefixes.
1.3.40: After **क्रम्** with **आङ्**, when it means a heavenly body rising, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.41: After **क्रम्** with **वि**, when it means stepping or pacing, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.42: After **क्रम्** with **प्र** or **उप**, when the two prefixes mean the same thing — beginning an action — use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.43: After **क्रम्** with no prefix, optionally use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.44: After **ज्ञा**, when it means to deny or disown, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.45: After **ज्ञा**, when it takes no object, use **आत्मनेपद** — when the fruit doesn't go to the agent.
1.3.46: After **ज्ञा** with **सम्** or **प्रति**, use **आत्मनेपद** — except when it means longing remembrance.
1.3.47: After **वद्**, use **आत्मनेपद** when it means: to shine forth, to coax, to know thoroughly, to strive, to differ in opinion, or to entice.
1.3.48: After **वद्**, when clear-speaking beings speak together at once, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.49: After **वद्** with **अनु**, when it takes no object and means clear speech, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.50: After **वद्**, when clear-speaking beings wrangle and contradict each other at once, optionally use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.52: After **गॄ** with **सम्**, when it means to promise, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.53: After **चर्** with **उत्**, when it takes an object, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.54: After **चर्** with **सम्**, when tied to a word in the instrumental (third case), use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.55: After **दा** with **सम्**, when tied to an instrumental (third case) that carries dative (fourth case) sense, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.56: After **यम्** with **उप**, when it means taking a wife, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.57: After the desiderative (**सन्**) of **ज्ञा**, **श्रु**, **स्मृ**, or **दृश्**, use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.58: After the desiderative of **ज्ञा** with **अनु**, do not use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.59: After the desiderative of **श्रु** with **प्रति** or **आङ्**, do not use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.60: After **शद्** (to decay), when its affix is **शित्** (marked with **श्**), use **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.61: After **मृ** (to die), use **आत्मनेपद** only with a **शित्** affix and with **लुङ्** (aorist) and **लिङ्** (benedictive) — nowhere else.
1.3.62: A desiderative (**सन्**) verb takes **आत्मनेपद** wherever the plain root would — the same trigger carries over.
1.3.63: When **कृ** is the auxiliary in the periphrastic perfect (after **आम्**), it takes **आत्मनेपद** just like the verb that took **आम्** — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.64: After प्र or उप, **युज्** takes **आत्मनेपद** — except about sacrificial vessels — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.67: A causative (**णि**) takes **आत्मनेपद** when the non-causative object becomes the causative's agent — but not when it means 'remember with regret' — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.68: The causatives of **भी** 'fear' and **स्मि** 'wonder' take **आत्मनेपद** when the causing agent itself produces the fear — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.69: The causatives of **गृध** and **वञ्च्** take **आत्मनेपद** when they mean 'deceive' — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.70: The causative of **लि** takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means 'show respect', 'subdue', or 'deceive' — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.71: The causative of **कृ** with **मिथ्या** as **उपपद** takes **आत्मनेपद** when it means 'say wrong over and over' — even when the fruit doesn't reach the agent.
1.3.72: A verb marked **स्वरित** or **ञित्** takes **आत्मनेपद** when the fruit of the action reaches the agent.
1.3.73: After अप, **वद्** 'tell' takes **आत्मनेपद** when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.74: A causative (**णिच्**) takes **आत्मनेपद** when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.75: After सम्, उत्, or आङ्, **यम्** takes **आत्मनेपद** when the fruit reaches the agent — but not about a book.
1.3.76: **ज्ञा** with no **उपसर्ग** takes **आत्मनेपद** when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.77: When an **उपपद** already shows the fruit reaching the agent, **आत्मनेपद** is optional.
1.3.78: Every other verb — those no earlier rule claimed for **आत्मनेपद** — takes **परस्मैपद** for the agent.
1.3.79: After अनु or परा, **कृ** takes **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.80: After अभि, प्रति, or अति, **क्षिप्** takes **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.81: After प्र, **वह्** takes **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.82: After परि, **मृष्** takes **परस्मैपद** when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.85: After उप, **रम्** used intransitively takes **परस्मैपद** optionally.
1.3.86: The causatives of बुध्, युध्, नश्, जन, इङ्, प्रु, द्रु, स्रु take **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.87: The causatives of verbs meaning 'swallow' or 'shake/move' take **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.88: A causative whose plain verb was intransitive with a thinking agent takes **परस्मैपद**, even when the fruit reaches the agent.
1.3.89: But the causatives of पा, दम्, आयम्, आयस्, परिमुह, रुच्, नृत्, वद्, वस् do not take **परस्मैपद** — they keep **आत्मनेपद**.
1.3.90: A denominative ending in **क्यष्** takes **परस्मैपद** optionally.
1.3.91: In the aorist (**लुङ्**), द्युत् and its group take **परस्मैपद** optionally.
1.3.92: Before **स्य** (future/conditional) and **सन्** (desiderative), वृत् and its group take **परस्मैपद** optionally.
1.3.93: After **कृप्** 'be fit', **परस्मैपद** is optional in the **लुट्** (periphrastic future), and also before **स्य** and **सन्**.
1.4.1: From here through **कडाराः कर्मधारये** [[2.2.38]], each thing gets only one **संज्ञा** (no piling up of names).
1.4.2: When two rules of equal strength clash, the later one wins. (Exception/general, fixed/optional, **अन्तरङ्ग**/**बहिरङ्ग** are not equal strength — the stronger one wins there.)
1.4.3: A feminine word-form ending in long ई or ऊ is **नदी**.
1.4.4: A feminine ई/ऊ word that takes **इयङ्** or **उवङ्** [[6.1.77]] is not **नदी** — except **स्त्री**, which stays **नदी**.
1.4.5: Before **आम्** (genitive plural), an **इयङ्**/**उवङ्** feminine ई/ऊ word is optionally **नदी** — but **स्त्री** is always **नदी**.
1.4.6: Before a **ङित्** case-affix, a feminine short इ/उ word, and an **इयङ्**/**उवङ्** feminine ई/ऊ word, are optionally **नदी** — but **स्त्री** is always **नदी**.
1.4.7: Every other word ending in short इ or उ is **घि**, except **सखि**.
1.4.9: In the **छन्दस्**, **पति** joined to a genitive word is optionally **घि**.
1.4.11: Before a conjunct consonant, a short vowel is **गुरु**.
1.4.13: When a **प्रत्यय** is added after a root or **प्रातिपदिक**, the form starting from that base, taken with the affix following, is the **अङ्ग**.
1.4.14: A form ending in **सुप्** [[4.1.2]] or **तिङ्** [[3.4.78]] is a **पद**.
1.4.15: Before **क्य** (the affixes **क्यच्**, **क्यङ्**, **क्यष्**), a form ending in न् is a **पद**.
1.4.16: Before a **सित्** affix, what comes before it is a **पद**.
1.4.17: Before the affixes from **सु** [[4.1.2]] through **कप्** [[5.4.151]], when they are not **सर्वनामस्थान**, what comes before is a **पद**.
1.4.18: Before such an affix (from **सु** to **कप्**, not **सर्वनामस्थान**) that starts with य् or a vowel, what comes before is **भ** instead.
1.4.19: A form ending in त् or स् is **भ** before an affix carrying the sense of **मतुप्** ('having it') [[5.2.94]].
1.4.20: Words like **अयस्मय** are valid forms in the **छन्दस्** (formed by the **भ**/**पद** rules).
1.4.21: For many, the plural affix is used.
1.4.22: For two, the dual affix; for one, the singular affix.
1.4.23: From here on, **कारक** (a thing in relation to the action) is in force.
1.4.24: The fixed point that something moves away from is **अपादान**.
1.4.25: With verbs of fearing or protecting, the source of the fear is **अपादान**.
1.4.26: With **पराजि** 'find unbearable', what one cannot endure is **अपादान**.
1.4.27: With verbs of warding off, the desired thing one is kept from is **अपादान**.
1.4.28: In hiding, the one whose sight you want to escape is **अपादान**.
1.4.29: In formal learning, the teacher one learns from is **अपादान**.
1.4.30: With जन् (be born), the source the agent springs from is the **अपादान**.
1.4.31: With भू (arise), the source the agent springs from is the **अपादान**.
1.4.32: The one the agent aims the object of giving at is the **सम्प्रदान** (the recipient).
1.4.33: With verbs meaning like रुच् (please), the one who is pleased is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.34: With श्लाघ् (praise), ह्नु (deny), स्था (offer oneself), शप् (curse), the one you want to make aware of it is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.35: With धारि (owe), the creditor is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.36: With स्पृह् (desire), the thing desired is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.37: With verbs meaning क्रुध् (be angry), द्रुह् (harm), ईर्ष्या (envy), असूया (find fault), the one the anger is aimed at is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.38: But when क्रुध् and द्रुह् carry a preposition, the one the anger is aimed at is instead the **कर्म**.
1.4.39: With राध् and ईक्ष् (read someone's fortune), the one whose luck is being asked about is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.40: With श्रु after प्रति or आङ् (promise), the one who prompted the promise — the agent of that prior act — is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.41: And with गृ after अनु or प्रति (chant in response, to cheer on), the one who chanted first — the agent of that prior act — is the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.42: The most effective means of getting the action done is the **करण**.
1.4.43: With दिव् (play, gamble), that most effective means is the **कर्म** — and the **करण** too.
1.4.44: With परिक्री (hire for wages), the most effective means is optionally the **सम्प्रदान**.
1.4.45: The site that holds the action is the **अधिकरण**.
1.4.46: With शीङ् (lie), स्था (stand), आस् (sit) after अधि, the site is instead the **कर्म**.
1.4.47: With विश् after अभिनि (settle into), the site is also the **कर्म**.
1.4.48: With वस् (dwell) after उप, अनु, अधि, or आङ्, the site is the **कर्म**.
1.4.49: What the agent most wants to reach by the action is the **कर्म**.
1.4.50: Anything else caught up in the action the same way — even if unwanted — is also the **कर्म**.
1.4.51: And any **कारक** not pinned down as **अपादान** or the rest is the **कर्म**.
1.4.52: For verbs of motion, knowing, or eating, verbs whose object is something spoken, and intransitive verbs, the plain verb's agent becomes the **कर्म** once the verb takes causative णि.
1.4.53: With हृ (carry) and कृ (do), the plain verb's agent optionally becomes the **कर्म** once the verb takes णि.
1.4.54: Whatever the speaker treats as acting on its own is the **कर्ता**.
1.4.55: Whatever drives that **कर्ता** is the **हेतु** — and a **कर्ता** too.
1.4.56: From here up to अधिरीश्वरे (1.4.97), every word named is a **निपात**.
1.4.57: च and the rest are **निपात**s when they do not name a thing (a substance).
1.4.58: प्र and the rest are **निपात**s (when they do not name a thing).
1.4.59: प्र and the rest are **उपसर्ग**s when joined to a verb.
1.4.60: A word like प्र, joined to a verb, is also a **गति**.
1.4.61: The उरी-group words, and words ending in **च्वि** or **डाच्**, are **गति** when joined to कृ, भू, or अस्.
1.4.62: A sound-imitating word joined to a verb is a **गति**, unless इति follows it.
1.4.63: सत् and असत् joined to a verb are **गति** when they mean respect and disrespect.
1.4.64: अलम् joined to a verb is a **गति** when it means adornment.
1.4.65: अन्तर् joined to a verb is a **गति** when it means letting go (not taking up).
1.4.66: कणे and मनस् joined to a verb are **गति** when they mean drinking one's fill until the craving turns back.
1.4.67: The indeclinable पुरस् joined to a verb is a **गति**.
1.4.68: The indeclinable अस्तम् joined to a verb is also a **गति**.
1.4.69: The indeclinable अच्छ is a **गति** before a verb of motion or before वद्.
1.4.70: अदस् joined to a verb is a **गति** when it is not pointing something out to another.
1.4.71: तिरस् joined to a verb is a **गति** when it means vanishing.
1.4.72: Before कृ, तिरस् (meaning vanishing) is optionally a **गति**.
1.4.73: उपाजे and अन्वाजे, meaning propping up the weak, are optionally **गति** before कृ.
1.4.74: साक्षात् and the rest are optionally **गति** before कृ.
1.4.75: उरसि and मनसि are optionally **गति** before कृ, except when they mean physically placing.
1.4.76: मध्ये, पदे, and निवचने are optionally **गति** before कृ, except when they mean physically placing.
1.4.77: हस्ते and पाणौ are always **गति** before कृ when the sense is marrying.
1.4.78: The indeclinable प्राध्वम् is always a **गति** before कृ when the sense is binding.
1.4.79: जीविका and उपनिषद् are **गति** before कृ when the sense is likeness.
1.4.80: The **गति** and **उपसर्ग** words go before the verb.
1.4.81: In the **छन्दस्**, these **गति** and **उपसर्ग** words may also go after the verb.
1.4.82: In the **छन्दस्**, these **गति** and **उपसर्ग** words are also seen split off from the verb by words in between.
1.4.83: From here through 1.4.97, the words named are **कर्मप्रवचनीय**.
1.4.84: अनु is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it marks a sign or attendant cause.
1.4.85: अनु is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it carries the force of the instrumental (with, alongside).
1.4.86: अनु is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means being lesser than something.
1.4.87: उप is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means being more than, and also when it means being less than.
1.4.88: अप and परि are **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when they mean leaving out.
1.4.89: आङ् is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it marks a limit (up to, whether including or excluding the endpoint).
1.4.90: प्रति, परि, and अनु are **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when they mean a sign/direction toward something, a mere statement of circumstance ("as regards"), a share, or pervasion ("one after another").
1.4.91: अभि is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** in those same senses — but not in the sense of a share.
1.4.92: प्रति is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means a stand-in ("in place of") or an exchange ("in return for").
1.4.93: अधि and परि are **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when they add no meaning at all (so they don't become **उपसर्ग** or **गति**).
1.4.94: सु is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means praise ("excellently").
1.4.95: अति is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means going too far ("excessively") — and, by च, also when it means praise.
1.4.96: अपि is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** in the senses of an unspoken word, possibility, leave-to-do-as-one-likes, blame, or joining ("and").
1.4.97: अधि is **कर्मप्रवचनीय** when it means a master — marking the master-and-property relation.
1.4.98: अधि is optionally **कर्मप्रवचनीय** before the verb कृ.
1.4.100: The **तङ्** affixes and the two ending in आन (शानच्, कानच्), as replacements of ल, are **आत्मनेपद**.
1.4.101: Take the **तिङ्** affixes three at a time: each triad is, in order, **प्रथम** (3rd person), **मध्यम** (2nd), **उत्तम** (1st).
1.4.102: Within each such triad, the three are, one by one, **एकवचन** (singular), **द्विवचन** (dual), and **बहुवचन** (plural).
1.4.103: The **सुप्** affixes too, three at a time, are **एकवचन**, **द्विवचन**, and **बहुवचन**.
1.4.104: Each triad of **तिङ्** and **सुप्** affixes is also a **विभक्ति**.
1.4.105: When युष्मद् ("you") agrees with the verb — whether the word is actually there or just understood — the verb takes the **मध्यम** (2nd person).
1.4.106: When mockery is meant and मन्य ("think") stands by, the verb takes **मध्यम** (2nd person), and मन्य itself takes **उत्तम** (1st person) singular.
1.4.107: When अस्मद् ("I") agrees with the verb — present or merely understood — the verb takes the **उत्तम** (1st person).
1.4.108: Everywhere else — when neither "you" nor "I" agrees with the verb — it takes the **प्रथम** (3rd person).
1.4.109: The tightest closeness of sounds, a gap of half a **मात्रा** between them, is **संहिता**.
1.4.110: A stop, with no sound following, is **अवसान**.
2.1.1: A **पदविधि** (any rule operating on finished **पद**, not on roots) applies only when the words are **समर्थ** — connected in sense.
2.1.2: When an accent rule applies, a word ending in **सुप्** that stands before a vocative counts as part of the **अङ्ग** of that vocative.
2.1.3: From here up to कडाराः कर्मधारये [[2.2.38]], everything specified is a **समास**.
2.1.4: सह सुपा — "together with a word ending in **सुप्**" — carries into the following sūtras.
2.1.5: From here forward, the **समास** specified is an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.6: An **अव्यय** carrying the sense of a **विभक्ति**, or nearness, prosperity, lack of prosperity, absence, departure, not-now, the rise of a sound, after, according-to, sequence, simultaneity, likeness, becoming, totality, or ending, combines with a connected word ending in **सुप्** to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.7: यथा, when it does not mean likeness, combines with a connected word ending in **सुप्** to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.8: यावत्, when it means limitation, combines with a connected word ending in **सुप्** to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.9: A word ending in **सुप्** combines with प्रति, when प्रति means "a little," to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.10: अक्ष, शलाका, and a **संख्या** combine with परि to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.12: अप, परि, बहिस्, and words ending in अञ्चु optionally combine with a word ending in the fifth **विभक्ति** to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.13: आङ्, when it marks a limit excluded or included, optionally combines with a word ending in the fifth **विभक्ति** to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.14: अभि and प्रति, when they mean "facing toward," optionally combine with a word ending in **सुप्** that names the mark aimed at, forming an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.15: अनु optionally combines with the word whose nearness it marks, forming an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.16: अनु optionally combines with the word whose length it marks, forming an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.17: And तिष्ठद्गु, वहद्गु, खलेयवम् and the rest are **अव्ययीभाव** — irregularly fixed compounds, and nothing else.
2.1.18: पार and मध्य optionally combine with a word ending in the sixth **विभक्ति**, taking the forms परे and मध्ये, to form an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.19: A **संख्या** optionally combines with a word naming one who belongs to a lineage, forming an **अव्ययीभाव**.
2.1.20: A **संख्या** optionally combines with river-names, forming an **अव्ययीभाव** that means their aggregate.
2.1.21: A word ending in **सुप्** combines with a river-name to form an **अव्ययीभाव**, when the whole is a name for something other than its parts.
2.1.22: From here up to बहुव्रीहि [[2.2.23]], the **समास** specified is a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.24: A word ending in the second **विभक्ति** combines with श्रित, अतीत, पतित, गत, अत्यस्त, प्राप्त, or आपन्न to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.25: स्वयम् combines with a word ending in **क्त** to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.26: खट्वा in the second **विभक्ति** combines with a word ending in **क्त**, when censure is meant, to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.27: सामि ("half") combines with a word ending in **क्त** to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.28: Time-words in the second **विभक्ति** optionally combine with a word ending in **क्त** to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.29: And time-words in the second **विभक्ति** optionally combine with a word ending in **सुप्**, when unbroken connection through that whole time is meant, to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.30: A word ending in the third **विभक्ति** optionally combines with a quality-word — the quality being one the third-case thing produced — or with अर्थ, to form a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.31: A word in the instrumental (third case) compounds with पूर्व, सदृश, सम, a word meaning 'less', कलह, निपुण, मिश्र, or श्लक्ष्ण, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.32: A word in the instrumental (third case) marking the agent or instrument compounds, with much latitude, with a word ending in a **कृत्** affix, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.33: A word in the instrumental (third case) marking the agent or instrument optionally compounds with a word ending in a **कृत्य** affix when the statement exaggerates (praise or blame), giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.34: A word in the instrumental (third case) naming a condiment optionally compounds with a word naming the food it flavors, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.35: A word in the instrumental (third case) naming what is mixed in compounds with a word naming the eatable, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.36: A word in the dative (fourth case) compounds with a word naming what serves that purpose, and with अर्थ, बलि, हित, सुख, or रक्षित, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.37: A word in the ablative (fifth case) optionally compounds with भय, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.38: A word in the ablative (fifth case) compounds with अपेत, अपोढ, मुक्त, पतित, or अपत्रस्त when the separation is slight and gradual, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.39: A word meaning स्तोक, अन्तिक, दूर, or कृच्छ्र in the ablative (fifth case) compounds with a word ending in **क्त**, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.40: A word in the locative (seventh case) compounds with शौण्ड and the rest of its list, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.41: A word in the locative (seventh case) compounds with सिद्ध, शुष्क, पक्व, or बन्ध, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.42: A word in the locative (seventh case) compounds with ध्वाङ्क्ष or another word for 'crow' when contempt is meant, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.43: A word in the locative (seventh case) compounds with a word ending in a **कृत्य** affix when a debt due within that time is meant, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.44: A word in the locative (seventh case) always compounds with another case-inflected word when the whole is a name (**संज्ञा**), giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.45: A word naming a part of day or night, in the locative (seventh case), compounds with a word ending in **क्त**, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.46: तत्र compounds with a word ending in **क्त**, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.47: A word in the locative (seventh case) compounds with a word ending in **क्त** when censure is meant, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.48: पात्रेसमित and the rest of its list are **तत्पुरुष** compounds when contempt is meant.
2.1.49: A word naming a prior-in-time action, and the words एक, सर्व, जरत्, पुराण, नव, and केवल, compound with a case-inflected word in the same case, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.50: A word for a direction or a **संख्या** compounds with a case-inflected word in the same case when the whole is a name (**संज्ञा**), giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.51: A word for a direction or a **संख्या** compounds with a case-inflected word in the same case when a **तद्धित** sense is meant, or a further member follows, or an aggregate is meant, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.52: In those three cases (the **तद्धित** sense, a following member, an aggregate), a compound whose first member is a **संख्या** is a **द्विगु**.
2.1.53: A case-inflected word naming something low compounds with a case-inflected word of contempt, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.54: पाप and अणक compound with case-inflected words naming something low, standing first, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.55: A case-inflected word naming the standard of comparison compounds with a word naming the shared quality, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.56: A case-inflected word naming the thing compared compounds with व्याघ्र and the rest of its list (the standard), so long as no word for the shared quality is used, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.57: A case-inflected qualifier (**विशेषण**) compounds, with much latitude, with the case-inflected thing it qualifies (**विशेष्य**) in the same case, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.58: पूर्व, अपर, प्रथम, चरम, जघन्य, समान, मध्य, मध्यम, and वीर compound with a case-inflected word in the same case, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.59: श्रेणी and the rest of its list compound with कृत and the rest of its list, in the same case, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.60: A word ending in **क्त** without नञ् compounds with the same word ending in **क्त** but carrying नञ्, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.61: सत्, महत्, परम, उत्तम, उत्कृष्ट compound with a word naming the respected person, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.62: A case-inflected word naming the respected thing compounds with वृन्दारक, नाग, कुञ्जर, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.63: कतर and कतम, when they ask which class something belongs to, compound with the word they govern, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.64: किम्, when it expresses contempt, compounds with a case-inflected word, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.65: A case-inflected word naming a **जाति** compounds with पोटा, युवति, स्तोक, कतिपय, गृष्टि, धेनु, वशा, वेहत्, बष्कयणी, प्रवक्तृ, श्रोत्रिय, अध्यापक, धूर्त, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.66: A case-inflected word naming a **जाति** compounds with a word of praise, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.67: युवन् compounds with खलति, पलित, वलिन, जरती when they agree in case, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.68: A word ending in a **कृत्** affix, and तुल्य with its synonyms, compound with an agreeing word that does not name a **जाति**, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.69: A case-inflected word naming a colour compounds with an agreeing case-inflected word that also names a colour, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.70: कुमार compounds with the agreeing words श्रमणा and the rest, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.71: A case-inflected word naming a quadruped compounds with the agreeing word गर्भिणी, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.1.72: मयूरव्यंसक and the rest are **तत्पुरुष** by name (irregularly formed, and only these fixed forms count).
2.2.1: पूर्व, अपर, अधर, उत्तर compound with a word naming a whole that has parts, when that whole is numerically one, and take first place; the compound is **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.2: अर्ध, when it is neuter and means an exact half, compounds with a word naming a whole that has parts, when that whole is numerically one, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.3: द्वितीय, तृतीय, चतुर्थ, तुर्य optionally compound with a word naming a whole that has parts, when that whole is numerically one, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.4: प्राप्त and आपन्न optionally compound with a word in the accusative, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.5: Words naming a stretch of time compound with the word whose duration that time measures, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.6: नञ् compounds with the case-inflected word it governs, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.7: ईषत् compounds with a case-inflected word that does not end in a **कृत्** affix, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.8: A word in the genitive compounds with the case-inflected word it governs, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.9: A word in the genitive compounds with याजक and the rest, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.10: A genitive does not compound when it singles one out from a group (**निर्धारण**).
2.2.11: A genitive does not compound with an ordinal, a quality-word, a word for satisfaction, a participle in **सत्**, an indeclinable, a word in **तव्य**, or an agreeing word naming the same thing.
2.2.12: A genitive does not compound with a word ending in **क्त** when the **क्त** expresses respect (and likewise inclination or understanding).
2.2.13: A genitive does not compound with a word ending in **क्त** when the **क्त** names the place where the action happened.
2.2.14: A genitive does not compound when it carries the force of the accusative (the object).
2.2.15: A genitive does not compound with a word ending in **तृच्** or अक when the genitive carries the force of the agent.
2.2.16: A genitive does not compound with a word ending in **तृच्** or अक when that affix carries the force of the agent.
2.2.17: A genitive always compounds with a word ending in अक when that अक names a game or a livelihood, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.18: कु, the **गति** particles, and प्र and the rest always compound with the word they govern, giving a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.19: An **उपपद** that does not end in a tense-**प्रत्यय** always compounds with the word it goes with, forming a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.20: An **उपपद** compounds with an **अव्यय** only when that **अव्यय** ends in अम्.
2.2.21: An **उपपद** in the third case or any later case optionally compounds with an अम्-ending **अव्यय**, forming a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.22: An **उपपद** in the third case or any later case optionally compounds with a word ending in **क्त्वा**, forming a **तत्पुरुष**.
2.2.23: Any compound left over, not covered by the rules above, is a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.24: Two or more inflected words compound to name something other than what they name singly, forming a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.25: An **अव्यय**, and आसन्न, अदूर, अधिक, and a **संख्या** compound with another **संख्या** when the sense is a number, forming a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.26: Names of the directions compound to name an intermediate direction, forming a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.27: Two like-formed words, both in the locative or both in the instrumental, compound in the sense 'this happens therein / by that', forming a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.28: सह compounds with a word in the third case when companion and accompanied share equally in an action, forming a **बहुव्रीहि**.
2.2.29: Several inflected words standing in an 'and' relation compound into a **द्वन्द्व**.
2.2.30: The **उपसर्जन** stands first in a compound.
2.2.31: In राजदन्त and the like, the **उपसर्जन** stands last.
2.2.32: In a **द्वन्द्व**, a **घि** word stands first.
2.2.33: In a **द्वन्द्व**, the word that begins with a vowel and ends in short अ stands first.
2.2.34: In a **द्वन्द्व**, the word with fewer vowels stands first.
2.2.35: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, a word in the seventh case and a qualifier stand first.
2.2.36: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, a word ending in **निष्ठा** stands first.
2.2.37: In अहिताग्नि and the like, the **निष्ठा**-ending word stands first optionally.
2.2.38: कडार and the like stand first optionally in a **कर्मधारय**.
2.3.1: From here on, **अनभिहिते** governs: a case-**प्रत्यय** is added only when its sense is not already conveyed by a verb, **कृत्**, **तद्धित**, or compound.
2.3.2: The second case marks the object, when the object is not already conveyed.
2.3.3: In the **छन्दस्**, the object of हु takes the third case, and the second case as well.
2.3.4: A word governed by अन्तरा or अन्तरेण takes the second case.
2.3.5: A word for time or distance takes the second case when it spans an unbroken whole duration.
2.3.6: A word for time or distance takes the third case when the action reaches completion across it.
2.3.7: A word for time or distance takes the seventh or fifth case when it is the interval between two **कारक**s.
2.3.8: A word governed by a **कर्मप्रवचनीय** takes the second case.
2.3.9: When a **कर्मप्रवचनीय** governs a word in the sense 'more than which' or 'lord of which', that word takes the seventh case.
2.3.10: A word governed by the **कर्मप्रवचनीय**s अप, आङ्, or परि takes the fifth case.
2.3.11: After the noun governed by the **कर्मप्रवचनीय** प्रति in the sense of substitute or exchange, use the 5th case (अभिमन्युरर्जुनतः प्रति, माषानस्मै तिलेभ्यः प्रति यच्छति).
2.3.12: With a root of motion, the goal as **कर्म** takes the 2nd or the 4th case — but only for physical motion, and not when the goal is a word for 'road'.
2.3.13: The **सम्प्रदान** (the one the agent aims at through the action) takes the 4th case.
2.3.14: When a purpose-infinitive (the **तुमुन्**/**ण्वुल्** verb) is dropped from the sentence, its **कर्म** takes the 4th case (फलेभ्यो व्रजति = फलान्याहर्तुं व्रजति).
2.3.15: After an abstract-action noun (**भाववचन**) that carries the force of **तुम्** (the purpose-infinitive), use the 4th case (यागाय व्रजति = यष्टुं व्रजति).
2.3.16: In construction with नमः, स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलम्, or वषट्, use the 4th case (नमो देवेभ्यः, स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः, अलं मल्लो मल्लाय).
2.3.17: The non-living **कर्म** of the verb मन्य (Divādi, with **श्यन्**) optionally takes the 4th case when contempt is meant (न त्वा तृणं/तृणाय मन्ये).
2.3.18: The **कर्तृ** (the independent doer) and the **करण** (the most effective means) take the 3rd case (देवदत्तेन कृतम्, दात्रेण लुनाति).
2.3.19: With सह, the accompanying — not the principal — word takes the 3rd case (पुत्रेण सहागतः पिता).
2.3.20: The defective limb by which a person's defect is marked takes the 3rd case (अक्ष्णा काणः, पादेन खञ्जः).
2.3.21: The mark by which someone is recognized as being in a particular state takes the 3rd case (जटाभिस्तापसः, शिखया परिव्राजकम्).
2.3.22: The **कर्म** of the verb सम्-ज्ञा optionally takes the 3rd case (पित्रा/पितरं संजानीते).
2.3.23: A word denoting the cause takes the 3rd case (विद्यया यशः, धनेन कुलम्). Here हेतु is the ordinary 'cause', not the **हेतु** of 1.4.55.
2.3.24: A debt that is the cause but not the **कर्तृ** takes the 5th case (शताद् बद्धः).
2.3.25: A non-feminine quality-word that is the cause optionally takes the 5th case (जाड्याद्/जाड्येन बद्धः).
2.3.26: A cause-word takes the 6th case when the word हेतु is used alongside it (अन्नस्य हेतोर्वसति).
2.3.27: A **सर्वनाम** that is the cause, with the word हेतु alongside it, takes the 3rd case as well as the 6th (कस्य/केन हेतुना वसति).
2.3.28: The **अपादान** (the fixed point from which departure happens) takes the 5th case (ग्रामादागच्छति, वृकेभ्यो बिभेति).
2.3.29: In construction with अन्य ('other than'), आरात् ('far/near'), इतर, ऋते ('without'), a direction-word, a word ending in अञ्चु meaning direction, or a word ending in **आच्**/**आहि**, use the 5th case (अन्यो देवदत्तात्, ऋते देवदत्तात्, पूर्वो ग्रामात्).
2.3.30: In construction with a word ending in an affix that has the sense of **अतसुच्**, use the 6th case (दक्षिणतो ग्रामस्य, पुरस्ताद् ग्रामस्य).
2.3.31: With a word ending in **एनप्**, use the 2nd case as well as the 6th (दक्षिणेन ग्रामम्/ग्रामस्य).
2.3.32: With पृथक्, विना, or नाना, use the 3rd case optionally — and also the 5th and the 2nd (रामेण/रामाद्/रामं विना).
2.3.33: As **करण**, स्तोक, अल्प, कृच्छ्र, and कतिपय optionally take the 5th case when they name a quality, not a substance (स्तोकाद्/स्तोकेन मुक्तः) — but स्तोकेन विषेण हतः keeps the 3rd.
2.3.34: In construction with words meaning 'far' (दूर) or 'near' (अन्तिक), the 6th case is used optionally, alongside the 5th (दूरं ग्रामस्य/ग्रामात्).
2.3.35: After words meaning 'far' (दूर) or 'near' (अन्तिक), use the 2nd case as well — alongside the 5th and the 3rd (दूरं/दूराद्/दूरेण ग्रामस्य).
2.3.36: The **अधिकरण** (the locus of the action) takes the 7th case — and so do words meaning 'far' and 'near' (कटे आस्ते, स्थाल्यां पचति, दूरे/अन्तिके ग्रामस्य).
2.3.37: That whose action (**भाव**) marks the time of another action takes the 7th case — the locative absolute (गोषु दुह्यमानासु गतः).
2.3.38: When disregard is meant, that whose action marks the time of another action takes the 6th case as well as the 7th — the genitive absolute (रुदतः/रुदति प्राव्राजीत्).
2.3.39: In construction with स्वामिन्, ईश्वर, अधिपति, दायाद, साक्षिन्, प्रतिभू, or प्रसूत, use the 6th case and the 7th (गवां/गोषु स्वामी).
2.3.40: In construction with आयुक्त ('engaged') or कुशल ('skilled'), when deep absorption is meant, use the 6th case and the 7th (आयुक्तः/कुशलः कटकरणस्य/कटकरणे).
2.3.41: The **षष्ठी** (6th) and **सप्तमी** (7th) follow the word from which one item is singled out of a group by its kind, quality, or action (**निर्धारण**): गवां / गोषु कृष्णा.
2.3.42: The **पञ्चमी** (5th) follows the word from which one item is set apart as separate (not counted within the group): माथुराः पाटलिपुत्रेभ्यः सुकुमारतराः. This blocks the **षष्ठी** and **सप्तमी**.
2.3.43: With साधु or निपुण meaning good conduct toward someone (**अर्चा**, respect), that someone takes the **सप्तमी** (7th) — provided प्रति is not used: मातरि साधुः.
2.3.44: With प्रसित or उत्सुक (intent on), the object takes the **तृतीया** (3rd), and by च also the **सप्तमी** (7th): केशैः / केशेषु प्रसितः.
2.3.45: When a time-of-asterism affix drops by **लुप्**, the asterism word takes the **सप्तमी** (7th) and the **तृतीया** (3rd): पुष्येण / पुष्ये पायसमश्नीयात्.
2.3.46: Where the sense is the bare **प्रातिपदिक** meaning (existence) alone, or gender alone, or measure alone, or number alone, the **प्रथमा** (1st) is used: वृक्षः, कुमारी, द्रोणः, एकः.
2.3.47: And in addressing (**संबोधन**), the **प्रथमा** (1st) is used: हे राम.
2.3.48: A word ending in the **प्रथमा** in the sense of addressing is **आमन्त्रित**.
2.3.49: The singular of the **आमन्त्रित प्रथमा** is **संबुद्धि**.
2.3.50: In the remaining sense — a relation like owner-and-property, beyond the **कारक** roles and beyond the bare **प्रातिपदिक** meaning — the **षष्ठी** (6th) is used: राज्ञः पुरुषः.
2.3.51: With ज्ञा not meaning to know (instead, to engage in or to mistake), its instrument takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): सर्पिषो जानीते.
2.3.52: With verbs meaning to remember (**अधि-इ**), and with दय and ईश, the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): मातुरध्येति, सर्पिषो दयते, सर्पिष ईष्टे.
2.3.53: The object of कृ meaning to give a thing a new quality (**प्रतियत्न**) takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): एधोदकस्योपस्कुरुते.
2.3.54: With verbs meaning to afflict (sense of रुज्), excluding causative ज्वर, when the verb runs of its own (subject is the condition itself), the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): चौरस्य रुजति रोगः.
2.3.55: With नाथ् meaning to bless (**आशिस्**), the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): मधुनो नाथते.
2.3.56: With जासि, हन् preceded by नि or प्र, नाट्, क्राथ, and पिष् meaning to injure (**हिंसा**), the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): चौरस्योज्जासयति.
2.3.57: With व्यवहृ and पण् when synonymous (dealing in trade or staking at dice), the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): शतस्य व्यवहरति / पणते.
2.3.58: With दिव् in that same sense of dealing or staking, the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): शतस्य दीव्यति.
2.3.59: When दिव् in that sense carries an **उपसर्ग**, the object optionally takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): शतस्य / शतं प्रति दीव्यति.
2.3.60: With दिव् in that sense, in the **ब्राह्मण** texts the object takes the **द्वितीया** (2nd): गामस्य तदहः सभायां दीव्येयुः.
2.3.61: With प्रेष्य and ब्रूहि, the oblation (**हविस्**) they govern takes the **षष्ठी** (6th) when offering to a deity is meant: अग्नये छागस्य हविषो वपाया मेदसोऽनुब्रूहि / प्रेष्य.
2.3.62: In the **छन्दस्**, the **षष्ठी** (6th) is used freely (**बहुलम्**) for the sense of the **चतुर्थी** (4th): पुरुषमृगश्चन्द्रमसः / चन्द्रमसे.
2.3.63: And in the **छन्दस्**, the instrument of यज् takes the **षष्ठी** (6th) freely: घृतस्य / घृतेन यजते.
2.3.64: After a time word (**काल**) in the sense of location (**अधिकरण**), when a word meaning so-many-times (**कृत्वसुच्** sense) is present, the **षष्ठी** (6th) is used: पञ्चकृत्वोऽह्नो भुङ्क्ते.
2.3.65: For the agent (**कर्तृ**) and the object (**कर्मन्**), when a **कृत्**-formed word is present, the **षष्ठी** (6th) is used: भवतः शायिका, अपां स्रष्टा.
2.3.66: When a **कृत्** word brings both the agent and the object into the sentence, only the object takes the **षष्ठी** (6th), not the agent: आश्चर्यो गवां दोहोऽगोपालकेन.
2.3.67: A **क्त** participle used in present sense takes the **षष्ठी** (6th) for its agent: राज्ञां मतः, राज्ञां पूजितः.
2.3.68: A **क्त** participle expressing location (**अधिकरण**) takes the **षष्ठी** (6th): इदमेषामासितम्.
2.3.69: The **षष्ठी** (6th) for agent or object is blocked when the governing word ends in ल (a **लकार** substitute participle), उ, उक, an **अव्यय**, a **निष्ठा** (**क्त**/**क्तवतु**), a **खल्**-sense affix, or **तृन्**: ओदनं पचन्, कटं कृत्वा, ओदनं भुक्तवान्.
2.3.70: The **षष्ठी** (6th) is blocked when the governing word ends in अक denoting future action, or in इन् denoting future action or debt: कटं कारको व्रजति, शतं दायी.
2.3.71: Under a **कृत्य** (future passive participle), the agent optionally takes the 6th case; the object always takes the 6th.
2.3.72: With a word meaning "like" or "resembling" — but not तुला or उपमा — the other word optionally takes the 3rd case; otherwise the 6th.
2.3.73: In a blessing, आयुष्य, मद्र, भद्र, कुशल, सुख, अर्थ, हित take the 4th case for the one blessed; otherwise the 6th.
2.4.1: A **द्विगु** is singular: it names a single aggregate (पञ्चपूली, "the group of five bundles").
2.4.2: A समाहार **द्वन्द्व** of words for body parts, instrument-players, or army-divisions is also singular (पाणिपादम्).
2.4.3: A **द्वन्द्व** of चरण words (people named for the Vedic school they study) is singular when the sense is repeating a point already made.
2.4.4: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for यजुर्वेद sacrifices is singular, provided those words are never neuter.
2.4.5: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for people studying subjects that come close together in the order of study is singular (पदकक्रमकम्).
2.4.6: A **द्वन्द्व** of जाति (kind) words that are not names of living beings is singular (आराशस्त्रि).
2.4.7: A **द्वन्द्व** of differently-gendered names of rivers and countries — but not towns — is singular (गङ्गाशोणम्).
2.4.8: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for small creatures is singular (दंशमशकम्).
2.4.9: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for creatures with permanent natural enmity is singular (मार्जारमूषकम्) — and only singular, even for beasts and birds.
2.4.10: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for शूद्र groups not cast out of communion with the higher classes is singular (तक्षायस्कारम्).
2.4.11: गवाश्व and the rest of that list are also singular **द्वन्द्व** compounds.
2.4.12: A **द्वन्द्व** of words for trees, wild animals, grass, grain, condiments, domestic beasts, or birds, and the compounds अश्ववडव, पूर्वापर, अधरोत्तर, is optionally singular.
2.4.13: A **द्वन्द्व** of words of opposite meaning that do not name concrete substances is optionally singular (शीतोष्णम्).
2.4.14: दधिपयस् and the rest of that list are not singular as **द्वन्द्व** compounds.
2.4.15: A **द्वन्द्व** that fixes the count of concrete things is not singular (दश दन्तोष्ठाः).
2.4.16: A **द्वन्द्व** giving an approximate count of concrete things is optionally singular (उपदशं दन्तोष्ठम्).
2.4.17: A **द्विगु** or **द्वन्द्व** made singular by the rules above is neuter (दशगवम्, पाणिपादम्).
2.4.19: A **तत्पुरुष** — but not a नञ् compound and not a **कर्मधारय** — is neuter in the cases the following rules give.
2.4.20: As a name, a **तत्पुरुष** ending in कन्था is neuter, provided the town is in the उशीनर country (सौशमिकन्थम्).
2.4.21: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in उपज्ञा or उपक्रम is neuter when it states the starting point of something first invented or begun (पाणिन्युपज्ञम्).
2.4.22: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in छाया is neuter when it means a dense mass of the first thing (शलभच्छायम्, a sky-darkening swarm of locusts).
2.4.23: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in सभा is neuter when preceded by a synonym of राजा or by a word for a non-human being (इनसभम्, रक्षःसभम्).
2.4.24: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in सभा is neuter when it means a gathering rather than a hall (स्त्रीसभम्).
2.4.25: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in सेना, सुरा, छाया, शाला, or निशा is optionally neuter — excluding the नञ् compound and the **कर्मधारय**.
2.4.26: A **द्वन्द्व** or **तत्पुरुष** takes the gender of its last word.
2.4.27: The compound अश्ववडव takes the gender of its first word, अश्व.
2.4.28: In the **छन्दस्**, the compounds हेमन्तशिशिरौ and अहोरात्रे take the gender of their first member, not the gender of the last.
2.4.29: A **द्वन्द्व** or **तत्पुरुष** ending in रात्र or अह्न (or अह) is masculine.
2.4.31: अर्धर्च, गोमय, and the rest are both masculine and neuter.
2.4.32: Once इदम् has already named a thing and the same thing comes up again later in a sentence (**अन्वादेश**), इदम् becomes the unaccented अश् (i.e. अ) before the instrumental and the case-affixes after it.
2.4.33: In **अन्वादेश**, एतद् becomes the unaccented अश् before त्रल् (locative) and तसिल् (ablative), and those त्र and तस् are themselves unaccented.
2.4.34: In **अन्वादेश**, इदम् and एतद् become the unaccented एन् before the accusative, before टा (instrumental singular), and before ओस् (locative/genitive dual).
2.4.35: From here through 2.4.58, read in "when the **आर्धधातुक** affix is the subject" — the substitutions below apply only before **आर्धधातुक** affixes, not **सार्वधातुक** ones.
2.4.36: अद् becomes जग्धि before ल्यप् and before an **आर्धधातुक** **कित्** affix starting with त्.
2.4.37: अद् becomes घस् (घसॢ) before लुङ् and before सन्.
2.4.38: अद् becomes घस् (घसॢ) before घञ् and before अप् as well.
2.4.39: In the **छन्दस्**, अद् becomes घस् (घसॢ) variously — sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn't.
2.4.40: Before लिट्, अद् optionally becomes घस् (घसॢ).
2.4.41: Before लिट्, वेञ् 'weave' optionally becomes वय् (वयि).
2.4.42: हन् becomes वध् before the **आर्धधातुक** लिङ् (the Benedictive).
2.4.43: हन् becomes वध् before लुङ् as well.
2.4.44: Before **आत्मनेपद** affixes in लुङ्, हन् optionally becomes वध्.
2.4.45: इण् 'go' becomes गा before लुङ् — always, with no option, in every **पद**.
2.4.46: Before णि (the causative), इण् 'go' becomes गम् (गमि) when the sense is not 'informing'.
2.4.47: Before सन्, इण् 'go' becomes गम् (गमि) when the sense is not 'informing'.
2.4.48: इङ् 'study' becomes गम् (गमि) before सन् as well.
2.4.50: इङ् 'study' optionally becomes गाङ् before लुङ् and before लृङ्.
2.4.51: In the causative णि, इङ् 'study' optionally becomes गाङ् when that causative carries सन् or चङ्.
2.4.52: अस् 'be' becomes भू before an **आर्धधातुक** affix.
2.4.53: ब्रू 'speak' becomes वच् (वचि) before an **आर्धधातुक** affix.
2.4.54: चक्षिङ् 'see, tell' becomes ख्याञ् before an **आर्धधातुक** affix.
2.4.55: Before लिट्, चक्षिङ् optionally becomes ख्याञ्.
2.4.56: अज् 'drive' becomes वी before an **आर्धधातुक** affix, except before घञ् and अप्.
2.4.57: अज् 'drive' optionally becomes वी before ल्युट् (यु).
2.4.58: After a **गोत्र** word ending in **ण्य**, a **गोत्र** word naming a क्षत्रिय's or ऋषि's descendant, or a **गोत्र** word ending in a **ञित्** affix, the **युवन्** affixes **ञ्**, **अण्**, and **इञ्** drop by **लुक्**.
2.4.59: After पैल and the rest, the **युवन्** affix drops by **लुक्**.
2.4.60: After a word ending in the **गोत्र** affix **इञ्**, the **युवन्** affix drops by **लुक्** when the **गोत्र** named is that of the प्राच्य (Eastern) people.
2.4.61: After तौल्वलि and the rest, the **युवन्** affix does not drop by **लुक्**.
2.4.62: A **तद्राज** affix drops by **लुक्** in the plural, provided the base itself takes that plural and the base is not feminine.
2.4.63: After यस्क and the rest, the **गोत्र** affix drops by **लुक्** when the base itself takes the plural and is not feminine.
2.4.64: The **गोत्र** affixes **यञ्** and **अञ्** drop by **लुक्** when the base itself takes the plural and is not feminine.
2.4.65: After अत्रि, भृगु, कुत्स, वसिष्ठ, गोतम, अङ्गिरस्, the **गोत्र** affix drops by **लुक्** in the plural, but not in the feminine.
2.4.66: After a polysyllabic base, the **गोत्र** affix **इञ्** drops by **लुक्** in the plural when the **गोत्र** named is that of the प्राच्य or भरत people.
2.4.67: After गोपवन and the rest, the **गोत्र** affix does not drop by **लुक्** in the plural.
2.4.68: After तिक, कितव and the rest in a **द्वन्द्व**, the **गोत्र** affixes drop by **लुक्** when the compound takes the plural.
2.4.69: After उपक and the rest, the **गोत्र** affix optionally drops by **लुक्** in the plural, whether in a **द्वन्द्व** or standing alone.
2.4.70: For अगस्त्य and कौण्डिन्य in the plural, the **गोत्र** affixes **अण्** and **यञ्** drop by **लुक्**, and the remaining bases become अगस्ति and कुण्डिनच्.
2.4.71: A case-affix (**सुप्**) drops by **लुक्** within a **धातु** or a **प्रातिपदिक**.
2.4.72: After अद् and the rest, **शप्** drops by **लुक्**.
2.4.74: **यङ्** drops by **लुक्** variably (बहुलम्) before the affix **अच्**.
2.4.75: After हु and the rest, **शप्** drops by **श्लु** (the drop that triggers reduplication).
2.4.77: After गा, स्था, the **घु** verbs, पा, and भू, **सिच्** drops by **लुक्** before **परस्मैपद** endings.
2.4.78: After घ्रा, धेट्, शा, छा, सा, **सिच्** optionally drops by **लुक्** before **परस्मैपद** endings.
2.4.79: After तन् and the rest, **सिच्** optionally drops by **लुक्** before the **आत्मनेपद** endings त and थास्.
2.4.80: In a मन्त्र, the tense-marker **लि** drops by **लुक्** after घस्, ह्वृ, णश्, वृ, दह्, a verb ending in long आ, वृच्, कृ, गम्, and जन्.
2.4.83: After an **अव्ययीभाव** ending in अ, the case-affix does not drop by **लुक्**; instead it becomes **अम्**, except when it is the fifth (ablative).
2.4.84: After an **अव्ययीभाव** ending in अ, the third (instrumental) and seventh (locative) case-affixes become **अम्** variably (बहुलम्).
2.4.85: For the three third-person **लुट्** endings, **परस्मैपद** and **आत्मनेपद** alike, **डा**, **रौ**, **रस्** are the substitutes respectively.
3.1.1: From here on, what is introduced is a **प्रत्यय**.
3.1.2: And a **प्रत्यय** comes after the **धातु** or **प्रातिपदिक**.
3.1.3: A **प्रत्यय** takes the acute accent on its first syllable, unless a more specific rule places it elsewhere.
3.1.4: The **सुप्** case-endings and **पित्** affixes (those with indicatory प) are अनुदात्त. This blocks 3.1.3.
3.1.5: गुप्, तिज्, and कित् take **सन्** — गुप् in the sense of despising, तिज् of enduring, कित् of healing: जुगुप्सते, तितिक्षते, चिकित्सते.
3.1.6: मान्, बध्, दान्, and शान् take **सन्**, and the इ of the **अभ्यास** (reduplicate) becomes long ई: मीमांसते, बीभत्सते, दीदांसते, शीशांसते.
3.1.7: After a root naming the wished-for object, when the wisher is also its agent, **सन्** optionally marks wishing: कर्तुम् इच्छति becomes चिकीर्षति.
3.1.8: **क्यच्** optionally attaches to a **सुप्**-ending word naming the wished-for object, when that object is wished for oneself: पुत्रम् इच्छति becomes पुत्रीयति.
3.1.9: **काम्यच्** also attaches, in the same sense of wishing the object for oneself, to a **सुप्**-ending word: पुत्रकाम्यति.
3.1.10: **क्यच्** optionally attaches to a **सुप्**-ending word naming the standard of comparison, in the sense of treating something as that: पुत्रीयति छात्रम् — he treats the pupil as a son.
3.1.11: **क्यङ्** optionally attaches to a **सुप्**-ending word naming the standard the agent is compared to, in the sense of behaving like it, and a final स of the word drops: श्येनायते, अप्सरायते.
3.1.12: **क्यङ्** attaches to भृश् and the rest (not already carrying **च्वि**) in the sense of becoming what one was not, and a final consonant of the word drops: भृशायते, शीघ्रायते.
3.1.13: **क्यष्** attaches to लोहित and the rest, and to words ending in **डाच्**, in the sense of becoming what one was not: लोहितायति, पटपटायते.
3.1.14: **क्यङ्** attaches to कष्ट (in the dative) in the sense of exerting oneself in dishonesty: कष्टाय कर्मणे क्रामति becomes कष्टायते.
3.1.15: **क्यङ्** attaches to रोमन्थ as object of chewing and to तपस् as object of performing: रोमन्थायते (the cow ruminates).
3.1.16: **क्यङ्** attaches to बाष्प and ऊष्म as object, in the sense of emitting: बाष्पायते, ऊष्मायते.
3.1.17: **क्यङ्** attaches to शब्द, वैर, कलह, अभ्र, कण्व, and मेघ as object, in the sense of making: शब्दायते, वैरायते.
3.1.18: **क्यङ्** attaches to सुख and the rest in the sense of feeling, when the feeling belongs to the agent who feels it: सुखायते, दुःखायते.
3.1.19: **क्यच्** attaches to नमस्, वरिवस्, and चित्रङ् in the sense of making: नमस्यति, वरिवस्यति, चित्रीयते.
3.1.20: **णिङ्** attaches to पुच्छ, भाण्ड, and चीवर as object, in the sense of making: उत्पुच्छयते, सम्भाण्डयते, सञ्चीवरयते.
3.1.21: **णिच्** attaches to मुण्ड, मिश्र, श्लक्ष्ण, लवण, व्रत, वस्त्र, हल, कल, कृत, and तूस्त as object, in the sense of making: मुण्डयति, मिश्रयति, लवणयति.
3.1.22: **यङ्** attaches to a single-vowel root beginning with a consonant, in the sense of repeated or intense action: पापच्यते, जाज्वल्यते.
3.1.23: **यङ्** always attaches to a root of motion in the sense of crookedness: चङ्क्रम्यते, दन्द्रम्यते.
3.1.24: **यङ्** always attaches to लुप्, सद्, चर्, जप्, जभ्, दह्, दश्, and गॄ when the action is done contemptibly: लोलुप्यते, सासद्यते, चञ्चूर्यते.
3.1.25: **णिच्** attaches to सत्य (as सत्याप्), पाश, रूप, वीणा, तूल, श्लोक, सेना, लोम, त्वच्, वर्म, वर्ण, चूर्ण, and the चुरादि roots: सत्यापयति, उपवीणयति, चोरयति.
3.1.26: **णिच्** attaches to a root when a causer's action is expressed: कटं कारयति, ओदनं पाचयति.
3.1.27: **यक्** attaches to कण्डु and the rest: कण्डूयति, कण्डूयते.
3.1.28: **आय** attaches to गुप्, धूप्, विच्छ्, पण्, and पन्: गोपायति, धूपायति, विच्छायति, पणायति, पनायति.
3.1.29: **ईयङ्** attaches to the root ऋति (to reproach): ऋतीयते.
3.1.30: **णिङ्** attaches to the root कम् (to desire): कामयते.
3.1.31: **आय** and the affixes after it — **आय**, **ईयङ्**, **णिङ्** — attach optionally before an **आर्धधातुक** affix: गोपायिता or गोप्ता.
3.1.32: Anything ending in **सन्** or the affixes after it are **धातु**: चिकीर्षति, पुत्रीयति, पुत्रकाम्यति.
3.1.33: Before **लृ** (the **लृङ्** and **लृट्** tenses) and **लुट्**, a root takes **स्य** and **तासि** respectively. The इ of **तासि** is indicatory, blocking loss of a root nasal: मन् gives मन्ता.
3.1.34: Before **लेट्** (the Vedic subjunctive), a root takes **सिप्** variously.
3.1.35: Before **लिट्** outside a **मन्त्र**, कास् and any root ending in a **प्रत्यय** take **आम्**.
3.1.36: Before **लिट्**, a root beginning with an **इच्** vowel and carrying a heavy vowel takes **आम्**, except ऋच्छ्.
3.1.37: Before **लिट्**, दय, अय, and आस take **आम्**.
3.1.38: Before **लिट्**, उष्, विद्, and जागृ optionally take **आम्**.
3.1.39: Before **लिट्**, भी, ह्री, भृ, and हु optionally take **आम्**; with **आम्** they behave as if **श्लु** had applied (so they reduplicate) and belong to the ह्वादि class.
3.1.40: Before **लिट्**, कृ is added after the **आम्**-form. **कृञ्** here covers कृ, भू, and अस्; that use blocks the replacement of अस् by भू.
3.1.41: विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु is an optional irregular form: विद् takes **आम्** before **लोट्**, the **लोट्** ending drops by **लुक्**, no **गुण**, and कृ in **लोट्** follows. The इति extends this to every person and number.
3.1.42: In the **छन्दस्**, the forms अभ्युत्सादयांकः, प्रजनयांकः, चिकयांकः, रमयांकः, पावयांक्रियात्, and विदामक्रन् are irregular: **आम्** is added, with अकः, क्रियात्, or अक्रन् following as the auxiliary.
3.1.43: Before **लुङ्** (the aorist), a root takes **च्लि**. The इ is for pronunciation, the च for accent; **च्लि** is the common name for every aorist sign, replaced by the affixes that follow.
3.1.44: **सिच्** replaces **च्लि**. The इ is for pronunciation, the च for accent; the real affix is स्.
3.1.45: **क्स** replaces **च्लि** after a root that ends in a **शल्** consonant (श, ष, स, ह), has an **इक्** vowel (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ) as its penult, and takes no **इट्**.
3.1.46: **क्स** replaces **च्लि** after श्लिष् when it means 'embrace'. (A restriction: only in that sense.)
3.1.48: Before **लुङ्** signifying the agent, **चङ्** replaces **च्लि** after a root ending in **णि** and after श्रि, द्रु, स्रु. The ङ blocks **गुण** and **वृद्धि**, the च marks it off from **अङ्**; **चङ्** triggers reduplication.
3.1.49: After धे and श्वि, **चङ्** optionally replaces **च्लि** before agentive **लुङ्**.
3.1.50: After गुप्, **चङ्** optionally replaces **च्लि** in the **छन्दस्** (where गुप् does not take आय).
3.1.51: After the causatives ऊनयति, ध्वनयति, इलयति, and अर्दयति, **चङ्** does not replace **च्लि** in the **छन्दस्**.
3.1.52: Before **लुङ्** signifying the agent, **अङ्** replaces **च्लि** after अस्, वच्, and ख्या. अस् is repeated here to extend **अङ्** to the **आत्मनेपद** as well.
3.1.53: Before **लुङ्** signifying the agent, **अङ्** replaces **च्लि** after लिप्, सिच्, and ह्वे.
3.1.54: After लिप्, सिच्, and ह्वे, **अङ्** optionally replaces **च्लि** before **आत्मनेपद** endings.
3.1.55: Before **परस्मैपद** endings, **अङ्** replaces **च्लि** after the पुषादि roots, the द्युतादि roots, and roots with an indicatory ऌ.
3.1.56: **अङ्** replaces **च्लि** after सृ, शास्, and ऋ, in both **परस्मैपद** and **आत्मनेपद**. (Stated separately to reach the **आत्मनेपद**; the च carries 'in the **परस्मैपद**' forward.)
3.1.57: Before **परस्मैपद** endings, **अङ्** optionally replaces **च्लि** after a root with an indicatory इर्.
3.1.58: Before **परस्मैपद** endings, **अङ्** optionally replaces **च्लि** after जॄ, स्तम्भु, म्रुचु, म्लुचु, ग्रुचु, ग्लुचु, ग्लुञ्चु, and श्वि.
3.1.59: In the **छन्दस्**, **अङ्** replaces **च्लि** after कृ, मृ, दॄ, and रुह्.
3.1.60: After पद्, **चिण्** replaces **च्लि** before the affix त (the **आत्मनेपद** third-person singular).
3.1.61: Before त, **चिण्** optionally replaces **च्लि** after दीप्, जन्, बुध्, पूर्, ताय्, and प्याय्.
3.1.62: Before त, **चिण्** optionally replaces **च्लि** after a root ending in a vowel when the object itself is spoken of as the agent.
3.1.63: After दुह् in the reflexive sense, with the त ending following, **च्लि** optionally becomes **चिण्**.
3.1.64: After रुध् in the reflexive sense, **च्लि** does not become **चिण्**.
3.1.65: After तप् in the reflexive sense, and in the sense of remorse, **च्लि** does not become **चिण्**; in the remorse sense the block holds in the impersonal and passive too.
3.1.66: With the त ending (3rd singular **आत्मनेपद**) following in the impersonal (**भाव**) or passive (**कर्मन्**) sense, **च्लि** becomes **चिण्**.
3.1.67: A root takes **यक्** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the impersonal or passive sense. (The क् blocks **गुण** and **वृद्धि**.)
3.1.68: A root takes **शप्** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense.
3.1.69: A दिवादि root takes **श्यन्** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.70: After भ्राश्, भ्लाश्, भ्रम्, क्रम्, क्लम्, त्रस्, त्रुट्, लष्, **श्यन्** is optional in the agent sense.
3.1.71: After यस् without a preverb, **श्यन्** is optional in the agent sense.
3.1.72: After यस् preceded by सम्, **श्यन्** is optional in the agent sense.
3.1.73: A स्वादि root takes **श्नु** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.74: श्रु takes **श्नु** in the agent sense, and along with it श्रु becomes शृ.
3.1.75: After अक्ष्, **श्नु** is optional in the agent sense.
3.1.76: After तक्ष् in the sense of paring down, **श्नु** is optional in the agent sense.
3.1.77: A तुदादि root takes **श** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.78: A रुधादि root takes **श्नम्** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense; the म् places न after the root's last vowel. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.79: A तनादि root and कृ take **उ** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.80: धिन्व् and कृण्व् take **उ** in the agent sense, and their final इ becomes अ.
3.1.81: A क्र्यादि root takes **श्ना** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.82: स्तम्भ्, स्तुम्भ्, स्कम्भ्, स्कुम्भ् and स्कु take **श्ना** or **श्नु** before a **सार्वधातुक** ending in the agent sense.
3.1.83: After a root ending in a consonant, **श्ना** becomes **शानच्** before हि.
3.1.84: In the **छन्दस्**, after a root ending in a consonant, **श्ना** becomes **शायच्** as well as **शानच्** before हि.
3.1.85: In the **छन्दस्**, the **विकरण**-affixes (**शप्** and the rest) are swapped about freely.
3.1.86: In the **छन्दस्**, a root takes **अङ्** before the **आशीर्लिङ्** endings. (This blocks **शप्**.)
3.1.87: When the action falling on the agent matches the action that falls on an object, the agent-denoting **ल** counts as an object-denoting **ल** (so **यक्**, **आत्मनेपद**, **चिण्** and the rest follow).
3.1.88: The agent of तप् counts as the object only when the object is the word तपस् itself.
3.1.89: In the reflexive sense of दुह्, स्नु and नम्, the **यक्** and **चिण्** of the object-treatment do not apply.
3.1.90: In the reflexive sense, कुष् and रञ्ज् take **श्यन्** and the **परस्मैपद** endings, in the Easterners' view. (This blocks **यक्** and **आत्मनेपद**.)
3.1.91: From here to the end of the Third Chapter, the affixes come after a root.
3.1.92: In this section on roots, a word stated in the locative case is an **उपपद**.
3.1.93: In this section about verbal roots, every **प्रत्यय** except **तिङ्** (the tense/personal endings) is a **कृत्**.
3.1.94: In this section, an **अपवाद** **प्रत्यय** of a different form optionally blocks the general one it would override — except a **प्रत्यय** specified under the feminine heading **स्त्रियाम्**, which blocks without option.
3.1.95: From here through ण्वुल्तृचौ [[3.1.133]], every **प्रत्यय** specified is a **कृत्य**.
3.1.96: A root takes **तव्यत्**, **तव्य**, or **अनीयर्** (the त् and र् only mark accent).
3.1.97: A root ending in a vowel takes **यत्**.
3.1.98: A root ending in a labial (the प-वर्ग) preceded by short अ takes **यत्**.
3.1.100: गद्, मद्, चर्, and यम्, with no **उपसर्ग**, take **यत्**.
3.1.101: अवद्य, पण्य, and वर्या are formed irregularly with **यत्**, meaning respectively 'blameworthy', 'for sale', and 'unobstructable'.
3.1.102: वह्य is formed irregularly with **यत्** when it means an instrument of carrying.
3.1.103: अर्य is formed irregularly with **यत्** when it means 'lord' or 'वैश्य'.
3.1.104: उपसर्या is formed irregularly with **यत्** when it means a female that has reached the time fit for conception.
3.1.105: अजर्य 'undecaying' is formed irregularly with **यत्** when it qualifies सङ्गत 'friendship'.
3.1.106: वद् with a case-inflected **उपपद** and no **उपसर्ग** takes **क्यप्** — and, by च, **यत्** as well.
3.1.107: भू with a case-inflected **उपपद** and no **उपसर्ग** takes **क्यप्** to denote the **भाव** (state).
3.1.108: हन् with a case-inflected **उपपद** and no **उपसर्ग** takes **क्यप्** to denote the **भाव**, and त replaces its final न्.
3.1.109: इ, स्तु, शास्, वृ, and जुष् take **क्यप्**.
3.1.110: A root with penultimate short ऋ takes **क्यप्**, except कॢप् and चृत्.
3.1.111: खन् takes **क्यप्**, and long ई replaces its final.
3.1.112: भृञ् takes **क्यप्** when the word is not a name.
3.1.114: राजसूय, सूर्य, मृषोद्य, रुच्य, कुप्य, कृष्टपच्य, and अव्यथ्य are formed irregularly with **क्यप्**.
3.1.115: भिद्य and उद्ध्य are formed irregularly with **क्यप्** when they name a river (the झ् of उज्झ् also becomes ध).
3.1.116: पुष्य and सिद्ध्य are formed irregularly with **क्यप्** when they name an asterism.
3.1.117: विपूय, विनीय, and जित्य are formed irregularly with **क्यप्**, meaning respectively the मुञ्ज grass, the sediment, and the plough.
3.1.118: ग्रह् preceded by प्रति or अपि takes **क्यप्** in the **छन्दस्** (Vedic).
3.1.119: ग्रह् takes **क्यप्** when the word means a पद (word), a dependent, something outside, or a partisan.
3.1.121: युग्य is formed irregularly with **क्यप्** when it means a vehicle (the ज् of युज् becomes ग).
3.1.122: अमावस्य is formed irregularly: वस् after अमा takes **ण्यत्** for time-location, and optionally the **वृद्धि** is dropped.
