3.1.123: In the **छन्दस्** these words are irregular: निष्टर्क्य, देवहूय, प्रणीय, उन्नीय, उच्छिष्य, मर्य, स्तर्या, ध्वर्य, खन्य, खान्य, देवयज्या, आपृच्छ्य, प्रतिषीव्य, ब्रह्मवाद्य, भाव्य, स्ताव्य, उपचाय्य, पृड.
3.1.124: A root ending in ऋ (short or long) or in a consonant takes **ण्यत्**.
3.1.125: A root ending in उ (short or long) takes **ण्यत्** when the sense is necessity.
3.1.126: आसु, यु, वप्, रप्, लप्, त्रप्, चम् take **ण्यत्**.
3.1.127: आनाय्य is irregular when it means impermanent.
3.1.128: प्रणाय्य is irregular when it means disapproved.
3.1.129: पाय्य, सान्नाय्य, निकाय्य, धाय्या are irregular, meaning respectively a measure, an oblation, a dwelling, and a सामिधेनी verse.
3.1.130: कुण्डपाय्य and संचाय्य are irregular when they name a sacrifice.
3.1.131: परिचाय्य, उपचाय्य, समूह्य are irregular when they name a fire.
3.1.132: चित्य and अग्निचित्या are also irregular.
3.1.133: Every root takes **ण्वुल्** (अक्) and **तृच्** (तृ) for the agent.
3.1.134: The नन्द्यादि roots take **ल्यु** (अन), the ग्रह्यादि roots take **णिनि** (इन्), and the पचादि roots take **अच्** (अ), each for the agent.
3.1.135: A consonant-final root with इ, उ, or ऋ (short or long) as its penult, and the roots ज्ञा, प्री, कॄ, take **क** (अ).
3.1.136: A root ending in आ also takes **क** when an **उपसर्ग** precedes it.
3.1.137: पा, घ्रा, ध्मा, धेट्, दृश् take **श** (अ) when an **उपसर्ग** precedes them.
3.1.138: With no **उपसर्ग**, लिम्प्, विन्द्, धारि, पारि, वेदि, उदेजि, चेति, साति, साहि take **श**.
3.1.139: दा and धा optionally take **श** when no **उपसर्ग** precedes them.
3.1.140: The roots from ज्वल् through कस् optionally take **ण** when no **उपसर्ग** precedes them.
3.1.141: श्यै, the roots ending in आ, व्यध्, आस्रु, संस्रु, अतीण्, अवसा, अवहृ, लिह्, श्लिष्, श्वस् take **ण**.
3.1.142: दु and नी take **ण** when no **उपसर्ग** precedes them.
3.1.144: ग्रह् takes **क** when the agent it names is a house.
3.1.145: A root takes **ष्वुन्** (अक्) when the agent it names is a craftsman.
3.1.146: गै takes **थकन्** (थक) when the agent it names is a craftsman.
3.1.147: गै also takes **ण्युट्** when the agent it names is a craftsman.
3.1.148: हा also takes **ण्युट्** when the agent it names is rice or time.
3.1.149: प्रु, सृ, स्रु, लू take **वुन्** when repeated, well-done action is meant.
3.1.150: Every root takes **वुन्** when a benediction is meant.
3.2.1: A root takes **अण्** when its object stands with it as **उपपद**.
3.2.2: हूञ्, वेञ्, माङ् take **अण्** when their object stands with them as **उपपद**.
3.2.3: A root ending in long आ, with no **उपसर्ग** before it, takes **क** when its object stands in composition (गोदः). This blocks **अण्**.
3.2.4: स्था takes **क** when a case-inflected word stands before it as **उपपद** — the **उपपद** need not be the object (समस्थः).
3.2.5: परिमृज् with तुन्द before it, and अपनुद् with शोक before it, each take **क** as object — meaning lazy and joy-giving respectively (तुन्दपरिमृजः, शोकापनुदः).
3.2.6: दा and ज्ञा with प्र before them take **क** when the object stands in composition (सर्वप्रदः, पथिप्रज्ञः). This blocks **अण्**.
3.2.7: ख्या with सम् before it takes **क** when the object stands in composition (गोसंख्यः). This blocks **अण्**.
3.2.8: गै and पा, with no **उपसर्ग**, take **टक्** when the object stands in composition (शक्रगः, सामगः); the ट् gives the feminine in **ङीप्** (शक्रगी).
3.2.9: हृञ्, when it does not mean raising a load, takes **अच्** with its object in composition (अंशहरः, रिक्थहरः). This blocks **अण्**.
3.2.10: हृञ् takes **अच्** with its object in composition when the word marks the reaching of an age fit for the act (अस्थिहरः श्वा, कवचहरः क्षत्रियकुमारः).
3.2.11: हृञ् with आङ् before it takes **अच्**, object in composition, when the word names a natural bent or habit (पुष्पाहरः, फलाहरः).
3.2.12: अर्ह् takes **अच्** with its object in composition (पूजार्हा, मालार्हा), the form being feminine. This blocks **अण्**.
3.2.13: रम् with case-inflected स्तम्ब before it, and जप् with कर्ण before it, take **अच्** — meaning elephant and tale-bearer (स्तम्बेरमः, कर्णेजपः).
3.2.14: Any root takes **अच्** with शम् before it when the word is a name (शंकरः, शंभवः). The repeated धातु blocks the **ट** that कृ would otherwise take, so the feminine is शंकरा, not शंकरी.
3.2.15: शी takes **अच्** when a case-inflected word naming the place of lying stands in composition (खशयः, गर्तशयः).
3.2.16: चर् takes **ट** when a case-inflected word naming the place stands in composition (कुरुचरः, मद्रचरः); the ट् gives the feminine in **ङीप्** (कुरुचरी).
3.2.17: चर् takes **ट** when भिक्षा, सेना, or आदाय stands before it (भिक्षाचरः, सेनाचरः, आदायचरः).
3.2.18: सृ takes **ट** when पुरः, अग्रतः, or अग्रे stands before it (पुरःसरः, अग्रतःसरः, अग्रेसरः).
3.2.19: सृ takes **ट** when पूर्व, naming the agent, stands before it (पूर्वसरः). Otherwise **अण्** applies (पूर्वसारः).
3.2.20: कृञ् takes **ट** with its object in composition when the word marks cause, habit, or going-with-the-grain (शोककरी, श्राद्धकरः, प्रैषकरः).
3.2.21: कृञ् takes **ट** when दिवा, विभा, निशा, प्रभा, भाः, कार, अन्त, अनन्त, आदि, बहु, नान्दी, किम्, लिपि, लिबि, बलि, भक्ति, कर्तृ, चित्र, क्षेत्र, a number-word, जङ्घा, बाहु, अहः, यत्, तत्, धनुस्, or अरुस् stands before it (दिवाकरः, भास्करः, किंकरः).
3.2.22: कृञ् takes **ट** when the word कर्म stands before it and the form means wages — a hired laborer (कर्मकरः). Otherwise **अण्** applies (कर्मकारः).
3.2.23: कृञ् does not take **ट** when शब्द, श्लोक, कलह, गाथा, वैर, चाटु, सूत्र, मन्त्र, or पद stands before it; **अण्** takes its place (शब्दकारः, श्लोककारः, पदकारः).
3.2.24: कृ takes **इन्** when स्तम्ब or शकृत् stands before it as object, the forms meaning rice and a calf (स्तम्बकरिः, शकृत्करिः). Otherwise **अण्** applies (स्तम्बकारः).
3.2.25: हृ takes **इन्** when दृति or नाथ stands before it as object and the agent is an animal (दृतिहरिः, नाथहरिः). Otherwise **अण्** applies (दृतिहारः).
3.2.26: फलेग्रहि and आत्मम्भरि are irregular: फल takes final ए with **इन्** on ग्रह (फलेग्रहिः), and आत्म takes the augment मुम् with **इन्** on भृञ् (आत्मम्भरिः). Others fall here too — कुक्षिम्भरिः, उदरम्भरिः.
3.2.27: In the **छन्दस्**, वन्, सन्, रक्ष्, and अथ् take **इन्** with the object in composition (ब्रह्मवनिः, गोसनिः, पथिरक्षी, हविर्मथी).
3.2.28: The causative of एजृ takes **खश्** with its object in composition (अङ्गमेजयः, जनमेजयः); the ख् adds मुम् to the **उपपद**, the श् makes it **सार्वधातुक** so a **विकरण** comes in.
3.2.29: ध्मा and धे take **खश्** when नासिका or स्तन stands before them as object (स्तनन्धयः, नासिकन्धमः, नासिकन्धयः) — pairing is free, not term-for-term.
3.2.30: ध्मा and धे take **खश्** when नाडी or मुष्टि stands before them as object (नाडिन्धमः, मुष्टिन्धयः) — pairing is free; घटिन्धमः, वातन्धमः and the like fall here too.
3.2.31: रुज् and वह्, with उत् before them, take **खश्** when कूल stands before them as object (कूलमुद्रुजः, कूलमुद्वहः).
3.2.32: लिह् takes **खश्** when वह or अभ्र stands before it as object (वहंलिहो गौः, अभ्रंलिहो वायुः).
3.2.33: **खश्** comes after पच् when the object compounded with it is a measure (प्रस्थ, द्रोण, खारि): प्रस्थम्पचा, द्रोणम्पचः.
3.2.34: **खश्** comes after पच् when मित (a measured bit) or नख is the object compounded with it, in senses other than a measure: मितम्पचा, नखम्पचा.
3.2.35: **खश्** comes after तुद् when विधु (moon) or अरुस् (a wound) is the object compounded with it: विधुन्तुदः, अरुन्तुदः.
3.2.36: **खश्** comes after दृश् and तप् when असूर्य and ललाट respectively are the objects compounded with them: असूर्यम्पश्या, ललाटन्तपः. (असूर्य is an irregular compound—the अ negates दृश्, not सूर्य.)
3.2.37: उग्रम्पश्य, इरम्मद, पाणिन्धम are irregularly formed: उग्रम्पश्यः (fierce-looking), इरम्मदः, पाणिन्धमाः पन्थानः.
3.2.38: **खच्** comes after वद् when प्रिय or वश is the object compounded with it: प्रियंवदः, वशंवदः.
3.2.39: **खच्** comes after तप् (causative) when द्विषत् or पर is the object compounded with it: द्विषन्तपः, परन्तपः. With these objects in the feminine, **अण्** is used instead (द्विषतीतापः).
3.2.40: **खच्** comes after यम् when वाक् is the object compounded with it and a vow is meant: वाचंयमः. Without the vow sense the form is वाग्यामः.
3.2.41: **खच्** comes after दारि (to split) and सह् (to bear) when पुर् and सर्व respectively are the objects compounded with them: पुरन्दरः, सर्वंसहः. So also दारि with भग: भगन्दरः.
3.2.42: **खच्** comes after कष् when सर्व, कूल, अभ्र, or करीष is the object compounded with it: सर्वंकषः, कूलंकषा, अभ्रंकषः, करीषंकषा.
3.2.43: **खच्** comes after कृ when मेघ, ऋति, or भय is the object compounded with it: मेघंकरः, ऋतिंकरः, भयंकरः. Here तदन्तविधि applies, so अभयंकरः too.
3.2.44: **अण्** as well as **खच्** comes after कृ when क्षेम, प्रिय, or भद्र is the object compounded with it: क्षेमकारः or क्षेमंकरः, प्रियकारः or प्रियंकरः, भद्रकारः or भद्रंकरः. (The fresh mention of **अण्** blocks the **ट** feminine, so their feminine takes आ.)
3.2.45: **खच्** comes after भू when the case-inflected word आशित (satisfied by eating) is compounded with it in the sense of instrument or condition: आशितंभवः (food, by which one is satisfied; or satiety).
3.2.46: **खच्** comes after भृ, तॄ, वृ, जि, धारि, सहि, तपि, दम् when an object compounded with it makes a name: विश्वम्भरा, रथन्तरम्, पतिंवरा, शत्रुञ्जयः, युगन्धरः, शत्रुंसहः, शत्रुन्तपः, अरिन्दमः. Without the name sense: कुटुम्बभारः.
3.2.47: **खच्** comes after गम् when a case-inflected word compounded with it makes a name: सुतंगमः.
3.2.48: **ड** comes after गम् when अन्त, अत्यन्त, अध्वन्, दूर, पार, सर्व, or अनन्त is the object compounded with it: अन्तगः, अत्यन्तगः, अध्वगः, दूरगः, पारगः, सर्वगः, अनन्तगः. (The ड् drops the टि portion of गम्.)
3.2.49: **ड** comes after हन् when an object is compounded with it and a benediction is meant: तिमिहः (may he kill the whale), शत्रुहः. Without the benediction sense: शत्रुघातः.
3.2.50: **ड** comes after हन् preceded by अप when क्लेश or तमस् is the object compounded with it (and no benediction is meant): क्लेशापहः, तमोपहः.
3.2.51: **णिनि** comes after हन् when कुमार or शीर्ष is the object compounded with it: कुमारघाती, शीर्षघाती. (शीर्ष is an irregular form of शिरस्.)
3.2.52: **टक्** comes after हन् when जाया or पति is the object compounded with it and the agent bears that mark: जायाघ्नः, पतिघ्नी.
3.2.53: **टक्** comes after हन् when the object is compounded with it and the agent is non-human: जायाघ्नस्तिलकालकः, पतिघ्नी पाणिरेखा, श्लेष्मघ्नं मधु, पित्तघ्नं घृतम्. With a human agent, **अण्** is used instead: आखुघातः.
3.2.54: **टक्** comes after हन् when हस्ति or कपाट is the object compounded with it and capability is meant: हस्तिघ्नः (a man strong enough to kill an elephant), कपाटघ्नः. Without the capability sense, **अण्**: हस्तिघातः.
3.2.55: पाणिघ and ताडघ are irregularly formed when they name an artisan: पाणिघः (a drummer), ताडघः (a smith). Otherwise: पाणिघातः, ताडघातः. So also राजघः.
3.2.56: **ख्युन्** comes after कृ in the sense of instrument when आढ्य, सुभग, स्थूल, पलित, नग्न, अन्ध, or प्रिय is the object compounded with it, carrying the **च्वि** sense (becoming what it was not) but not actually ending in **च्वि**: आढ्यंकरणम्, सुभगंकरणम्, स्थूलंकरणम्.
3.2.57: **खिष्णुच्** and **खुकञ्** come after भू denoting the agent when आढ्य, सुभग etc. is the object compounded with it, carrying the **च्वि** sense but not ending in **च्वि**: आढ्यम्भविष्णुः, आढ्यम्भावुकः.
3.2.58: **क्विन्** comes after स्पृश् when a case-inflected word other than उदक is compounded with it: घृतस्पृक्, मन्त्रस्पृक्. Not with उदक: उदकस्पर्शः.
3.2.59: ऋत्विक्, दधृक्, स्रक्, दिक्, उष्णिक् are irregularly formed with **क्विन्**; and **क्विन्** also comes after अञ्चु, युजि, क्रुञ्च्: प्राङ्, युङ्, क्रुङ्.
3.2.60: **कञ्** (and also **क्विन्**) comes after दृश् when a त्यद्-series pronoun is compounded with it and perception is not meant: त्यादृशः or त्यादृक्, तादृशः or तादृक्, यादृशः or यादृक्. In the perception sense: तद्दर्शः.
3.2.61: **क्विप्** comes after सद्, सू, द्विष्, द्रुह्, दुह्, युज्, विद्, भिद्, छिद्, जि, नी, राज् when a case-inflected word—an उपसर्ग included—is compounded with it: शुचिषत्, अण्डसूः, मित्रद्विट्, मित्रध्रुक्, गोधुक्, अश्वयुक्, वेदवित्, काष्ठभित्. (Mentioning the उपसर्ग here shows that elsewhere a case-inflected word does not include an उपसर्ग.)
3.2.62: **ण्वि** comes after भज् when a case-inflected word—an उपसर्ग included—is compounded with it: अर्धभाक्, प्रभाक्.
3.2.63: In the **छन्दस्**, after सह् the affix **ण्वि** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands in composition before it.
3.2.64: And in the **छन्दस्**, after वह् the affix **ण्वि** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands in composition before it.
3.2.65: After वह् the affix **ञ्युट्** attaches in the **छन्दस्** when कव्य, पुरीष, or पुरीष्य stands before it.
3.2.66: After वह् the affix **ञ्युट्** attaches in the **छन्दस्** when हव्य stands before it, provided the word does not fall inside a पाद.
3.2.67: After जन्, सन्, खन्, क्रम्, गम् the affix **विट्** attaches in the **छन्दस्** when a word ending in a case-affix stands before it; the whole affix drops, and the final nasal becomes long आ।
3.2.68: After अद् the affix **विट्** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix other than अन्न stands before it.
3.2.69: And after अद् the affix **विट्** attaches when क्रव्य stands before it.
3.2.70: After दुह् the affix **कप्** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands before it, and घ् replaces the final.
3.2.71: In the **मन्त्र** literature श्वेतवह, उक्थश, and पुरोडाश् take the affix **ण्विन्**.
3.2.72: In the **मन्त्र** literature, after यज् the affix **ण्विन्** attaches when अव stands before it.
3.2.73: In the **छन्दस्**, after यज् the affix **विच्** attaches only when उप stands before it.
3.2.74: In the **छन्दस्**, after a verb ending in long आ the affixes **मनिन्**, **क्वनिप्**, **वनिप्**, and **विच्** attach when a word ending in a case-affix or an **उपसर्ग** stands before it.
3.2.75: **मनिन्**, **क्वनिप्**, **वनिप्**, and **विच्** are seen after other verbs too, not only those ending in long आ, and even with no **उपपद** before them.
3.2.76: And **क्विप्** is seen after any verb, with or without an **उपपद**, in both the **छन्दस्** and the spoken language.
3.2.77: After स्था the affixes **क** and **क्विप्** attach when a word ending in a case-affix or an **उपसर्ग** stands before it.
3.2.78: When habit is meant, after a verb the affix **णिनि** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix that does not name a genus stands before it.
3.2.79: After a verb the affix **णिनि** attaches, with agent force, when a word naming the standard of comparison stands before it — the agent acting like that standard.
3.2.80: When a vow is meant, after a verb the affix **णिनि** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands before it, the whole word naming the vow.
3.2.81: When repeated, assiduous action is meant, after a verb the affix **णिनि** attaches variously.
3.2.82: After मन् the affix **णिनि** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands before it.
3.2.83: When the thought is about oneself, after मन् the affix **खश्** attaches when a word ending in a case-affix stands before it — and also **णिनि** — the agent thinking himself such.
3.2.84: From here on, the affixes carry the sense of past time.
3.2.85: With past sense, after यज् the affix **णिनि** attaches when an instrumental word stands before it.
3.2.86: With past sense, after हन् the affix **णिनि** attaches when an accusative word stands before it.
3.2.87: With past sense, after हन् the affix **क्विप्** attaches only when ब्रह्म, भ्रूण, or वृत्र stands as the accusative word before it.
3.2.88: In the **छन्दस्**, with past sense, **क्विप्** attaches after हन् variously, even when the accusative word before it is not ब्रह्म, भ्रूण, or वृत्र।
3.2.89: With past sense, after कृ the affix **क्विप्** attaches when सु, कर्म, पाप, मन्त्र, or पुण्य stands as the accusative word before it.
3.2.90: With past sense, after सु the affix **क्विप्** attaches when सोम stands as the accusative word before it.
3.2.91: With past sense, after चि the affix **क्विप्** attaches when अग्नि stands as the accusative word before it.
3.2.92: With past sense, with object force, after चि the affix **क्विप्** attaches when an accusative word stands before it, provided the whole word names a fire.
3.2.93: With an object-word in the accusative as **उपपद**, the **प्रत्यय** इनि follows विकृ 'sell' for past sense — and the repeated कर्मणि restricts it to objects that censure the agent (सोमविक्रयी, रसविक्रयी, but not धान्यविक्राय).
3.2.94: With an object-word in the accusative as **उपपद**, दृश् 'see' takes the **प्रत्यय** क्वनिप् for past sense (मेरुदृश्वा); the restatement blocks any other affix here.
3.2.95: With राजन् as the accusative **उपपद**, युध् 'fight' and कृ 'make' take the **प्रत्यय** क्वनिप् for past sense (राजयुध्वा, राजकृत्वा).
3.2.96: With सह as **उपपद**, युध् and कृ take the **प्रत्यय** क्वनिप् for past sense (सहयुध्वा, सहकृत्वा); सह, naming no substance, takes no case.
3.2.97: With a locative **उपपद**, जन् 'be born' takes the **प्रत्यय** ड for past sense (उपसरज, मन्दुरज).
3.2.98: With an ablative **उपपद** that does not name a genus, जन् 'be born' takes the **प्रत्यय** ड for past sense (बुद्धिज, संस्कारज, दुःखज), but not हस्तिनो जातः, अश्वाज्जातः.
3.2.99: With an **उपसर्ग** as **उपपद**, जन् 'be born' takes the **प्रत्यय** ड for past sense when the whole names something (a **संज्ञा**), as प्रजाः.
3.2.100: With अनु prefixed and an accusative **उपपद**, जन् 'be born' takes the **प्रत्यय** ड for past sense (पुमनुज, स्त्र्यनुज).
3.2.101: जन् 'be born' is also seen taking the **प्रत्यय** ड for past sense with other **उपपद**s and other cases than the preceding rules name — अज, द्विज, ब्राह्मणज, अभिजाः, even after other roots (परिखा).
3.2.102: The **निष्ठा** affixes (क्त, क्तवतु) follow a root for past sense (कृत, कृतवान्, भुक्त, भुक्तवान्); by a **वार्त्तिक** they also mark the start of an action (प्रकृतः कटं देवदत्तः).
3.2.103: सु 'press out juice' and यज् 'sacrifice' take the **प्रत्यय** ङ्वनिप् for past sense (सुत्वा, यज्वा).
3.2.104: जृ 'grow old' takes the **प्रत्यय** अतृन् for past sense (जरन्, जरन्तौ, जरन्तः); by वासरूप the **निष्ठा** also follows (जीर्ण, जीर्णवान्).
3.2.105: In the **छन्दस्**, a root takes the **प्रत्यय** लिट् (perfect) for past sense (ददर्श, आततान).
3.2.106: In the **छन्दस्**, कानच् optionally replaces लिट् (चिक्यानः, सुषुवाणः); replacing every लिट्, not only the Vedic one, it forms verbal adjectives as well as the perfect, and only after **आत्मनेपद** roots.
3.2.107: In the **छन्दस्**, क्वसु optionally replaces लिट् (जक्षिवान्, पपिवान्).
3.2.108: In the spoken language, क्वसु optionally replaces लिट् for past sense after सद्, वस्, श्रु (उपसेदिवान्, अनूषिवान्, उपशुश्रुवान्).
3.2.109: उपेयिवान्, अनाश्वान्, अनूचान are fixed irregular forms — उप+इ and the negated अश् with क्वसु, and negated अनु+वच् with कानच्.
3.2.110: A root takes the **प्रत्यय** लुङ् (aorist) for past sense (अकार्षीत्, अहार्षीत्).
3.2.111: A root takes the **प्रत्यय** लङ् (imperfect) for past sense that does not fall within the current day (अकरोत्, अहरत्); the **बहुव्रीहि** अनद्यतन keeps it out when the day is in doubt (अद्य ह्यो वा अभुञ्ज्महि).
3.2.112: With a word for recollection (**अभिज्ञा**) connected to it, a root takes लृट् (second future) for past sense before the current day, blocking लङ् (अभिजानासि देवदत्त कश्मीरेषु वत्स्यामः); वचन extends this to अभिज्ञा's synonyms.
3.2.113: लृट् does not apply when the recollection **उपपद** carries यत् with it (अभिजानासि देवदत्त यत् कश्मीरेष्ववसाम).
3.2.114: लृट् applies optionally for past sense, with or without यत्, when the speaker's two clauses depend on each other (साकाङ्क्ष) — one verb pointing to the other (अभिजानासि देवदत्त कश्मीरेषु वत्स्यामस्तत्रौदनं भोक्ष्यामहे).
3.2.115: A root takes लिट् (perfect) for past sense that is before the current day and unwitnessed (**परोक्ष**) by the speaker (चकार, जहार).
3.2.116: With ह or शश्वत् connected to it, a root takes लङ् for past sense before the current day and unwitnessed; च also keeps लिट् (इति हाकरोत् / इति ह चकार, शश्वदकरोत् / शश्वच्चकार).
3.2.117: In a question about a recent past (आसन्नकाल), a root takes लङ् or लिट् for past sense before the current day and unwitnessed (अगच्छत् / जगाम देवदत्तः).
3.2.118: With स्म connected to it, a root takes लट् (present) for past sense before the current day and unwitnessed, blocking लिट् (यजति स्म युधिष्ठिरः).
3.2.119: With स्म connected to it, a root also takes लट् for past sense before the current day when the action was witnessed (एवं स्म पिता ब्रवीति, इति स्मोपाध्यायः कथयति).
3.2.120: With ननु connected to it, a root takes लट् for past sense in an answer to a question, blocking लुङ् (अकार्षीः कटं देवदत्त? — ननु करोमि भोः).
3.2.121: With न or नु connected to it, a root optionally takes लट् for past sense in an answer to a question (अकार्षीः कटं देवदत्त? — न करोमि / नाकार्षम्; अहं नु करोमि / अहं न्वकार्षम्).
3.2.122: With पुरा in the sentence and स्म absent, a root optionally takes लुङ् or लट् for past sense not in the current day (वसन्तीह पुरा छात्राः); otherwise the regular tense stands.
3.2.123: A verb naming an action that is underway takes **लट्** (the present).
3.2.124: **शतृ** and **शानच्** replace **लट्** when the participle agrees with a word that does not end in the first (nominative) case-ending.
3.2.125: **शतृ** and **शानच्** also replace **लट्** when the agreeing word is in the vocative, even though it ends in the first (nominative) case-ending.
3.2.126: **शतृ** and **शानच्** replace **लट्** when the action is the mark of, or the cause of, another action.
3.2.128: **शानन्** comes after पू (to purify) and यज् (to sacrifice).
3.2.129: **चानश्** comes after a verb to express habit, stage of life, or capacity.
3.2.130: **शतृ** comes after इङ् (to go) and धारि (to hold) when the agent does it with ease.
3.2.131: **शतृ** comes after द्विष् when the agent meant is an enemy.
3.2.132: **शतृ** comes after सु (to press out juice) when the sense is connection with a sacrifice.
3.2.133: **शतृ** comes after अर्ह to express praise.
3.2.134: From here through **क्विप्** (3.4.177, inclusive), the affixes taught come after a verb to name an agent who has that habit, that duty, or skill in that action.
3.2.135: **तृन्** comes after any verb to name such an agent.
3.2.136: **इष्णुच्** comes after अलंकृ, ञिराकृ, प्रजन्, उत्पच्, उत्पत्, उन्मद्, रुच्, अपत्रप्, वृत्, वृध्, सह, and चर् to name such an agent.
3.2.137: In the Vedas, **इष्णुच्** comes after a verb ending in the causative णि to name such an agent.
3.2.138: In the Vedas, **इष्णुच्** also comes after भू (to be) to name such an agent.
3.2.139: **क्स्नु** comes after ग्ला (to tire), जि (to conquer), स्था (to stand), and भू (to be) to name such an agent.
3.2.140: **क्नु** comes after त्रस् (to tremble), गृध् (to be greedy), धृष् (to be bold), and क्षिप् (to throw) to name such an agent.
3.2.141: **घिनुण्** comes after the eight verbs from शम् (to be calm) onward to name such an agent.
3.2.142: **घिनुण्** comes after संपृच्, अनुरुध्, आङ्यम्, आङ्यस्, परिसृ, संसृज्, परिदेवि, संज्वर्, परिक्षिप्, परिरट्, परिवद्, परिदह्, परिमुह्, दुष्, द्विष्, द्रुह्, दुह्, युज्, आक्रीड्, विविच्, त्यज्, रज्, भज्, अतिचर्, अपचर्, आमुष्, and अभ्याहन् to name such an agent.
3.2.143: **घिनुण्** comes after कष् (to injure), लस् (to sport), कत्थ (to praise), and स्रम्भ (to trust) when वि is the upapada.
3.2.144: **घिनुण्** comes after लष (to wish) when अप, or वि, is the upapada.
3.2.145: **घिनुण्** comes after लप्, सृ, द्रु, मथ, वद्, and वस् when प्र is the upapada.
3.2.146: **वुञ्** comes after निन्द्, हिंस्, क्लिश्, खाद्, विनाश्, परिक्षिप्, परिरट्, परिवद्, व्याभाष्, and असूय to name such an agent.
3.2.147: **वुञ्** comes after देवि (to lament) and क्रुश (to cry out) when an **उपसर्ग** is the upapada.
3.2.148: **युच्** comes after an intransitive verb meaning to move or to sound, to name such an agent.
3.2.149: **युच्** also comes after an intransitive verb that is आत्मनेपदी, begins with a consonant, and is अनुदात्तेत् (has a gravely-accented indicatory vowel).
3.2.150: **युच्** comes after जु, चङ्क्रम्य, दन्द्रम्य, सृ, गृध, ज्वल, शुच, लष, पत, and पद to name such an agent.
3.2.151: **युच्** also comes after verbs meaning क्रुध् (to be angry) and मण्ड (to adorn).
3.2.152: **युच्** does not come after a verb ending in य्.
3.2.153: After सूद्, दीप्, and दीक्ष्, **युच्** does not attach (these would otherwise take it by being **अनुदात्तेत्**).
3.2.154: After लष्, पत्, पद्, स्था, भू, वृष्, हन्, कम्, गम्, and शॄ, **उकञ्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.155: After जल्प्, भिक्ष्, कुट्ट्, लुण्ट्, and वृङ्, **षाकन्** attaches for the habitual agent (the ष marks **ङीष्** in the feminine).
3.2.156: After प्रजु, **इनि** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.157: After जि, दृ, क्षि, विश्रि, इ, वम्, अव्यथ, अभ्यम, परिभू, and प्रसू, **इनि** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.158: After स्पृह्, गृह्, पत्, दय्, निद्रा, तन्द्रा, and श्रद्धा, **आलुच्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.159: After दा, धेट्, सि, शद्, and सद्, **रु** attaches.
3.2.160: After सृ, घस्, and अद्, **क्मरच्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.161: After भञ्ज्, भास्, and मिद्, **घुरच्** attaches for the habitual agent (the घ triggers the guttural change, as in भङ्गुर).
3.2.162: After विद् (to know), भिद्, and छिद्, **कुरच्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.163: After इ, नश्, जि, and सृ, **क्वरप्** attaches for the habitual agent (the प marks the **तुक्** augment, as in इत्वर).
3.2.164: गत्वर is formed irregularly: drop the नासिक्य of गम् and add **क्वरप्**.
3.2.165: After जागृ, **ऊक** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.166: After यज्, जप्, and दश् when they end in **यङ्**, **ऊक** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.167: After नम्, कम्प्, स्मि, अजस्, कम्, हिंस्, and दीप्, **र** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.168: After a root ending in **सन्**, and after आशंस् and भिक्ष्, **उ** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.169: विन्दु and इच्छु are formed irregularly with **उ** for the habitual agent (विद् takes the नुम् augment; इष् changes ष to छ).
3.2.170: In the **छन्दस्**, after a root ending in **क्य** (क्यच्, क्यङ्, क्यप्), **उ** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.171: In the **छन्दस्**, after a root ending in आ or in ऋ/ॠ, and after गम्, हन्, and जन्, **कि** and **किन्** attach for the habitual agent, and they count as **लिट्** (so the root reduplicates).
3.2.172: After स्वप् and तृष्, **नजिङ्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.173: After शॄ and वन्द्, **आरु** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.174: After भी, **क्रु** and **क्लुकन्** attach for the habitual agent.
3.2.175: After स्था, ईश्, भास्, पिस्, and कस्, **वरच्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.176: After या ending in **यङ्**, **वरच्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.177: After भ्राज्, भास्, धुर्व्, द्युत्, ऊर्ज्, पॄ, जु, and स्तु preceded by ग्रावन्, **क्विप्** attaches for the habitual agent.
3.2.178: After roots other than these too, **क्विप्** is seen for the habitual agent.
3.2.179: After भू, **क्विप्** attaches when the word names something or means a surety.
3.2.180: After भू preceded by वि, प्र, or सम्, **डु** attaches, provided the word is not a name.
3.2.181: After धा (to suckle), **ष्ट्रन्** attaches in the sense of the object (the ष marks **ङीप्** in the feminine, as in धात्री).
3.2.182: After दाप्, नी, शस्, यु, युज्, स्तु, तुद्, सि, सिच्, मिह्, पत्, दश्, and नह्, **ष्ट्रन्** attaches in the sense of the instrument.
3.2.183: After पू (purify), **ष्ट्रन्** marks the instrument when the word names a part of a plough or a hog (पोत्रम्, the plough-share or the snout).
3.2.184: After ऋ, लू, धू, सू, खन्, सह्, चर्, **इत्र** marks the instrument.
3.2.185: After पू (purify), **इत्र** marks the instrument when the whole word is a name (पवित्रम्).
3.2.186: After पू (purify), **इत्र** marks the instrument when the word goes with a sage, and the agent when it goes with a deity.
3.2.187: After a root marked with **ञि**, **क्त** carries present meaning.
3.2.188: After roots meaning wish, knowledge, or honor, **क्त** also carries present meaning; च brings in further such roots.
3.3.1: The **उणादि** affixes (उण् and the rest) attach diversely, with present meaning and naming sense.
3.3.2: The **उणादि** affixes are also seen with past meaning.
3.3.3: गामि and the rest are valid forms with future meaning.
3.3.4: With the particle यावत् or पुरा, **लट्** carries future meaning.
3.3.5: With the adverb कदा or कर्हि, **लट्** optionally carries future meaning.
3.3.6: With किम् (or its डतर/डतम derivatives) in the sentence, **लट्** optionally carries future meaning when the speaker wants to gain something.
3.3.7: **लट्** also optionally carries future meaning when the sentence shows the gain another secures by meeting the speaker's wish.
3.3.8: **लट्** optionally carries future meaning after the root whose action is the condition for another action stated in the imperative.
3.3.9: Under those same conditions, when the future moment lies beyond a मुहूर्त (48 minutes), **लिङ्** optionally carries future meaning, and by च so does **लट्**.
3.3.10: **तुमुन्** and **ण्वुल्** carry future meaning when the verb they go with names an action done for the sake of this future action.
3.3.11: The action-naming affixes (घञ् and the rest) also carry future meaning when the verb they go with names an action done for the sake of this future action.
3.3.12: **अण्** carries future meaning when the word with it is in the accusative and the action is done for the sake of another action.
3.3.13: In the remaining cases of plain future, and also with a verb naming an action done for the sake of the future action, **लृट्** is the affix.
3.3.15: For a future that is not within the current day, **लुट्** is the affix (blocking **लृट्**).
3.3.16: After पद् (pace), रुज् (pain), विश् (enter), स्पृश् (touch), **घञ्** is the affix.
3.3.17: After सृ (move), **घञ्** is the affix when the agent stays permanently fixed.
3.3.18: After a root, **घञ्** marks the bare action (**भाव**).
3.3.19: After a root, **घञ्** marks a name tied to some कारक other than the agent.
3.3.20: After any root, **घञ्** is the affix when the word names a measure.
3.3.22: After रु (roar) with an **उपसर्ग**, **घञ्** is the affix.
3.3.23: After यु (join), द्रु (run), दु (burn) with सम्, **घञ्** is the affix.
3.3.24: After श्रि (resort to), नी (lead), भू (be) with no **उपसर्ग**, **घञ्** is the affix.
3.3.25: **घञ्** comes after क्षु (sneeze) and श्रु (hear) when वि precedes — blocking **अप्**.
3.3.26: **घञ्** comes after नी (lead) when अव or उद् precedes.
3.3.27: **घञ्** comes after द्रु (run), स्तु (praise), and स्रु (flow) when प्र precedes.
3.3.28: **घञ्** comes after पू (purify) when निर् precedes, and after लू (cut) when अभि precedes.
3.3.29: **घञ्** comes after गॄ (sound, swallow) when उद् or नि precedes.
3.3.30: **घञ्** comes after कॄ (scatter) when उद् or नि precedes and the sense is about grain.
3.3.31: **घञ्** comes after स्तु (praise) when सम् precedes and the sense is about sacrifice.
3.3.32: **घञ्** comes after स्तॄ (spread) when प्र precedes, as long as the sense is not about sacrifice.
3.3.33: **घञ्** comes after स्तॄ (spread) when वि precedes and the sense is extent — but not extent of words.
3.3.34: **घञ्** comes after स्तॄ (spread) with वि when the word is the name of a metre.
3.3.35: **घञ्** comes after ग्रह् (seize) when उद् precedes — blocking **अप्**.
3.3.36: **घञ्** comes after ग्रह् (seize) when सम् precedes and the sense is about the fist.
3.3.37: **घञ्** comes after नी (lead) when परि precedes and the sense is a game, and after इ (go) when नि precedes and the sense is propriety — blocking **अच्**.
3.3.38: **घञ्** comes after इ (go) when परि precedes and the sense is following in regular succession.
3.3.39: **घञ्** comes after शी (lie down) when वि or उप precedes and the sense is regular succession.
3.3.40: **घञ्** comes after चि (gather) when the sense is taking by hand, as long as it is not stealing.
3.3.41: **घञ्** comes after चि (gather), and क replaces its initial च, in the senses dwelling, funeral pile, body, and heap.
3.3.42: **घञ्** comes after चि (gather), and क replaces its initial च, in the sense of an assembly of living beings — but not a mere disorderly crowd.
3.3.43: **णच्** comes after a root when the sense is reciprocal action and the word is feminine.
3.3.44: **इनुण्** comes after a root in the **भाव** sense when the meaning is full co-extensiveness.
3.3.45: **घञ्** comes after ग्रह् (seize) when अव or नि precedes and the sense is cursing.
3.3.46: **घञ्** comes after ग्रह् (seize) when प्र precedes and the sense is the wish to acquire.
3.3.47: **घञ्** comes after ग्रह् (seize) when परि precedes and the sense is about sacrifice.
3.3.48: **घञ्** comes after वृ when नि precedes and the sense is grain — blocking **अप्**.
3.3.49: **घञ्** comes after श्रि (resort), यु (join), पू (purify), and द्रु (run) when उद् precedes — blocking **अच्**.
3.3.50: **घञ्** optionally comes after रु (roar) and प्लु (float) when आङ् precedes.
3.3.51: **घञ्** optionally comes after ग्रह् (seize) when अव precedes and the sense is withholding of rain.
3.3.52: **घञ्** optionally comes after ग्रह् (seize) when प्र precedes and the word names the cord of a balance.
3.3.53: **घञ्** optionally comes after ग्रह् (seize) when प्र precedes and the word means a rein.
3.3.54: **घञ्** optionally comes after वृ (choose) when प्र precedes and the word means a covering.
3.3.55: After भू with परि, when the sense is disregard, **घञ्** comes optionally (परिभावः, परिभवः).
3.3.56: After a root ending in इ or ई, in the sense of **भाव** or of a non-agent **कारक** as a **संज्ञा**, **अच्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.57: After a root ending in ॠ, उ, or ऊ, **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.58: After ग्रह्, वृ, दृ, निश्चि, and गम्, **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्** (and blocking **अच्** for निश्चि).
3.3.60: After अद् with नि, **ण** comes, and also **अप्**.
3.3.61: After व्यध् and जप् without an **उपसर्ग**, **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.62: After स्वन् and हस् without an **उपसर्ग**, **अप्** comes optionally (स्वनः/स्वानः, हसः/हासः).
3.3.63: After यम् with सम्, उप, नि, or वि—and even without an **उपसर्ग**—**अप्** comes optionally, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.64: After गद्, नद्, पठ्, and स्वन् with नि, **अप्** comes optionally, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.65: After क्वण् with नि, or without an **उपसर्ग**, or when a flute is meant, **अप्** comes optionally, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.66: After पण्, when the sense is a measure, **अप्** comes—always, not optionally (मूलकपणः).
3.3.67: After मद् without an **उपसर्ग**, **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.68: प्रमद and सम्मद are the forms fixed when the sense is joy.
3.3.69: After अज् with सम् or उत्, when the word refers to beasts, **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.70: ग्लह is the form fixed (from ग्रह्, with र→ल) when the sense refers to dicing.
3.3.71: After सृ, in the sense of impregnating (a cow's first covering), **अप्** comes, blocking **घञ्**.
3.3.72: After ह्वे with नि, अभि, उप, or वि, **अप्** comes and the root takes **सम्प्रसारण**, blocking **घञ्** (निहवः, अभिहवः, उपहवः, विहवः).
3.3.73: After ह्वे with आङ्, when the sense is battle, **अप्** comes and the root takes **सम्प्रसारण** (आहवः).
3.3.74: आहाव is the form fixed—ह्वे with आङ्, **सम्प्रसारण**, **अप्**, and **वृद्धि**—when the sense is a watering-trough.
3.3.75: After ह्वे without an **उपसर्ग**, in the sense of **भाव**, **अप्** comes and the root takes **सम्प्रसारण** (हवः).
3.3.76: After हन् without an **उपसर्ग**, in the sense of **भाव**, **अप्** comes, and वध replaces हन् before it (वधः).
3.3.77: After हन्, when the sense is solidity, **अप्** comes, and घन replaces हन् (अभ्रघनः, दधिघनः).
3.3.78: After हन् with अन्तर्, when the sense is a country, **अप्** comes, and घन replaces हन् (अन्तर्घनः).
3.3.79: प्रघण and प्रघाण are the forms fixed (from हन् with प्र) when the sense is a portion of a dwelling.
3.3.80: उद्घन is the form fixed (from हन् with उत्) when the sense is a carpenter's bench.
3.3.81: अपघन is the form fixed (from हन् with अप) when the sense is a limb of the body.
3.3.82: After हन् with अयस्, वि, or द्रु, as the instrument **कारक**, **अप्** comes, and घन replaces हन् (अयोघनः, विघनः, द्रुघनः).
3.3.83: After हन् with स्तम्ब, as the instrument **कारक**, **क** comes—and also **अप्** (with घन replacing हन्): स्तम्बघ्नः, स्तम्बघनः.
3.3.84: After हन् with परि, as the instrument **कारक**, **अप्** comes, and घ replaces हन् (परिघः).
3.3.85: उपघ्न, meaning a slope to lean on, is the irregular form of उप + हन् with **अप्**: the penultimate अ of ह drops and हन् becomes घ्न. It holds only when the sense is proximity (आश्रय).
3.3.86: संघ 'collection' and उद्घ 'praise' are the irregular forms of सम्/उद् + हन् with **अप्**: the final न drops and ह becomes घ. संघ is for a collection, उद्घ for praise, respectively.
3.3.87: निघ, meaning as high as it is broad, is the irregular form of नि + हन् with **अप्**: the final न drops and ह becomes घ. It holds only in that sense.
3.3.88: A root marked with डु takes **क्त्रि** for the action. By [[4.4.20]] क्त्रि never stands alone, so म is always added: पक्त्रिम, उप्त्रिम, कृत्रिम.
3.3.89: A root marked with टु takes **अथुच्** for the action: वेपथु, श्वयथु, क्षवथु.
3.3.90: यज्, याच्, यत्, विच्छ्, प्रच्छ्, रक्ष् take **नङ्** for the action: यज्ञ, याच्ञा, यत्न, विश्न, प्रश्न, रक्ष्ण. The ङ् blocks **गुण** and **वृद्धि**.
3.3.91: स्वप् takes **नन्** for the action: स्वप्न. The final न् fixes the accent.
3.3.92: A **घु** root (दा, धा by [[1.1.20]]) with an **उपसर्ग** before it takes **कि** for the action: प्रदि, प्रधि, अन्तर्धि. The क् drops the final आ.
3.3.93: A **घु** root with an accusative word before it takes **कि** when the formed word names the location: जलधि 'ocean', शरधि 'quiver'.
3.3.94: For a feminine word naming the action, a root takes **क्तिन्**: कृति, चिति, मति. This blocks **घञ्**, **अच्**, and **अप्**.
3.3.95: स्था, गा, पा, पच् take **क्तिन्** for a feminine word naming the action: प्रस्थिति, उद्गीति, प्रपीति, पक्ति. This blocks **अङ्**.
3.3.96: In मन्त्र texts, वृष्, इष्, पच्, मन्, विद्, भू, वि, रा take acutely accented **क्तिन्** for a feminine word naming the action: वृष्टि, इष्टि, पक्ति, मति, वित्ति, भूति, वीति, राति.
3.3.97: ऊति, यूति, जूति, साति, हेति, कीर्ति are irregular forms with the acute accent on the last syllable.
3.3.98: व्रज् and यज् take acutely accented **क्यप्** for a feminine word naming the action: व्रज्या, इज्या. This blocks **क्तिन्**.
3.3.99: समज्, निषद्, निपत्, मन्, विद्, षु, शी, भृ, इ take acutely accented **क्यप्** for a feminine word that is an appellative: समज्या, निषद्या, निपत्या, मन्या, विद्या, सुत्या, शय्या, भृत्या, इत्या.
3.3.100: कृ takes **श** for a feminine word, and also **क्यप्** (and, by splitting the rule, **क्तिन्**): क्रिया, कृत्या, कृति.
3.3.101: इच्छा is the irregular form of इष् + **श**: the यक् of [[3.1.67]] is not added.
3.3.102: A root ending in an affix (desiderative, causative, intensive, denominative) takes **अ** for a feminine word: चिकीर्षा, जिहीर्षा, पुत्रीया, लोलूया.
3.3.103: A root with a prosodially heavy vowel that ends in a consonant takes **अ** for a feminine word: कुण्डा, हुण्डा, ईहा, ऊहा. This blocks **क्तिन्**.
3.3.104: Roots marked with षि, and the भिद्-group roots, take **अङ्** for a feminine word: जरा, त्रपा, भिदा, छिदा, धारा.
3.3.105: चिन्त्, पूज्, कथ्, कुम्ब्, चर्च् take **अङ्**, and also **युच्**, for a feminine word: चिन्ता, पूजा, कथा, कुम्बा, चर्चा (or चिन्तना with युच्).
3.3.106: A root ending in long आ, with an **उपसर्ग** before it, takes **अङ्** for a feminine word: प्रदा, प्रधा, उपदा, उपधा. This blocks **क्तिन्**.
3.3.107: A root ending in णि, and आस् and श्रन्थ्, take **युच्** for a feminine word: कारणा, हारणा, आसना, श्रन्थना. This blocks **अ**.
3.3.108: For a feminine word that names a disease, a root variously takes **ण्वुल्**: प्रच्छर्दिका, प्रवाहिका, विचर्चिका. This blocks **क्तिन्** and the rest.
3.3.109: For a feminine word that is an appellative, a root takes **ण्वुल्**: उद्दालकपुष्पभञ्जिका, शालभञ्जिका, तालभञ्जिका.
3.3.110: In a question and its answer, a root optionally takes **इञ्**, and also **ण्वुल्** (and whatever other affixes would otherwise apply): कारि, कारिका, क्रिया, कृति.
3.3.111: In the sense of turn-in-succession, merit, debt, or production, a root takes **ण्वुच्**: शायिका, इक्षुभक्षिका, ओदनभोजिका, पयःपायिका. This blocks **क्तिन्** and the rest. ण्वुच् and **ण्वुल्** give the same form, differing only in accent.
3.3.112: In the sense of cursing, a root with नञ् before it takes **अनि**: अकरणिस्ते भूयात्. This blocks **क्तिन्** and the rest.
3.3.113: The **कृत्य** affixes [[3.1.95]] and **ल्युट्** apply variously, in senses beyond those already taught: स्नानीयं चूर्णम्, दानीयो ब्राह्मणः, अपसेचनम्, प्रस्कन्दनम्.
3.3.114: A root takes **क्त** for a neuter word naming the action: हसितम्, जल्पितम्, शायितम्, गतम्.
3.3.115: **ल्युट्** also attaches to a root for the name of the action, in the neuter.
3.3.116: **ल्युट्** attaches to a root in the neuter for the name of the action when the object in construction with it names the thing whose contact gives the agent bodily pleasure (पयःपानं सुखम्).
3.3.117: **ल्युट्** attaches to a root when the word names the **करण** (instrument) or **अधिकरण** (locus) of the action.
3.3.118: **घ** generally attaches to a root for the **करण** or **अधिकरण**, in the masculine, when the whole word is a **संज्ञा**. (प्रायेण: not without exception.)
3.3.119: गोचर, संचर, वह, व्रज, व्यज, आपण, निगम are irregular forms with **घ** in that same sense; च covers others like कष, निकष.
3.3.120: After तॄ and स्तॄ with the **उपसर्ग** अव, **घञ्** attaches for the **करण** or **अधिकरण** **संज्ञा**, blocking **घ** (अवतारः, अवस्तारः).
3.3.121: After a root ending in a consonant, **घञ्** attaches (masculine **संज्ञा**, **करण** or **अधिकरण**), blocking **घ** (लेखः, वेदः, मार्गः).
3.3.122: अध्याय, न्याय, उद्याव, संहार, आधार, आवाय are irregular forms with **घञ्** instead of **घ**; च covers others like अवहार.
3.3.123: उदङ्क is an irregular **घञ्** form, but only when the sense does not concern water (तैलोदङ्कः, not for water).
3.3.124: आनाय is an irregular **घञ्** form when it means a net (आनायो मत्स्यानाम्).
3.3.125: After खन्, both **घ** and **घञ्** attach for the **करण** or **अधिकरण** **संज्ञा** (आखनः, आखानः).
3.3.126: With ईषद्, दुर्, सु as **उपपद**, meaning hard or easy, **खल्** attaches to a root (दुष्करः, सुकरः).
3.3.127: After भू and कृ, **खल्** attaches when the **उपपद** is, respectively, the agent and the object, preceded by ईषद् and the rest meaning hard or easy (ईषदाढ्यंभवम्, स्वाढ्यंकरः).
3.3.128: After a root ending in long आ, **युच्** attaches instead of **खल्** (with ईषद्, दुर्, सु, meaning hard or easy: सुपानः, दुष्पानः).
3.3.129: In the **छन्दस्**, after roots meaning to go, **युच्** attaches instead of **खल्** (सूपसदनोऽग्निः).
3.3.130: In the **छन्दस्**, **युच्** is also seen after roots other than those meaning to go (सुदोहनाम्, सुवेदनाम्); in the spoken language it follows शास्, युध्, दृश्, धृष्, मृष् (दुःशासनः, दुर्योधनः).
3.3.131: The present-tense affixes optionally count for past or future near the present (वर्तमानवत्: as if present).
3.3.132: When hope is expressed, the past-tense affixes too, and by च the present-tense ones, optionally count for the future (भूतवत्: as if past).
3.3.133: When a word for quickly is in construction and hope is expressed, **लृट्** attaches (blocking the as-if-past option: उपाध्यायश्चेत् क्षिप्रमागमिष्यति).
3.3.134: When a word expressing hope is the **उपपद**, **लिङ्** attaches for the future (आशंसे युक्तोऽधीयीय).
3.3.135: For continuous action or nearness in time, the non-current-day past and future affixes **लङ्** and **लुट्** do not count (नानद्यतनवत्); the **लुङ्** and First Future are used instead (यावज्जीवं भृशमन्नमदात्).
3.3.136: For the future, when a limit is stated and the statement concerns this (अवर) side of it, the non-current-day affix **लुट्** does not count; the First Future is used instead.
3.3.137: In stating a limit of time (not of day or night), on this (अवर) side, **लुट्** likewise does not count; च continues the prohibition for time-divisions, barring those of day and night.
3.3.138: On the far (पर) side of such a time-limit, the prohibition holds optionally.
3.3.139: Where a cause for **लिङ्** is present, **लृङ्** attaches for the future when the action fails to come off (क्रियातिपत्ति: the action does not happen).
3.3.140: And **लृङ्** attaches likewise for the past, where a cause for **लिङ्** is present and the action fails to come off.
3.3.141: From here up to उताप्योः [[3.3.152]], that **लृङ्** for the past (cause for **लिङ्** present, action failing to come off) holds optionally (वा).
3.3.142: When censure (**गर्हा**) is implied and अपि or जातु is in construction, **लट्** attaches regardless of the actual time (अपि तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयति).
3.3.143: With कथम् in construction and censure implied, **लिङ्**, and by च **लट्**, attach optionally, alongside the tense the time would otherwise call for.
3.3.144: With an interrogative किम्-word in construction and censure implied, **लिङ्** and **लृट्** attach, blocking all other tense-affixes (कः हरिं निन्देत्, निन्दिष्यति वा).
3.3.145: When you express that someone finds an action unbelievable (**अनवक्लृप्ति**) or intolerable (**अमर्ष**), the root takes **लिङ्** or **लृट्** — even without an interrogative word.
3.3.146: With किंकिल, or a word meaning अस्ति (अस्ति, भवति, विद्यते), the root takes **लृट्** when the sense is **अनवक्लृप्ति** or **अमर्ष**, blocking **लिङ्**.
3.3.147: With जातु or यत्, the root takes **लिङ्** when the sense is **अनवक्लृप्ति** or **अमर्ष**, blocking **लृट्**.
3.3.148: With यच्च or यत्र, the root takes **लिङ्** when the sense is **अनवक्लृप्ति** or **अमर्ष**, blocking **लृट्**.
3.3.149: With यच्च or यत्र, the root takes **लिङ्** when censure (**गर्हा**) is meant.
3.3.150: With यच्च or यत्र, the root takes **लिङ्** when wonder (**चित्रीकरण**) is meant.
3.3.151: When wonder is meant but the word is something other than यच्च or यत्र, the root takes **लृट्** — except when यदि is used.
3.3.152: With उत or अपि, both meaning बाढम् 'surely', the root takes **लिङ्**.
3.3.153: When the agent makes a wish known (**कामप्रवेदन**), the root takes **लिङ्** — except when कच्चित् is used.
3.3.154: When a genuine expectation of someone's competence (**सम्भावन**) is meant — the kind अलम् would mark, and अलम् is rightly left unsaid — the root takes **लिङ्**.
3.3.155: When a verb expressing such expectation (**सम्भावनवचन**) is in construction, the root optionally takes **लिङ्** — except when यत् is used.
3.3.156: When the meaning is a condition (**हेतु**) and its consequence (**हेतुमत्**), the root takes **लिङ्** in both.
3.3.157: When a verb meaning 'wish' (इच्छ्, कम्, प्रार्थ्) is in construction, the root takes **लिङ्** or **लोट्**.
3.3.158: When a verb meaning 'wish' is in construction and both verbs share one agent, the root takes **तुमुन्**.
3.3.159: When a verb meaning 'wish' is in construction and both verbs share one agent, the root also takes **लिङ्**.
3.3.160: Roots meaning 'wish' optionally take **लिङ्** in the present, where **लट्** would otherwise stand.
3.3.161: In commanding (**विधि**), inviting (**निमन्त्रण**), permitting (**आमन्त्रण**), a courteous request (**अधीष्ट**), questioning (**सम्प्रश्न**), or praying (**प्रार्थना**), the root takes **लिङ्**.
3.3.162: In those same senses — commanding, inviting, and the rest — the root also takes **लोट्**.
3.3.163: In directing (**प्रैष**), granting permission (**अतिसर्ग**), and the arrival of the proper time (**प्राप्तकाल**), the root takes the **कृत्य** affixes, and also **लोट्**.
3.3.164: When the action lies a **मुहूर्त** ahead, the root takes **लिङ्** in those senses (directing, permitting, and the rest) — and, by च, the **कृत्य** affixes and **लोट्** as before.
3.3.165: With स्म, in those senses and a **मुहूर्त** ahead, the root takes **लोट्**, blocking **लिङ्** and the **कृत्य** affixes.
3.3.166: With स्म, when a courteous request (**अधीष्ट**) is meant, the root takes **लोट्**, blocking **लिङ्**.
3.3.167: With काल, समय, or वेला — all meaning 'time' — the root takes **तुमुन्**.
3.3.168: With यद्, alongside काल, समय, or वेला, the root takes **लिङ्**, blocking **तुमुन्**.
3.3.169: When fitness in the agent (**अर्ह**) is meant, the root takes the **कृत्य** affixes and **तृच्** — and, by च, **लिङ्**.
3.3.170: When necessity (**आवश्यक**) or indebtedness (**आधमर्ण्य**) marks the agent, the root takes **णिनि**.
3.3.171: When necessity or indebtedness is meant, the root also takes the **कृत्य** affixes.
3.3.172: When capability (**शक्ति**) is meant, the root takes **लिङ्** — and, by च, the **कृत्य** affixes.
3.3.173: When a blessing (**आशीस्**) is meant, the root takes **लिङ्** or **लोट्**.
3.3.174: When a blessing is meant and the whole word is a name (**संज्ञा**), the root takes **क्तिच्** or **क्त**.
3.3.175: After a verb, when मा (माङ्) stands with it, add **लुङ्**. This blocks every other tense affix.
3.3.176: After a verb, when मा is followed by स्म, add **लङ्** — and by च also **लुङ्**.
3.4.1: When two verbal senses are linked as qualifier and qualified, the affixes hold even when they mark a time other than the one they were specified for. (So a word fixed as past by its affix can stand with a future verb.)
3.4.2: To mark an action done repeatedly or intensely, add **लोट्** to the root and double the verb; **लोट्** is then replaced by हि and स्व, and optionally by त and ध्वम्.
3.4.3: When several actions are heaped together, **लोट्** is added to the root optionally, with the same replacements हि/स्व, and optionally त/ध्वम्.
3.4.4: In the first case ([[3.4.2]]), the verb that follows must be the very root that took **लोट्** — no synonym.
3.4.5: In the second case ([[3.4.3]]), the verb that follows must be one whose sense is common to all the heaped actions.
3.4.6: In the **छन्दस्**, **लुङ्**, **लङ्**, and **लिट्** are used optionally for any time.
3.4.7: In the **छन्दस्**, **लेट्** is used optionally wherever **लिङ्** applies.
3.4.8: In the **छन्दस्**, **लेट्** is used after a root when a reciprocal agreement (उपसंवाद) or an apprehension (आशङ्का) is meant — and here necessarily, not optionally.
3.4.9: In the **छन्दस्**, with the force of **तुमुन्**, a root takes any of: से, सेन्, असे, असेन्, क्से, क्सेन्, अध्यै, अध्यैन्, कध्यै, कध्यैन्, शध्यै, शध्यैन्, तवै, तवेङ्, तवेन्.
3.4.10: प्रयै, रोहिष्यै, अव्यथिष्यै are irregularly fixed infinitives in the **छन्दस्**.
3.4.11: दृशे and विख्ये are irregularly fixed infinitives in the **छन्दस्**.
3.4.12: In the **छन्दस्**, when शक् 'be able' governs the root, add **णमुल्** or **कमुल्** with the force of **तुमुन्**.
3.4.13: In the **छन्दस्**, when ईश्वर is in composition, add **तोसुन्** or **कसुन्** with the force of **तुमुन्**.
3.4.14: In the **छन्दस्**, with the force of the **कृत्य** affixes (action and object), add तवै, केन्, केन्य, or त्वन्.
3.4.15: अवचक्षे is an irregularly fixed **कृत्य**-sense form in the **छन्दस्**.
3.4.16: In the **छन्दस्**, when the bare name of the action is meant, **तोसुन्** comes after स्था, इण्, कृञ्, वद्, चर्, हु, तम्, जन् with the force of **तुमुन्**.
3.4.17: In the **छन्दस्**, when the bare name of the action is meant, **कसुन्** comes after सृप् and तृद् with the force of **तुमुन्**.
3.4.18: By the Eastern teachers, **क्त्वा** comes after a verb when अलम् or खलु stands with it expressing prohibition.
3.4.19: By the Northern teachers, **क्त्वा** comes after मेङ् 'exchange' when interchange is meant — even though its action is not prior to the other.
3.4.20: **क्त्वा** comes after a verb to place a thing on the far side (पर) or the near side (अवर) of another.
3.4.21: When two actions share one agent, **क्त्वा** comes after the verb whose action is earlier in time.
3.4.22: To express repetition, **णमुल्** comes after a root, and by च also **क्त्वा** — the verb being doubled. (Same agent, earlier action, carried from [[3.4.21]].)
3.4.23: **णमुल्** and **क्त्वा** are not added when यद् stands in a self-contained clause that needs no other clause to complete its sense.
3.4.24: When अग्रे, प्रथम, or पूर्व is in composition, **णमुल्** and **क्त्वा** come optionally after the earlier-action verb of two sharing one agent.
3.4.25: When an accusative word stands with कृ 'make' and abuse is meant, add **खमुञ्** to कृ.
3.4.26: When a word meaning 'sweet' is in composition with कृ 'make', add **णमुल्** to कृ. (Same agent, earlier action, carried from [[3.4.21]].)
3.4.27: When अन्यथा, एवम्, कथम्, or इत्थम् is compounded with कृ 'make', add **णमुल्** to कृ — provided कृ could be dropped without harming the sense.
3.4.28: When यथा or तथा is compounded with कृ 'make' in an angry reply, add **णमुल्** to कृ — provided कृ could be dropped without harming the sense.
3.4.29: दृश् (to see) and विद् (to know) take **णमुल्** when an **उपपद** object is compounded with them and the whole denotes the total of those objects: कन्यादर्शं वरयति, every girl seen.
3.4.30: विद् (to get) and जीव् (to live) take **णमुल्** when यावत् is the **उपपद**: यावद्वेदं भुङ्क्ते, यावज्जीवमधीते.
3.4.31: पूर् (to fill) takes **णमुल्** when चर्मन् or उदर् is the object **उपपद**: चर्मपूरं स्तृणाति, उदरपूरं भुङ्क्ते.
3.4.32: पूर् (to fill) takes **णमुल्** when the whole word measures a rainfall, and the ऊ of this पूर् optionally drops: गोष्पदपूरं or गोष्पदप्रं वृष्टो देवः. अस्य restricts the drop to पूर्'s ऊ, not the **उपपद**'s.
3.4.33: क्नोपि (the causative of क्नूय्, to wet) takes **णमुल्** when a word for clothing is the object **उपपद** and the whole measures a rainfall: चेलक्नोपं वृष्टो देवः, वस्त्रक्नोपम्.
3.4.34: कष् (to scrape) takes **णमुल्** when निमूल or समूल is the object **उपपद**: निमूलकाषं कषति, समूलकाषं कषति.
3.4.35: पिष् (to grind) takes **णमुल्** when शुष्क, चूर्ण, or रूक्ष is the object **उपपद**: शुष्कपेषं पिनष्टि, चूर्णपेषं पिनष्टि, रूक्षपेषं पिनष्टि.
3.4.36: हन् (to kill), कृ (to make), and ग्रह् (to seize) take **णमुल्** when समूल, अकृत, and जीव are respectively the object **उपपद**: समूलघातं हन्ति, अकृतकारं करोति, जीवग्राहं गृह्णाति.
3.4.37: हन् (to strike) takes **णमुल्** when an instrumental word is the **उपपद**: पाणिघातं वेदिं हन्ति, पादघातं भूमिं हन्ति.
3.4.38: पिष् (to grind) takes **णमुल्** when an instrumental word for a liquid is the **उपपद**: उदपेषं पिनष्टि, तैलपेषं पिनष्टि.
3.4.39: वर्ति (the causative of वृत्) and ग्रह् (to seize) take **णमुल्** when an instrumental word for the hand is the **उपपद**: हस्तवर्तं वर्तयति, हस्तग्राहं गृह्णाति.
3.4.40: पुष् (to feed) takes **णमुल्** when an instrumental word meaning स्व (self, kin, or property) is the **उपपद**: स्वपोषं पुष्णाति, आत्मपोषम्, धनपोषम्.
3.4.41: बन्ध् (to bind) takes **णमुल्** when a locative word is the **उपपद**: चक्रबन्धं बध्नाति, मुष्टिबन्धं बध्नाति.
3.4.42: बन्ध् (to bind) takes **णमुल्** when the word formed is a **संज्ञा** for a kind of knot: क्रौञ्चबन्धं बध्नाति, मयूरिकाबन्धं बद्धः.
3.4.43: नश् (to perish) and वह् (to carry) take **णमुल्** when जीव and पुरुष, naming the agent, are respectively the **उपपद**: जीवनाशं नश्यति, पुरुषवाहं वहति.
3.4.44: शुष् (to dry) and पूर् (to fill) take **णमुल्** when ऊर्ध्व, naming the agent, is the **उपपद**: ऊर्ध्वशोषं शुष्यति, ऊर्ध्वपूरं पूर्यते.
3.4.45: A root takes **णमुल्** when the object or agent **उपपद** denotes a likeness (इव): घृतनिधायं निहितः, kept as ghee would be; अजकनाशं नष्टः, perished like a goat.
3.4.46: After a **णमुल्** gerund from कष् etc., the following verb must come from the same root the gerund came from (a restricting rule on the **अनुप्रयोग**).
3.4.47: उप + दंश् (to bite, relish) takes **णमुल्** when an instrumental word is the **उपपद**: मूलकोपदंशं भुङ्क्ते or मूलकेनोपदंशम्.
3.4.48: Roots meaning हिंसा (to strike, injure) take **णमुल्** when an instrumental word is the **उपपद** and the gerund's object is the same as the main verb's: दण्डोपघातं गाः कालयति, दण्डताडम्.
3.4.49: उप + पीड् (to press), रुध् (to obstruct), and कृष् (to draw) take **णमुल्** when a locative word, or by च an instrumental word, is the **उपपद**: पार्श्वोपपीडं शेते, व्रजोपरोधं गाः स्थापयति, पाण्युपकर्षं धानाः सङ्गृह्णाति.
3.4.50: A root takes **णमुल्** with a locative or instrumental **उपपद** when close contact is meant: केशग्राहं युध्यन्ते, fighting locked together by the hair.
3.4.51: A root takes **णमुल्** with a locative or instrumental **उपपद** when a measure of length is meant: द्व्यङ्गुलोत्कर्षं खण्डिकां छिनत्ति, cutting pieces two fingers long.
3.4.52: A root takes **णमुल्** with an ablative **उपपद** when haste (परीप्सा) is meant: शय्योत्थायं धावति, running the instant he is up from bed.
3.4.53: A root takes **णमुल्** with an accusative **उपपद** when haste is meant: यष्टिग्राहं युध्यन्ते, fighting with whatever stick is at hand.
3.4.54: A root takes **णमुल्** with an accusative **उपपद** naming a non-vital limb of one's own body: भ्रूविक्षेपं कथयति, अक्षिनिकाणं जल्पति. (अध्रुव: a limb whose loss does not kill.)
3.4.55: A root takes **णमुल्** with an accusative **उपपद** naming a limb of one's own body that the action wholly afflicts: उरःपेषं युध्यन्ते, शिरःपेषम्. This reaches vital limbs too, where 3.4.54 does not.
3.4.56: विश् (to enter), पत् (to fall), पद् (to go), and स्कन्द् (to leap) take **णमुल्** with an accusative **उपपद** when full pervasion of the thing and repeated performance of the act are meant: गेहानुप्रवेशमास्ते.
3.4.57: अस् (to throw) and तृष् (to be thirsty) take **णमुल्** with an accusative **उपपद** naming time, when an interval between actions is meant: द्व्यहात्यासं गाः पाययति, watering the cows every third day.
3.4.58: आदिश् and ग्रह् (to seize) take **णमुल्** when नामन् (name) is the accusative **उपपद**: नामादेशमाचष्टे, नामग्राहं मामाह्वयति, calling me by name.
3.4.59: After **कृ**, with an indeclinable in **उपपद**, add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्** when the meaning is reporting something in a manner that misfits it (good news told softly, bad news told loudly): नीचैःकृत्य, नीचैःकृत्वा, नीचैःकारम्.
3.4.60: After **कृ**, with तिर्यक् in **उपपद**, add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्** when the meaning is finishing something off: तिर्यक्कृत्य, तिर्यक्कृत्वा, तिर्यक्कारम्.
3.4.61: After **कृ** and **भू**, with a **स्वाङ्ग** (body-part) word ending in the **तस्** affix in **उपपद**, add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्**: मुखतःकृत्य, मुखतःकृत्वा, मुखतःकारम्; पृष्ठतोभूय, पृष्ठतोभूत्वा, पृष्ठतोभावम्.
3.4.62: After **कृ** and **भू**, with a word in **उपपद** ending in ना, or in an affix meaning धा, or in the sense of **च्वि** (becoming what one was not), add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्**: नानाकृत्य, द्विधाकृत्य, etc.
3.4.63: After **भू**, with तूष्णीम् in **उपपद**, add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्**: तूष्णीम्भूय, तूष्णीं भूत्वा, तूष्णीम्भावम्. (Only **भू** here; **कृ** drops out.)
3.4.64: After **भू**, with अन्वक् in **उपपद** meaning being favorably disposed, add **क्त्वा** and **णमुल्**: अन्वग्भूय, अन्वग्भूत्वा, अन्वग्भावम्.
3.4.65: Add **तुमुन्** to any verb when a verb meaning शक् (be able), धृष्, ज्ञा, ग्लै, घट्, रभ्, लभ्, क्रम्, सह्, अर्ह्, or अस् stands with it: शक्नोति भोक्तुम्, अर्हति भोक्तुम्.
3.4.66: Add **तुमुन्** to a verb when अलम् or a synonym of it, in the sense of being capable, stands with it: पर्याप्तो भोक्तुम्, अलं भोक्तुम्, भोक्तुं पारयति.
3.4.67: The **कृत्** affixes mark the agent: कारकः, कर्ता, नन्दनः, ग्राही, पचः.
3.4.68: भव्य, गेय, प्रवचनीय, उपस्थानीय, जन्य, आप्लाव्य, आपात्य optionally mark the agent (otherwise they mark **भाव** and **कर्म** as **कृत्य** words do).
3.4.69: The **ल** affixes mark the object and the agent; after intransitive verbs they mark **भाव** (the bare action) and the agent: गम्यते देवदत्तेन, गच्छति देवदत्तः, आस्यते देवदत्तेन.
3.4.70: The **कृत्य** affixes, **क्त**, and the affixes meaning **खल्** mark only **भाव** and **कर्म** (the action and the object), never the agent: कर्तव्यः कटो भवता, आसितव्यं भवता.
3.4.71: When **क्त** expresses the start of an action, it also marks the agent (and still, by च, **भाव** and **कर्म**): प्रकृतः कटं देवदत्तः (agent), प्रकृतः कटो देवदत्तेन (object), प्रकृतं देवदत्तेन (action).
3.4.72: After verbs of motion, after intransitive verbs, and after श्लिष्, शी, स्था, आस्, वस्, जन्, रुह्, जृ, **क्त** marks the agent too (and still **भाव** and **कर्म**): गतो देवदत्तो ग्रामम्, आरूढो वृक्षं भवान्.
3.4.73: दाश and गोघ्न are formed irregularly, their affix marking the **सम्प्रदान** (recipient): दाश is one to whom things are given (a servant), गोघ्न one for whom the cow is killed (an honored guest).
3.4.74: भीम and the rest are formed irregularly, marking the **अपादान** (point of departure): भीम, भीष्म, भयानक, वरु, चरु, भूमि, रज, संस्कार, समुद्र, स्रुक्, खलति.
3.4.75: The **उणादि** affixes mark something other than these two — **सम्प्रदान** and **अपादान**: कृषिः, तन्तुः, वर्त्म, चर्म.
3.4.76: After verbs of staying-fixed, motion, and taking/eating, **क्त** also marks the **अधिकरण** (location), keeping its other senses by च: आसितो देवदत्तः, इदमेषामासितम्; यातो देवदत्तेन, इदमेषां यातम्; भुक्त ओदनो देवदत्तेन.
3.4.77: Whatever follows replaces **ल**. (Heading: supply लस्य in the sutras below — the substitutes for the ten **ल** affixes.)
3.4.78: The substitutes of **ल** are तिप्, तस्, झि, सिप्, थस्, थ, मिप्, वस्, मस् (**परस्मैपद**) and त, आताम्, झ, थास्, आथाम्, ध्वम्, इट्, वहि, महिङ् (**आत्मनेपद**) — together the **तिङ्** endings.
3.4.79: For the **आत्मनेपद** substitutes of a ट्-marked **ल** (लट्, लिट्, लुट्, लृट्, लोट्, लेट्), ए replaces the **टि** (final vowel plus what follows): त→ते, आताम्→आते, झ→झे.
3.4.80: से replaces थास् in the ट्-marked tenses: पचसे, पेचिषे, पक्तासे, पक्ष्यसे.
3.4.81: In **लिट्**, एश् replaces त and इरेच् replaces झ: पेचे, पेचाते, पेचिरे.
3.4.82: In **लिट्**, the **परस्मैपद** endings become णल्, अतुस्, उस् / थल्, अथुस्, अ / णल्, व, म: पपाच, पेचतुः, पेचुः; पेचिथ, पेचथुः, पेच; पपाच, पेचिव, पेचिम.
3.4.83: After विद् (to know), these nine **लिट्** endings optionally replace the **लट्** endings: वेद or वेत्ति, विदतुः or वित्तः, विदुः or विदन्ति.
3.4.84: After ब्रु, the first five **परस्मैपद** **लट्** endings optionally become the **लिट्** endings, and ब्रु itself becomes आह: आह, आहतुः, आहुः, आत्थ, आहथुः.
3.4.85: The **लोट्** endings behave like the **लङ्** endings (so ताम्, तम्, त, व, म, and the स्-drop): पचताम्, पचतम्, पचत, पचाव, पचाम.
3.4.86: In **लोट्**, उ replaces इ: ति→तु, अन्ति→अन्तु — पचतु, पचन्तु.
3.4.87: In **लोट्**, हि replaces सि, and this हि is treated as not having indicatory प् (so it is ङित्, blocking **गुण**): लुनीहि, पुनीहि, राध्नुहि, तक्ष्णुहि.
3.4.88: In the **छन्दस्**, this हि is optionally treated as not having indicatory प्: प्रीणाहि or प्रीणीहि; युयोधि or युयुधि.
3.4.89: In the **लोट्**, नि replaces the ending मि. This overrides the इ→उ change and the **लोप**.
3.4.90: In the **लोट्**, आम् replaces the ए that टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे would otherwise give the **आत्मनेपद** endings.
3.4.91: In the **लोट्**, an ए after स् becomes व् and an ए after व् becomes अम्. This overrides the आम् of the previous rule: से→स्व, ध्वे→ध्वम्.
3.4.92: In the **लोट्**, the first-person ending takes the augment आट् and counts as having an indicatory प्.
3.4.93: In the **लोट्**, the ए of the first-person **आत्मनेपद** endings becomes ऐ. An ए that arises from sandhi is not touched.
3.4.94: In the **लेट्**, the **तिङ्** endings take the augments अट् and आट्, by turns.
3.4.95: In the **लेट्**, ऐ replaces the आ of the first- and second-person dual **आत्मनेपद** endings.
3.4.96: In the **लेट्**, anywhere other than where the previous rule applies, ए optionally becomes ऐ.
3.4.97: In the **लेट्**, the इ of the **परस्मैपद** endings optionally drops.
3.4.98: In the **लेट्**, the स् of the first-person ending optionally drops.
3.4.99: The स् of the first-person ending always drops in the endings that replace a ल marked with indicatory ङ् (**लङ्**, **लिङ्**, **लुङ्**, **लृङ्**).
3.4.100: The इ of a **परस्मैपद** ending that replaces a ल marked with indicatory ङ् drops: ति→त्, सि→स्.
3.4.101: For a ल marked with indicatory ङ्, the endings तस्, थस्, थ, मिप् become ताम्, तम्, त, अम् respectively.
3.4.102: The **आत्मनेपद** endings of the **लिङ्** take the augment स्युट् (placed before the ending).
3.4.103: Before the **परस्मैपद** endings of the **लिङ्**, the augment यासुट् is added, acutely accented, and the ending counts as having an indicatory ङ्. This augment's ङ् marks it; the ङ् of the ल itself does not pass to its substitutes.
3.4.104: In the benedictive **लिङ्**, यासुट् is also added, acutely accented, and there the endings count as having an indicatory क्.
3.4.105: In the **लिङ्**, रन् replaces झ (overriding the usual अन्त).
3.4.106: In the **लिङ्**, the **आत्मनेपद** first-person singular इट् becomes अ. The final त् of अत् is only for pronunciation.
3.4.107: In the **लिङ्**, the endings beginning with त and थ take the augment सुट्.
3.4.108: In the **लिङ्**, जुस् replaces झि, the **परस्मैपद** third-person plural ending (overriding अन्त).
3.4.109: जुस् also replaces झि after a सिच् **लुङ्**, after a reduplicated **लङ्**, and after विद् 'know'.
3.4.110: When सिच् has dropped, जुस् replaces झि only after a **लुङ्** stem ending in long आ.
3.4.111: In शाकटायन's view, in the **लङ्** of roots ending in long आ, जुस् replaces झि. This holds only for a ल that is genuinely **लङ्**, not for one merely treated like **लङ्**.
3.4.112: In शाकटायन's view, in the **लङ्** after द्विष् 'hate', जुस् replaces झि.
3.4.113: The **तिङ्** endings and every affix with an indicatory श् are **सार्वधातुक**.
3.4.114: Every other affix added to a root is **आर्धधातुक**.
3.4.116: In the sense of benediction, the **लिङ्** endings are **आर्धधातुक**.
3.4.117: In the **छन्दस्**, an affix may be treated either way, as **सार्वधातुक** or as **आर्धधातुक**.
4.1.1: From here to the end of the fifth chapter, what follows is added after a stem ending in the feminine **ङी** or **आप्**, or after a **प्रातिपदिक**.
4.1.2: After a **ङी** or **आप्** ending or after a **प्रातिपदिक**, the 21 case-affixes are: 1st सु, औ, जस्; 2nd अम्, औट्, शस्; 3rd टा, भ्याम्, भिस्; 4th ङे, भ्याम्, भ्यस्; 5th ङसि, भ्याम्, भ्यस्; 6th ङस्, ओस्, आम्; 7th ङि, ओस्, सुप्. Together they are **सुप्**.
4.1.3: From here on, every affix taught applies when the feminine is to be marked.
4.1.4: After अज and the words listed with it, and after any **प्रातिपदिक** ending in short अ, the feminine takes **टाप्** (आ).
4.1.5: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in ऋ or न्, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.6: After a word that carries an indicatory **उक्** (उ, ऋ, ऌ), the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.7: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in वन्, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई), and र् replaces the final न्.
4.1.8: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in पाद्, the feminine optionally takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.9: When the word means a verse of the ऋग्वेद, a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in पाद् takes **टाप्** (आ) in the feminine instead.
4.1.10: After a **षट्** stem and after स्वसृ and the words listed with it, no feminine affix is added.
4.1.11: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in मन्, **ङीप्** is not added.
4.1.12: After a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in अन्, **ङीप्** is not added.
4.1.13: After both a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in मन् and a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in अन्, the feminine optionally takes **डाप्** (आ).
4.1.14: From here on, the rules apply only to a **प्रातिपदिक** that is not an **उपसर्जन** (the subordinate term in a compound).
4.1.15: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in short अ, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई) when its affix carries an indicatory ट्, or when the affix is ढ, अण्, अञ्, द्वयसच्, दघ्नच्, मात्रच्, तयप्, ठक्, ठञ्, कञ्, or क्वरप्.
4.1.16: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in **यञ्**, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.17: For the Eastern grammarians, after a word ending in **यञ्** the feminine takes **ष्फ**, which counts as a **तद्धित**.
4.1.18: After the **यञ्**-ending words from लोहित through कत, the feminine always takes **ष्फ**.
4.1.19: After कौरव्य and माण्डूक, the feminine takes **ष्फ**.
4.1.20: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in अ that names early age, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.21: After a **द्विगु** ending in अ, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.22: When a **तद्धित** affix has dropped, **ङीप्** is not added after a **द्विगु** ending in a word that does not name a measure, nor after बिस्त, आचित, or कम्बल्य.
4.1.23: When the **तद्धित** affix has dropped and the word means a field, **ङीप्** is not added after a **द्विगु** ending in काण्ड.
4.1.24: When the **तद्धित** affix has dropped and the word means a measure, **ङीप्** is optionally withheld after a **द्विगु** ending in पुरुष.
4.1.25: After a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in ऊधस्, the feminine takes **ङीष्** (ई).
4.1.26: After a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in ऊधस् that begins with a numeral or an indeclinable, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई) instead.
4.1.27: After a **बहुव्रीहि** beginning with a numeral and ending in दामन् or हायन, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.28: After a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in अन् that drops its penultimate अ, the feminine optionally takes **ङीप्** (ई).
4.1.29: In a Name and in the **छन्दस्**, that **बहुव्रीहि** ending in अन् which drops its penultimate अ takes **ङीप्** (ई) without option.
4.1.30: In a Name and in the **छन्दस्**, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई) after केवल, मामक, भागधेय, पाप, अपर, समान, आर्यकृत, सुमङ्गल, and भेषज.
4.1.31: In a Name and in the **छन्दस्**, the feminine takes **ङीप्** (ई) after रात्रि, except when जस् follows.
4.1.32: अन्तर्वत् and पतिवत् take the augment **नुक्** before feminine **ङीप्**, giving अन्तर्वत्नी 'pregnant' and पतिवत्नी 'whose husband is living'.
4.1.33: The final इ of पति becomes न् before feminine **ङीप्** when the word means a wife who shares her husband's sacrifices: पत्नी.
4.1.34: When पति stands at the end of a compound (not as an **उपसर्जन**), its final इ optionally becomes न् before **ङीप्**: वृद्धपत्नी or वृद्धपतिः.
4.1.35: In सपत्नि, एकपत्नि and the rest of that list, the final इ of पति always becomes न् before **ङीप्**: सपत्नी, एकपत्नी.
4.1.36: पूतक्रतु ends in ऐ before **ङीप्** when it means Pūtakratu's wife: पूतक्रतायी.
4.1.37: वृषाकपि, अग्नि, कुसित and कुसीद end in उदात्त ऐ before **ङीप्** when the word means the wife of that one: वृषाकपायी, अग्नायी, कुसितायी, कुसीदायी.
4.1.38: मनु optionally ends in औ before **ङीप्** (alongside the उदात्त ऐ), giving three forms: मनायी, मनावी, मनुः.
4.1.39: After a colour-word ending in an **अनुदात्त** vowel with त् as its penultimate, **ङीप्** is optional and the त् becomes न्: एनी or एता, श्येनी or श्येता, हरिणी or हरिता.
4.1.40: Every other colour-word ending in an **अनुदात्त** vowel takes **ङीष्**: सारङ्गी, कल्माषी, शबली.
4.1.41: A word ending in an affix marked with इत् ष्, and the words गौर etc., take **ङीष्**: नर्तकी, गौरी, मत्सी.
4.1.42: The eleven words जानपद, कुण्ड, गोण, स्थल, भाज, नाग, काल, नील, कुश, कामुक, कबर take **ङीष्** respectively in the senses 'profession', 'bowl', 'grain-sack', 'natural ground', 'cooked food', 'stout', 'black', 'blue (not cloth)', 'ploughshare', 'libidinous woman', 'braid of hair'.
4.1.43: After शोण, **ङीष्** is the Eastern grammarians' option: शोणी or शोणा वडवा.
4.1.44: A quality-word ending in short उ optionally takes **ङीष्**: पट्वी or पटुः, मृद्वी or मृदुः.
4.1.45: बहु and the rest of that list optionally take **ङीष्**: बह्वी or बहुः.
4.1.46: In the **छन्दस्**, बहु etc. always take **ङीष्**: बह्वी.
4.1.47: In the **छन्दस्**, भु (ending in short उ) always takes **ङीष्**: विभ्वी, प्रभ्वी, सुभ्वी.
4.1.48: A word takes **ङीष्** when it names a woman by her tie to her husband: गणकी 'the astrologer's wife', महामात्री.
4.1.49: इन्द्र, वरुण, भव, शर्व, रुद्र, मृड, and हिम, अरण्य, यव, यवन, मातुल, आचार्य take the augment **आनुक्** before **ङीष्**: इन्द्राणी, भवानी, रुद्राणी, हिमानी, यवनानी, मातुलानी.
4.1.50: A compound ending in क्रीत 'bought', whose first member names the means of purchase, takes **ङीष्**: वस्त्रक्रीती 'bought for cloth'.
4.1.51: A compound whose first member names the means and whose second member is a क्त-word takes **ङीष्** when it means a small amount: अभ्रविलिप्ती द्यौः 'a sky lightly smeared with cloud'.
4.1.52: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in a क्त-word with उदात्त on its last syllable takes **ङीष्**: शङ्खभिन्नी, केशलूनी.
4.1.53: When the first member of such an end-उदात्त क्त **बहुव्रीहि** is not a **स्वाङ्ग** (body-part) word, **ङीष्** is optional: शार्ङ्गजग्धी or शार्ङ्गजग्धा.
4.1.54: After a compound ending in a subordinate **स्वाङ्ग** (body-part) word whose final अ is not preceded by a conjunct, **ङीष्** is optional: चन्द्रमुखी or चन्द्रमुखा.
4.1.55: After compounds ending in नासिका, उदर, ओष्ठ, जङ्घा, दन्त, कर्ण, शृङ्ग, **ङीष्** is optional: तुङ्गनासिकी or तुङ्गनासिका, बिम्बोष्ठी or बिम्बोष्ठा.
4.1.56: **ङीष्** does not come after a **स्वाङ्ग** word of the क्रोडा class, nor after one of more than two syllables: कल्याणक्रोडा, पृथुजघना.
4.1.57: **ङीष्** does not come after a subordinate **स्वाङ्ग** word preceded by सह, नञ्, or विद्यमान: सकेशा, अकेशा, विद्यमानकेशा.
4.1.58: **ङीष्** does not come after नख or मुख when the word is a name: शूर्पणखा, गौरमुखा.
4.1.59: दीर्घजिह्वी 'long-tongued', a name, takes **ङीष्** in the **छन्दस्** even though a conjunct precedes its final.
4.1.60: When the first member of the compound is a direction-word, the feminine affix is **ङीप्** (overriding the **ङीष्** of 4.1.54–58, differing only in accent): प्राङ्मुखी, प्राङ्नासिकी.
4.1.61: A word ending in वाह् takes **ङीष्**: दित्यौही, प्रष्ठौही.
4.1.62: सखी and अशिश्वी are irregular **ङीष्**-forms in ordinary (non-Vedic) Sanskrit.
4.1.63: After a word that names a **जाति** (a species), is not feminine in its own meaning, and does not have य् as its next-to-last sound, the feminine is **ङीष्**.
4.1.64: After a **जाति** word ending in पाक, कर्ण, पर्ण, पुष्प, फल, मूल, or वाल, the feminine is also **ङीष्**.
4.1.65: After a word ending in short इ that names a class of people, the feminine is **ङीष्**.
4.1.66: After a word ending in short उ that names a class of people, the feminine is **ऊङ्** (carrying over: not having य् before the उ).
4.1.67: After a word ending in बाहु, when it is a name, the feminine is **ऊङ्**.
4.1.68: After पङ्गु, the feminine is also **ऊङ्**.
4.1.69: After a word ending in ऊरु, when a comparison is meant, the feminine is **ऊङ्**.
4.1.70: In the **छन्दस्**, after ऊरु preceded by संहित, शफ, लक्षण, or वाम, the feminine is **ऊङ्** (no comparison meant).
4.1.71: In the **छन्दस्**, after कद्रु and कमण्डलु, the feminine is **ऊङ्**.
4.1.72: After कद्रु and कमण्डलु, when they are names, the feminine is **ऊङ्**.
4.1.73: After शार्ङ्गरव and its group, and after any word ending in **अञ्**, the feminine is **ङीन्** (same forms as **ङीष्**, differing only in accent).
4.1.74: After a word ending in **ञ्यङ्** or **ष्यङ्**, the feminine is **चाप्**.
4.1.75: After आवट्य, the feminine is also **चाप्**.
4.1.76: From here on, the affixes taught are **तद्धित**.
4.1.77: After युवन्, the feminine is ति, and this ति is a **तद्धित**.
4.1.78: In a **गोत्र** name, **अण्** and **इञ्** become **ष्यङ्** (with **चाप्**) for the feminine, when the word is non-ऋषि and has a heavy next-to-last syllable.
4.1.79: After a minor **गोत्र** (a family name), **अण्** and **इञ्** become **ष्यङ्** for the feminine, even when the next-to-last syllable is not heavy.
4.1.80: After क्रौडि and its group, the feminine is **ष्यङ्** (even without a heavy next-to-last syllable, and even without **अण्** or **इञ्**).
4.1.81: After दैवयज्ञि, शौचिवृक्षि, सात्यमुग्रि, and काण्ठेविद्धि, the feminine is **ष्यङ्** optionally.
4.1.82: Of the words in construction, a **तद्धित** attaches—optionally, when it attaches at all—after the first one.
4.1.83: From here up to तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् [[4.4.2]], the affix is **अण्** (except where a specific rule overrides it).
4.1.84: After अश्वपति and its group, the affix is **अण्** (in the senses running up to [[4.4.2]]).
4.1.85: After दिति, अदिति, आदित्य, and any word ending in पति, the affix is **ण्य**.
4.1.86: After उत्स and its group, the affix is **अञ्**.
4.1.87: After स्त्री the affix is **नञ्**, and after पुंस् the affix is **स्नञ्**, in the senses running up to धान्यानां भवने क्षेत्रे खञ् [[5.2.1]].
4.1.88: A **तद्धित** added because of a **द्विगु** compound drops by **लुक्** (in the senses up to [[4.4.2]]), except when it is a **गोत्र** affix.
4.1.89: The **लुक्** that drops a plural **गोत्र** affix is blocked when a vowel-initial affix (in the senses up to [[4.4.2]]) follows; the base counts as if the affix were still there.
4.1.90: The **युवन्** affix drops by **लुक्** when a vowel-initial affix (in the senses up to [[4.4.2]]) is to be added; drop it first, then add the new affix to what remains.
4.1.91: The **युवन्** affixes **फक्** and **फिञ्** drop by **लुक्** optionally when such a vowel-initial affix is to be added.
4.1.92: In the sense "descendant of ___," the **प्रत्यय** starting with **अण्** in प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] and all that follow attach to a word in the genitive.
4.1.93: For a **गोत्र** descendant — anyone from the grandson on down, however many generations removed — one and the same **प्रत्यय** attaches, always to the first ancestor's stem.
4.1.94: A **युवन्** **प्रत्यय** (for a descendant whose elder of the line is still alive, जीवति तु वंश्ये युवा [[4.1.163]]) attaches only after a stem that already ends in a **गोत्र** **प्रत्यय**; but in the feminine the word is not **युवन्** and takes no further **प्रत्यय**.
4.1.95: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in short अ, the descendant **प्रत्यय** is **इञ्**.
4.1.96: After बाहु and the rest, the descendant **प्रत्यय** is **इञ्**.
4.1.97: After सुधातृ the descendant **प्रत्यय** is **इञ्**, and the ऋ of सुधातृ becomes **अकङ्** before it.
4.1.98: For a **गोत्र** descendant, after कुञ्ज and the rest the **प्रत्यय** is **च्फञ्**.
4.1.99: For a **गोत्र** descendant, after the **प्रातिपदिक**s नड and the rest the **प्रत्यय** is **फक्**.
4.1.100: After हरित and the rest, once they end in **अञ्** (अनृष्यानन्तर्ये बिदादिभ्योऽञ् [[4.1.104]]), the **प्रत्यय** is **फक्**.
4.1.101: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in the **गोत्र** **प्रत्यय** **यञ्** or **इञ्**, the descendant **प्रत्यय** is **फक्**.
4.1.102: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **फक्** after शरद्वत्, शुनक, and दर्भ when they mean a descendant of भृगु, वत्स, and अग्रायण respectively.
4.1.103: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is optionally **फक्** after द्रोण, पर्वत, and जीवन्त.
4.1.104: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अञ्** after बिद and the rest; but after those of this set that are not names of sages, **अञ्** marks the immediate descendant.
4.1.105: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **यञ्** after गर्ग and the rest.
4.1.106: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **यञ्** after मधु and बभ्रु when the words formed mean a ब्राह्मण and a कौशिक respectively.
4.1.107: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **यञ्** after कपि and बोध when an आङ्गिरस descendant is meant.
4.1.108: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **यञ्** after वतण्ड when an आङ्गिरस descendant is meant.
4.1.109: In the feminine, the **यञ्** of वातण्ड्य drops by **लुक्** when an आङ्गिरस female descendant is meant.
4.1.110: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **फञ्** after अश्व and the rest.
4.1.111: For a **गोत्र** descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **फञ्** after भर्ग when a त्रैगर्त is meant.
4.1.112: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after शिव and the rest.
4.1.113: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after non-**वृद्ध** words that name a river or a woman, when used as a name and not as an adjective.
4.1.114: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after a **प्रातिपदिक** naming a sage or a person of the अन्धक, वृष्णि, or कुरु line.
4.1.115: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after मातृ preceded by a numeral or by सम् or भद्र, and the final ऋ of मातृ becomes उ.
4.1.116: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after कन्या, and कन्या becomes कनीन before it.
4.1.117: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **अण्** after विकर्ण, शुङ्ग, and छगल when a descendant of वत्स, भारद्वाज, and अत्रि respectively is meant.
