4.1.118: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is optionally **अण्** after पीला.
4.1.119: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** after मण्डूक is **ढक्**, and optionally **अण्** as well.
4.1.120: For a **गोत्र** descendant, words ending in a feminine **प्रत्यय** (आ or ई) take **ढक्**.
4.1.121: For a descendant, the **प्रत्यय** is **ढक्** after a word of two vowels ending in a feminine **प्रत्यय**.
4.1.122: After a disyllabic **प्रातिपदिक** ending in short इ, **ढक्** marks a descendant — but not after a stem ending in the patronymic **इञ्**.
4.1.123: After शुभ्र and the rest, **ढक्** marks a descendant; the list is an **आकृतिगण**, so words like गङ्गा and पाण्डव take it too.
4.1.124: After विकर्ण and कुषीतक, **ढक्** marks a descendant when the descendant is a काश्यप.
4.1.125: After भ्रू, **ढक्** marks a descendant, and the augment **वुक्** attaches along with it.
4.1.126: After कल्याणी and the rest, **ढक्** marks a descendant, and **इनङ्** replaces the final.
4.1.127: After कुलटा, **ढक्** marks a descendant, and **इनङ्** optionally replaces the final.
4.1.130: After गोधा, **आरक्** marks a descendant, by the Northern grammarians' rule.
4.1.131: After feminine stems naming mean or defective beings, **ढ्रक्** optionally marks a descendant.
4.1.133: The final vowel of पितृष्वसृ drops before the **ढक्** that marks a descendant.
4.1.134: After मातृष्वसृ likewise, **छण्** marks a descendant, and the final drops before **ढक्**.
4.1.135: After stems naming four-footed animals, **ढञ्** marks a descendant.
4.1.136: After गृष्टि and the rest, **ढञ्** marks a descendant.
4.1.137: After राजन् and श्वशुर, **यत्** marks a descendant.
4.1.139: After कुल, and after a compound ending in कुल, **ख** marks a descendant.
4.1.140: After कुल not preceded by a **पद**, **यत्** and **ढकञ्** optionally mark a descendant.
4.1.141: After महाकुल, **अञ्** and **खञ्** optionally mark a descendant.
4.1.142: After दुष्कुल, **ढक्** optionally marks a descendant.
4.1.144: After भ्रातृ, **व्यत्** marks a descendant; **च** adds **छ** as well.
4.1.145: After भ्रातृ, **व्यन्** marks an enemy (not a descendant).
4.1.146: After रेवती and the rest, **ठक्** marks a descendant.
4.1.147: After a feminine word naming a **गोत्र** descendant, when contempt is meant, **ण** marks a descendant; **च** adds **ठक्** as well.
4.1.148: After a **वृद्ध** word naming a सौवीर **गोत्र**, when contempt is meant, **ठक्** variously marks a descendant.
4.1.149: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in **फिञ्** and naming a सौवीर **गोत्र**, when contempt is meant, **छ** marks a descendant; **च** adds **ठक्** as well.
4.1.150: After फाण्टाहृति and मिमत naming a सौवीर descendant, **ण** and **फिञ्** mark a descendant.
4.1.151: After कुरु and the rest, **ण्य** marks a descendant.
4.1.152: A **प्रातिपदिक** ending in सेना, the word लक्षण, and words for artisans (कारि — weavers, barbers, potters and the like) take **ण्य** for a descendant.
4.1.153: For the Northern grammarians, those same stems — ending in सेना, लक्षण, and artisan-words — take **इञ्** for a descendant instead.
4.1.154: तिक, कितव, संज्ञा, बाल and the rest take **फिञ्** for a descendant.
4.1.155: कौसल्य and कार्मार्य take **फिञ्** for a descendant, blocking **इञ्**.
4.1.156: A two-syllable stem ending in the affix **अण्** takes **फिञ्** for a descendant, blocking **इञ्**.
4.1.157: For the Northern grammarians, a **वृद्ध** stem (one with a **वृद्धि** vowel in its first syllable) that is not a **गोत्र** name takes **फिञ्** for a descendant.
4.1.158: वाकिन, गारेध and the rest take **फिञ्** for a descendant and add the augment कुक् (क्) before it.
4.1.159: A stem ending in पुत्र optionally adds the augment कुक् (क्) before the **फिञ्** that marks a descendant.
4.1.160: For the Eastern grammarians, a stem without a **वृद्धि** vowel in its first syllable variably takes **फिन्** for a descendant.
4.1.161: मनु takes **अञ्** or **यत्** and adds the augment षुक् before them when the whole word names a **जाति** (a class): मानुष, मनुष्य.
4.1.162: A descendant from the grandson onward is **गोत्र**.
4.1.163: But while someone higher in the line of descent is alive, the descendant from the grandson onward is **युवन्**, not **गोत्र**.
4.1.164: And while an elder brother is alive, the younger one — a descendant from the grandson onward — is **युवन्**.
4.1.165: While a **सपिण्ड** other than a brother, higher in descent and older, is alive, the descendant from the grandson onward is optionally **युवन्**.
4.1.166: A **गोत्र** is optionally treated as **युवन्** when respect is meant.
4.1.167: A **युवन्** is optionally treated as **गोत्र** when contempt is meant.
4.1.168: A word that names a country and its **क्षत्रिय** tribe takes **अञ्** for a descendant.
4.1.169: साल्वेय and गान्धारि take **अञ्** for a descendant.
4.1.170: A two-syllable country-and-**क्षत्रिय** name, and मगध, कलिङ्ग, सूरमस, take **अण्** for a descendant, blocking **अञ्**.
4.1.171: A **वृद्ध** country-and-**क्षत्रिय** name, one ending in short इ, and कोसल, अजाद, take **ञ्यङ्** for a descendant, blocking **अञ्**.
4.1.172: कुरु and words beginning with न, as country-and-**क्षत्रिय** names, take **ण्य** for a descendant, blocking **अण्** and **अञ्**.
4.1.173: A word for a subdivision of the साल्व country, and प्रत्यग्रथ, कलकूट, अश्मक, take **इञ्** for a descendant, blocking **अञ्**.
4.1.175: After कम्बोज the **तद्राज** affix drops by **लुक्**.
4.1.176: In the feminine, the **तद्राज** affix drops by **लुक्** after अवन्ति, कुन्ति, and कुरु.
4.1.177: And in the feminine, a **तद्राज** affix that is अ drops by **लुक्**.
4.1.178: But the **तद्राज** does not drop in the feminine after the Eastern **क्षत्रिय** names, after भर्ग and the rest, or after यौधेय and the rest.
4.2.1: A colour-name in the instrumental takes **अण्** in the sense of "coloured by it": कषाय → काषाय.
4.2.2: लाक्षा, रोचना, शकल, कर्दम take **ठक्** in the sense of "coloured by it," blocking **अण्**.
4.2.3: A lunar-mansion name in the instrumental takes **अण्** for a time joined to that asterism (the moon standing in it): पुष्य → पौष.
4.2.4: The **प्रत्यय** of the preceding rule drops by **लुप्** when the time the asterism marks is not specified as day or night (अद्य पुष्यः).
4.2.5: After श्रवण and अश्वत्थ the **प्रत्यय** drops by **लुप्** when the whole word is a **संज्ञा** and the time is specified (श्रवणा रात्रिः).
4.2.6: After a **द्वन्द्व** of asterism-names in the third (instrumental) case, **छ** marks the time tied to those asterisks, specified or not (राधानुराधीया रात्रिः) — this blocks the **लुप्** of 4.2.4.
4.2.7: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, the **प्रत्यय** (अण् by 4.1.83) marks what that one saw, when the thing seen is a portion of the साम वेद (क्रुञ्चेन दृष्टं → क्रौञ्चं साम).
4.2.8: After कलि in the third case, **ढक्** marks the साम seen — this blocks अण् (कलिना दृष्टं → कालेयम्). After अग्नि and कलि **ढक्** always takes hold, in every sense, not just 'साम seen'.
4.2.9: After वामदेव in the third case, **ड्यत्** and **ड्य** mark the साम seen — these block अण् (वामदेवेन दृष्टं → वामदेव्यम्).
4.2.10: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, the **प्रत्यय** (अण् by 4.1.83) marks what it surrounds, when the thing surrounded is a chariot (वस्त्रेण परिवृतो रथः → वास्त्रः).
4.2.11: After पाण्डुकम्बल and the rest, in the third case, **इनि** marks the chariot surrounded by it — this blocks अण् (पाण्डुकम्बली रथः).
4.2.12: After द्वैप and वैयाघ्र in the third case, **अञ्** marks the chariot surrounded by it — this blocks अण्, differing only in accent (द्वैपेन परिवृतो रथः → द्वैपः).
4.2.13: कौमार is the irregular **अण्**-form of कुमारी meaning a marriage where the woman was a maid, never married before (कौमारो भर्ता, कौमारी भार्या).
4.2.14: After a word for a vessel in the seventh (locative) case, the **प्रत्यय** (अण्/अञ् by 4.1.83) marks what was served up on it (शरावेषूद्धृतः → शाराव ओदनः). This locative force governs through 4.2.20.
4.2.15: After स्थण्डिल in the seventh (locative) case, the **प्रत्यय** marks one whose **व्रत** is to sleep on it, the bare ground (स्थण्डिले शयितुं व्रतमस्य → स्थाण्डिलः).
4.2.16: After a word in the seventh (locative) case, **अण्** marks what is prepared in it, when that thing is granular food (भ्राष्ट्रे संस्कृता भक्षाः → भ्राष्ट्राः).
4.2.17: After शूल and उखा in the seventh (locative) case, **यत्** marks the food prepared in it — this blocks अण् (शूले संस्कृतम् → शूल्यम्).
4.2.18: After दधि in the seventh (locative) case, **ठक्** marks the food prepared in it — curd itself seasoned, not food seasoned with curd (दधनि संस्कृतम् → दाधिकम्).
4.2.19: After उदश्वित् in the seventh (locative) case, **ठक्** optionally marks the food prepared in it; otherwise अण् (औदश्वित्कम् or औदश्वितम्).
4.2.20: After क्षीर in the seventh (locative) case, **ढञ्** marks the food prepared in it — this blocks अण् (क्षीरे संस्कृता → क्षैरेयी यवागूः).
4.2.21: After the name of a full-moon night (first case), the **प्रत्यय** (अण् by 4.1.83) marks the division of time the night falls in, when the result is a **संज्ञा** for a month, fortnight, or year (पौषी पौर्णमासी अस्मिन् → पौषो मासः).
4.2.22: After आग्रहायणी and अश्वत्थ, full-moon-night names in the first case, **ठक्** marks the time they fall in — this blocks अण् (आग्रहायणिको मासः).
4.2.23: After फाल्गुनी, श्रवणा, कार्त्तिकी, चैत्री, full-moon-night names, **ढक्** optionally marks the division of time, against the usual अण् (फाल्गुनः or फाल्गुनिकः).
4.2.24: After the name of a देवता (first case), the **प्रत्यय** (अण् by 4.1.83) marks what belongs to that deity (इन्द्रो देवताऽस्य → ऐन्द्रं हविः). This 'its deity' sense governs through 4.2.35.
4.2.25: इ replaces the final अ of क when the **प्रत्यय** is added (क + अण् → कायम् हविः).
4.2.26: After शुक्र, **घन्** marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् (शुक्रियं हविः).
4.2.27: After अपोनप्तृ and अपान्नप्तृ, **घ** marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् (अपोनप्त्रियं हविः).
4.2.28: After अपोनप्तृ and अपान्नप्तृ, **छ** too marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् (अपोनप्त्रीयं हविः).
4.2.29: After महेन्द्र, **घ**, **अण्**, and **छ** mark it as the देवता (महेन्द्रियम्, माहेन्द्रम्, महेन्द्रीयम्).
4.2.30: After सोम, **ट्यण्** marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण्; the ण् gives **वृद्धि**, the ट gives **ङीप्** in the feminine (सौम्यं हविः, सौमी ऋक्).
4.2.31: After वायु, ऋतु, पितृ, उषस्, **यत्** marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् (वायव्यम्, ऋतव्यम्, पित्र्यम्, उषस्यम्).
4.2.32: After द्यावापृथिवी, शुनासीर, मरुत्वत्, अग्नीषोम, वास्तोष्पति, गृहमेधा, **छ** (and **यत्**) marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् and ण्य (द्यावापृथिवीयम् or द्यावापृथिव्यम्).
4.2.33: After अग्नि, **ढक्** marks it as the देवता — this blocks अण् (अग्निर्देवताऽस्य → आग्नेयोऽष्टाकपालः).
4.2.34: After a word for a time-period, the same affixes that mark "who stays in it" (**ठञ्** etc., from [[4.3.11]] through [[4.3.53]]) also mark "this is its deity".
4.2.35: After महाराज and प्रोष्ठपद, **ठञ्** marks "this is its deity".
4.2.36: पितृव्य, मातुल, मातामह, पितामह are formed irregularly; from their shape you read back the affix, its meaning, and the case it follows.
4.2.37: For "a collection of it", an affix follows the word in the genitive (by default **अण्**, where no later rule sets a different one).
4.2.38: After भिक्षा and the rest of its list, **अण्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.39: After a **गोत्र** (offspring) word and after उक्ष, उष्ट्र, उरभ्र, राजन्, राजन्य, राजपुत्र, वत्स, मनुष्य, अज, **वुञ्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.40: After केदार, **यञ्** and **वुञ्** mark "a collection of it".
4.2.41: After कवचिन्, and also (carried over by च) after केदार, **ठञ्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.42: After ब्राह्मण, माणव, वाडव, **यन्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.43: After ग्राम, जन, बन्धु, सहाय, **तल्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.44: After a word with **अनुदात्त** on its first syllable, **अञ्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.45: After खण्डिक and the rest of its list, **अञ्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.46: After the name of a Vedic school (चरण: कठ, कलाप, ...), the same affixes that mark its body of rules also mark "a collection of it".
4.2.47: After a word for an unconscious thing, and after हस्ति and धेनु, **ठक्** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.48: After केश and अश्व respectively, **यञ्** and **छ** optionally mark "a collection of it".
4.2.49: After पाश and the rest of its list, **य** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.50: After खल, गो, रथ, **य** marks "a collection of it".
4.2.51: After खल, गो, रथ respectively, **इनि**, **त्र**, **कट्यच्** mark "a collection of it".
4.2.52: After a word in the genitive, **अण्** marks its sphere (विषय), when that sphere is a country.
4.2.53: After राजन्य and the rest of its list, **वुञ्** marks the sphere-as-country.
4.2.54: After भौरिकि etc. and after ऐषुकारि etc. respectively, **विधल्** and **भक्तल्** mark the sphere-as-country.
4.2.55: After the name of a meter, **अण्** marks a प्रगाथ that begins with that meter.
4.2.56: After a word for the object of a battle or for its leading warriors, **अण्** marks the battle itself.
4.2.57: After the name of a weapon, **ण** marks a game played with it.
4.2.58: After an action-word ending in **घञ्**, **ञ** marks the thing in which that action occurs.
4.2.59: After a word for a subject of study (in the accusative), **अण्** marks "who studies it" or "who knows it".
4.2.60: After the name of a sacrifice, after उक्थ etc., and after a stem ending in सूत्र, **ठक्** marks "who studies it" or "who knows it".
4.2.61: After क्रम etc., **वुन्** marks "who studies it" or "who knows it".
4.2.62: After अनुब्राह्मण, **इनि** marks "who studies it" or "who knows it".
4.2.63: After वसन्त etc., **ठक्** marks "who studies it" or "who knows it".
4.2.64: After the name of a work that ends in a **प्रोक्त** affix (a word naming the one who announced the work), the affix meaning "studies it" or "knows it" drops by **लुक्**.
4.2.65: The affix meaning "studies it" or "knows it" drops by **लुक्** after the title of a **सूत्र** work that has क् as its penultimate sound and is not itself a **प्रोक्त** form (and the title is built on a number-word).
4.2.66: **छन्दस्** texts and **ब्राह्मण**s ending in a **प्रोक्त** affix carry only this sense: "who studies" or "who knows" them, nothing else.
4.2.67: After a thing-word in the first case, an affix is added in the sense "that thing is in this place," when the whole form names that place. (This blocks the **मतुप्**-class affixes.)
4.2.68: After a word in the third case, an affix is added in the sense "completed by it," when the whole form names a place.
4.2.69: After a word in the sixth case, an affix is added in the sense "their dwelling-place," when the whole form names a place.
4.2.70: And after a word in the sixth case, an affix is added in the sense "found near it," when the whole form names a place. (च carries all four senses—4.2.67 through 4.2.70—forward together.)
4.2.71: After a stem ending in उ or ऊ, the affix **अञ्** is added in these four senses. (This blocks the general **अण्**.)
4.2.72: After a word ending in **मतुप्** whose stem—**मतुप्** aside—has more than two vowels, the affix **अञ्** is added in the four senses. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.73: After a **प्रातिपदिक** of more than two vowels, the affix **अञ्** is added in the four senses when a well is named. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.74: The affix **अञ्** is added in the four senses for a well on the northern bank of the river विपाश्, after any stem. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.75: After संकल and the rest, the affix **अञ्** is added in the four senses. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.76: The affix **अञ्** is also added in the four senses, the form always feminine, when a place in the सौवीर, साल्व, or eastern lands is named. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.77: After सुवास्तु and the rest, the affix **अण्** is added in the four senses. (This blocks the **अञ्** of 4.2.71 and 4.2.73.)
4.2.78: After रोणी, the affix **अण्** is added in the four senses, whether रोणी stands alone or ends a compound. (This blocks the **अञ्** for a well.)
4.2.79: After a stem with क् as its penultimate sound, the affix **अण्** is added in the four senses. (This blocks the **अञ्** of 4.2.71 and 4.2.73.)
4.2.80: In the four senses, seventeen affixes—**वुञ्**, **छण्**, कठ, जिल, सेनि, ढञ्, ण्य, यफ, **फिञ्**, **इञ्**, **ञ्य**, क, **ठक्**—are added to the seventeen word-classes अरीहण, कृशाश्व, ऋश्य, कुमुद, काश, तृण, प्रेक्षा, अश्मन्, सखि, संकाश, बल, पक्ष, कर्ण, सुतंगम, प्रगदिन्, वराह, कुमुद and the rest, matched in order. (This blocks **अण्**.)
4.2.81: When the place named is a kingdom, the four-sense affix drops by **लुप्** (and number and gender stay as in the people's name).
4.2.82: After वरण and the rest, the four-sense affix also drops by **लुप्**, for a place that is not a kingdom. (This is an open class; the same holds beyond the listed words.)
4.2.83: After शर्करा, the four-sense affix optionally drops by **लुप्**—that is, when शर्करा takes the general **अण्**.
4.2.84: After शर्करा, the affixes **ठक्** and छ are also added in the four senses.
4.2.85: When a river is named, the affix **मतुप्** is added in the four senses.
4.2.86: After मधु and the rest, the affix **मतुप्** is added in the four senses, for what is not a river.
4.2.87: After कुमुद, नड, and वेतस, the affix **ड्मतुप्** is added in the four senses, dropping the stem's final sound. (So too after महिष.)
4.2.88: After नड and शाद, the affix **ड्वलच्** is added in the four senses, dropping the stem's final sound.
4.2.89: After शिखा, the affix वलच् is added in the four senses—this one names a place, unlike the वलच् of 5.2.113.
4.2.90: After उत्कर and the rest, the affix छ is added in the four senses.
4.2.91: After नड and the rest, the affix छ is added in the four senses, with the augment **कुक्** after the stem. (क्रुञ्चा shortens its vowel and तक्षन् drops its न् here.)
4.2.92: **शेष**: the affixes taught from here on carry senses other than progeny through the four place-senses already given.
4.2.93: After राष्ट्र the affix घ is added, and after अवारपार the affix ख—each to its own word.
4.2.94: ग्राम takes the **प्रत्यय**s य and खञ् (ईन).
4.2.96: कुल, कुक्षि, ग्रीवा take ढकञ् when the word means a dog, a sword, and an ornament respectively.
4.2.97: नदी, मही, वाराणसी... take ढक् in the remaining (शैषिक) senses.
4.2.98: दक्षिणा, पश्चात्, पुरस् take त्यक् (त्य) in the remaining senses.
4.2.99: कापिशी takes ष्फक् in the remaining senses (the feminine adds ङीष्).
4.2.100: रंकु takes ष्फक् and अण् in the remaining senses when the word names a non-human being.
4.2.101: दिव्, प्राच्, अपाच्, उदच्, प्रत्यच् take यत् in the remaining senses.
4.2.102: कन्था takes ठक् in the remaining senses.
4.2.103: कन्था takes वुक् instead when the कन्था is in the land of वर्णु.
4.2.104: An indeclinable takes त्यप् in the remaining senses.
4.2.105: ऐषमस्, ह्यस्, श्वस् optionally take त्यप् in the remaining senses.
4.2.106: A word ending in तीर takes अञ्, and a word ending in रूप्य takes ञ्, in the remaining senses.
4.2.107: A word whose first member names a direction takes ञ् in the remaining senses, when the whole is not a name.
4.2.108: मद्र preceded by a direction-word takes अञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.109: A word of more than two syllables, accented उदात्त on its final and naming a village of the North-folk, takes अञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.110: A word ending in प्रस्थ, the words पलदी and the rest, and a word with penultimate क take अण् in the remaining senses.
4.2.111: A गोत्र-name formed from कण्व and the rest takes अण् in the remaining senses.
4.2.112: A गोत्र-name formed by इञ् takes अण् in the remaining senses.
4.2.113: A two-syllable इञ्-ending गोत्र-name of the Eastern-folk or of भरत does not take that अण्.
4.2.114: A वृद्ध word takes छ in the remaining senses.
4.2.115: The वृद्ध word भवत् takes ठक् and छस् in the remaining senses.
4.2.116: काशि, चेदि... take ठञ् and ञिठ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.117: वृद्ध words naming villages of वाहीक take ठञ् and ञिठ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.118: वृद्ध words naming वाहीक villages in उशीनर optionally take ठञ् and ञिठ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.119: A nominal stem ending in उ and naming a locality takes ठञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.120: A वृद्ध word ending in उ and naming a locality of the East-folk takes ठञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.121: A वृद्ध locality-word with penultimate य, or one naming a desert (धन्व), takes वुञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.122: A वृद्ध locality-word ending in प्रस्थ, पुर, or वह takes वुञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.123: A वृद्ध word naming a locality of the East-folk, with penultimate र or ending in ई, takes वुञ् in the remaining senses.
4.2.124: After a **वृद्ध** word naming an inhabited kingdom (**जनपद**) or the boundary of one, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **छ**.
4.2.125: When the **जनपद** word or its boundary-word stands always in the plural, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses even from a non-**वृद्ध** word, as well as from a **वृद्ध** one, blocking **अण्** and **छ**.
4.2.126: After a place-name whose second member is कच्छ, अग्नि, वक्त्र, or गर्त, **वृद्ध** or not, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **छ** and **अण्**.
4.2.127: After धूम and the rest naming a place, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्** and the others.
4.2.128: After नगर, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses when censure or skill is meant.
4.2.129: After अरण्य, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses when a man is meant, blocking ण.
4.2.130: After कुरु and युगन्धर, **वुञ्** optionally comes in the leftover senses.
4.2.131: After मद्र and वृजि, **कन्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **वुञ्**.
4.2.132: After a place-name with क as its second-to-last sound, **अण्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **वुञ्**.
4.2.133: After कच्छ and the rest naming a place, **अण्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **वुञ्** and the others.
4.2.134: After कच्छ and the rest, **वुञ्** comes when a man or what is found in a man is meant, blocking **अण्**.
4.2.135: After साल्व, **वुञ्** comes for a man or what is found in a man only when no foot-soldier is meant.
4.2.136: After साल्व, **वुञ्** comes in the leftover senses when a cow or barley gruel is meant, blocking **अण्**.
4.2.137: After a place-name whose second member is गर्त, **छ** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्**.
4.2.138: After गह and the rest, **छ** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्** and the others.
4.2.139: After कट and the rest naming places of the Easterners, **छ** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्**.
4.2.140: With **छ**, क replaces the final of राजन्.
4.2.141: After a **वृद्ध** place-name ending in **अक्** or **इक्**, or having ख as its second-to-last sound, **छ** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्** and the others.
4.2.142: After a **वृद्ध** place-name whose second member is कन्था, पलद, नगर, ग्राम, or हृद, **छ** comes in the leftover senses.
4.2.143: After पर्वत, **छ** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्**.
4.2.144: After पर्वत, **छ** optionally comes in the leftover senses when no man is meant.
4.2.145: After कृकण and पर्ण naming the country भारद्वाज, **छ** comes in the leftover senses.
4.3.1: After युष्मद् and अस्मद्, **खञ्** optionally comes in the leftover senses; च adds **छ**, and the option leaves **अण्** too.
4.3.2: Before **खञ्** and before **अण्**, युष्माक and अस्माक replace युष्मद् and अस्मद्.
4.3.3: When one individual is meant, तवक and ममक replace युष्मद् and अस्मद् before **खञ्** and **अण्**.
4.3.4: After अर्ध, **यत्** comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.5: After अर्ध preceded by पर, अवर, अधम, or उत्तम, **यत्** comes in the leftover senses.
4.3.6: After अर्ध whose prior member names a direction, **ठञ्** comes in the leftover senses, and by च **यत्** too, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.7: After अर्ध preceded by a direction-word, naming a portion of a village or an inhabited country, **अञ्** and **ठञ्** come in the leftover senses, blocking **यत्**.
4.3.8: After मध्य, म comes in the leftover senses, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.9: After मध्य, in the remaining senses, add the **प्रत्यय** अ when the meaning is 'fit' or 'proper'; this blocks मस् (मध्य → माध्य).
4.3.10: After द्वीप meaning 'near the sea', in the remaining senses, add **यञ्**; this blocks both अण् and वुञ् (द्वीप → द्वैप्य).
4.3.11: After a word denoting time, in the remaining senses, add **ठञ्** instead of अण् (मास → मासिक); this heading on काल runs through 4.3.25.
4.3.12: After शरद् naming a श्राद्ध (funeral oblation), in the remaining senses, add **ठञ्** instead of अण् (शरद् → शारदिक).
4.3.13: After शरद् naming illness or heat, in the remaining senses, **ठञ्** is optional instead of अण् (शरद् → शारदिक / शारद).
4.3.14: After निशा and प्रदोष, in the remaining senses, **ठञ्** is optional (निशा → नैशिक / नैश).
4.3.15: After श्वस्, in the remaining senses, **ठञ्** is optional, and श्वस् takes the augment तुट् (श्वस् → शौवस्तिक).
4.3.16: After संधिवेला and its group, and after words for a season or an asterism, in the remaining senses, add **अण्** instead of ठञ्; restating अण् here also blocks छ for the वृद्ध words (संधिवेला → सांधिवेल, ग्रीष्म → ग्रैष्म, तिष्य → तैष).
4.3.17: After प्रावृष्, in the remaining senses, add **एण्य** instead of अण् (प्रावृष् → प्रावृषेण्य).
4.3.18: After वर्षा, in the remaining senses, add **ठक्** instead of अण् (वर्षा → वार्षिक).
4.3.19: In the **छन्दस्**, after वर्षा, in the remaining senses, add **ठञ्** instead of ठक्; the form matches, only the accent differs (वर्षा → वार्षिक).
4.3.20: In the **छन्दस्**, after वसन्त, in the remaining senses, add **ठञ्** instead of अण् (वसन्त → वासन्तिक).
4.3.21: In the **छन्दस्**, after हेमन्त, in the remaining senses, add **ठञ्** instead of अण् (हेमन्त → हैमन्तिक).
4.3.22: After हेमन्त, everywhere (छन्दस् and ordinary), add **अण्** and drop the त of हेमन्त (हेमन्त → हैमन).
4.3.23: After सायं, चिरम्, प्राह्णे, प्रगे, and after indeclinables denoting time, add **ट्यु** and **ट्युल्**, each with the augment तुट् (सायं → सायंतन, दिवा → दिवातन).
4.3.24: After पूर्वाह्ण and अपराह्ण, **ट्यु** and **ट्युल्** with augment तुट् are optional; otherwise ठञ् applies (पूर्वाह्ण → पूर्वाह्णेतन / पौर्वाह्णिक).
4.3.25: After a word in the locative meaning 'born, grown, or originated there or then', add the appropriate **प्रत्यय** taught above and below (स्रुघ्ने जातः → स्रौघ्न).
4.3.26: After प्रावृष् in the locative meaning 'born there', add **ठप्** instead of एण्य (प्रावृषि जातः → प्रावृषिक).
4.3.27: After शरद् in the locative meaning 'born there', when the whole word is a name, add **वुञ्** instead of अण् (शरद् → शारदक).
4.3.28: After पूर्वाह्ण, अपराह्ण, आर्द्रा, मूला, प्रदोष, and अवस्कर, meaning 'born there', when the whole word is a name, add **वुन्** (आर्द्रा → आर्द्रक).
4.3.29: After पथ् meaning 'born there', add **वुन्** instead of अण्, and पथ् becomes पन्थ (पथि जातः → पन्थक).
4.3.30: After अमावास्या meaning 'born there', **वुन्** is optional instead of अण् (अमावास्या → अमावास्यक / आमावास्य).
4.3.31: After अमावास्या meaning 'born there', also add the **प्रत्यय** अ, alongside the वुन् and अण् already available (अमावास्या → अमावास्य).
4.3.32: After सिन्धु and अपकर meaning 'born there', add **कन्**, blocking अण् and वुञ् (सिन्धु → सिन्धुक, अपकर → अपकरक).
4.3.33: After सिन्धु and अपकर meaning 'born there', add **अण्** and **अञ्** respectively (सिन्धु → सैन्धव, अपकर → आपकर).
4.3.34: After the asterism words श्रविष्ठा, फल्गुनी, अनुराधा, स्वाति, तिष्य, पुनर्वसु, हस्त, विशाखा, अषाढा, and बहुला, the 'born there' **प्रत्यय** drops by **लुक्** (श्रविष्ठासु जातः → श्रविष्ठ).
4.3.35: After a word ending in स्थान, and after गोशाल and खरशाल, the 'born there' **प्रत्यय** drops by **लुक्** (गोस्थाने जातः → गोस्थान).
4.3.36: After वत्सशाला, अभिजित्, अश्वयुक्, and शतभिष्, the 'born there' **प्रत्यय** optionally drops by **लुक्** (अभिजित् → अभिजित् / आभिजित).
4.3.37: After an asterism, the 'born there' **प्रत्यय** drops by **लुक्** variably (रोहिण → रोहिण / रौहिण).
4.3.38: After a word in the locative meaning 'done there', 'obtained there', 'bought there', or 'skilled there', add the appropriate **प्रत्यय** taught above (स्रुघ्ने कृतः → स्रौघ्न).
4.3.39: After a word in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** (the same one already specified for that base) marks the sense "generally found there."
4.3.40: After उपजानु, उपकरण, उपनीवि in the locative, **ठक्** marks the sense "mostly found there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.41: After a **प्रातिपदिक** or ङी/आप्-ending word in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "suited to it" (संभूत here is adequacy, not origin or existence).
4.3.42: After कोश and the rest, **ढञ्** marks the sense "suited to it" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.43: After a word for time in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "good there," "flowering there," or "ripening there."
4.3.44: After a word for time in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** also marks the sense "sown then."
4.3.45: After आश्वयुजी, **वुञ्** marks the sense "sown then" (blocking **ठञ्**).
4.3.46: After ग्रीष्म and वसन्त, **वुञ्** optionally marks the sense "sown then" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.47: After a **प्रातिपदिक** for time in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "due then" — but only when what is due is a debt.
4.3.48: After कलापिन्, अश्वत्थ, यवबुस (each naming a time) in the locative, **वुन्** marks the sense "debt due then."
4.3.49: After ग्रीष्म and अवरसम, **वुञ्** marks the sense "debt due then" (blocking **अण्** and **ठञ्**; this one takes वृद्धि).
4.3.50: After संवत्सरा and अग्रहायणी, **ठञ्** — and also **वुञ्** — marks the sense "debt due then."
4.3.51: After a word for time in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "the beast that wanders (or cries) then," the formed word naming a wild beast.
4.3.52: After a word for time in the nominative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "this is his habit, endured by him" (सोढ here is what one is inured to).
4.3.53: After a word in the locative, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "who stays there" (भव here is presence, not birth; the time-sense from before drops here).
4.3.54: After दिक् and the rest, **यत्** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **अण्** and **छ**).
4.3.55: After a word for a part of the body, **यत्** marks the sense "what stays there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.56: After दृति, कुक्षि, कलशि, वस्ति, अस्ति, अहि, **ढञ्** marks the sense "what stays there."
4.3.57: After ग्रीवा, **अण्** — and also **ढञ्** — marks the sense "what stays there" (blocking **यत्**).
4.3.58: After गम्भीर, **ञ्य** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.59: After an **अव्ययीभाव** (of the परिमुख list), **ञ्य** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.60: After an **अव्ययीभाव** whose prior member is अन्तर्, **ठञ्** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.61: After an **अव्ययीभाव** ending in ग्राम and preceded by परि or अनु, **ठञ्** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.62: After जिह्वामूल and अङ्गुलि, **छ** marks the sense "who stays there" (blocking **यत्**).
4.3.63: After a word ending in वर्ग, **छ** marks the sense "what occurs there" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.64: After a word ending in वर्ग not meaning a letter or word, **यत्** and **ख** optionally mark the sense "who stays there" (**छ** stays available too).
4.3.65: After कर्ण and ललाट, **कन्** marks the sense "what occurs there" when the word names an ornament (blocking **यत्**).
4.3.66: After the name of a thing to be explained, in the genitive, a **प्रत्यय** marks the sense "its commentary" — and, by च, also "what occurs there."
4.3.67: After a polysyllabic name of a thing to be explained with **उदात्त** on its final, **ठञ्** marks the senses "staying there" and "its commentary" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.68: After the name of a work to be explained that concerns a **क्रतु** or a **यज्ञ**, **ठञ्** marks the senses "occurring there" and "its commentary" (blocking **अण्**).
4.3.69: After the name of a work named for a **ऋषि** (a work whose author is a Rishi from the Pravara list), **ठञ्** comes in the senses 'occurring therein' or 'commentary thereon' — only when the result names an अध्याय (chapter).
4.3.70: After पौरोडाश and पुरोडाश, **ष्ठन्** comes in the senses 'occurring therein' or 'commentary thereon'; the ष marks the feminine in **ङीष्**.
4.3.71: After छन्दस्, **यत्** and **अण्** come in the senses 'occurring therein' or 'commentary thereon'.
4.3.72: After a two-syllable word, a word ending in short ऋ, and ब्राह्मण, ऋक्, प्रथम, पुरश्चरण, नाम, आख्यात, नामाख्यात (names of explainable works), **ठक्** comes in the senses 'occurring therein' or 'commentary thereon'.
4.3.73: After ऋगयन and the rest, **अण्** comes in the senses 'occurring therein' or 'commentary thereon'; naming **अण्** again here blocks every later **अपवाद** from applying to these words.
4.3.74: After a stem in the ablative, the affix already specified (**प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण्** and the rest) comes in the sense 'what has come from there'.
4.3.75: After a word naming a source of revenue (आयस्थान), **ठक्** comes in the sense 'come from there'.
4.3.76: After शुण्डिक and the rest, **अण्** comes in the sense 'come from there'; naming **अण्** again blocks later अपवाद affixes for these words.
4.3.77: After a word naming someone connected through learning (teacher, pupil) or through blood (विद्यायोनिसम्बन्ध), **वुञ्** comes in the sense 'come from there'.
4.3.78: After a word ending in short ऋ that names someone connected through learning or blood, **ठञ्** comes in the sense 'come from there'; the त् in ऋत् is only for easy pronunciation.
4.3.79: After पितृ, **यत्** and **ठञ्** come in the sense 'come from there'.
4.3.80: After a stem ending in a **गोत्र** (descendant-denoting) affix, the affix in the sense 'come from there' is the same one that marks 'his मark' — that is, **वुञ्** of 4.3.126.
4.3.81: After a word denoting a cause (हेतु) or a man viewed as a cause, **रूप्य** optionally comes in the sense 'originating from that'.
4.3.82: After a word denoting a cause or a man viewed as a cause, **मयट्** also comes in the sense 'come from there'; the ट् marks the feminine in **ङीप्**.
4.3.83: After a stem in the ablative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'what appears for the first time there' (its source unknown).
4.3.84: After विदुर, **ञ्य** comes in the sense 'what appears for the first time there'.
4.3.85: After a word in the accusative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'what goes to that' — when the thing going is a road or a messenger.
4.3.86: After a word in the accusative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'what faces toward that' — when the thing is a door.
4.3.87: After a word in the accusative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'made about that subject' — when the thing made is a book.
4.3.88: After शिशुक्रन्द, यमसभ, a **द्वन्द्व** compound, and इन्द्रजनन and the rest (in the accusative), **छ** comes in the sense 'a book made about that subject'.
4.3.89: After a word in the nominative naming a dwelling-place, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'this is his निवास (where he now lives)'.
4.3.90: After a word in the nominative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'this is his अभिजन (where his ancestors lived)'.
4.3.91: After a word denoting a mountain, **छ** comes in the sense 'this is his ancestral land' — when the person lives by arms (आयुधजीवी).
4.3.92: After शण्डिक and the rest, **ञ्य** comes in the sense 'this is his ancestral land'.
4.3.93: After सिन्धु and the rest, **अण्**; after तक्षशिला and the rest, **अञ्** — each in the sense 'this is his ancestral land'.
4.3.94: After तूदी, शलातुर, वर्मती, कूचवार come respectively **ढक्**, **छण्**, **ढञ्**, **यक्** in the sense 'this is his ancestral land'.
4.3.95: After a word in the nominative, the affix already specified comes in the sense 'this is his भक्ति (object of devotion or love)'.
4.3.96: After a word denoting an unconscious thing that is not a country or a time, **ठक्** comes in the sense 'this is his object of devotion or love'.
4.3.97: After महाराज, **ठञ्** comes in the sense 'this is his object of veneration'; it differs from the previous **ठक्** only in accent.
4.3.98: After वासुदेव and अर्जुन, **वुन्** comes in the sense 'this is his object of veneration'; here वासुदेव names God, not a Kshatriya.
4.3.99: After a **गोत्र** word or the name of a known क्षत्रिय, in the sense 'this is his object of veneration', the **तद्धित** is **वुञ्** — applied variably (**बहुलम्**: it sometimes fails to apply).
4.3.100: For words naming क्षत्रिय princes that in the plural have the same form as their जनपद (country), the base and **तद्धित** in the sense 'this is his object of veneration' are exactly those of the जनपद word.
4.3.101: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is the one already fixed by **प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण्** and the rules following it.
4.3.102: After तित्तिरि, वरतन्तु, खण्डिक, उख, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **छण्**.
4.3.103: After काश्यप and कौशिक as names of ऋषि-s, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **णिनि**.
4.3.104: After words naming the direct pupils of कलापि and वैशम्पायन, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **णिनि**.
4.3.105: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **णिनि** when the work enounced is a ब्राह्मण or a कल्प spoken by an ancient (पुराण) sage.
4.3.106: After शौनक and the rest, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **णिनि** when what is enounced is छन्दस्.
4.3.107: After कठ and चरक, the 'enounced by him' **तद्धित** drops by **लुक्**.
4.3.108: After कलापि, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **अण्**.
4.3.109: After छगलिन्, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **ढिनुक्**.
4.3.110: After पाराशर्य and शिलालिन्, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **णिनि** — for the भिक्षु-sūtra and the नट-sūtra respectively.
4.3.111: After कर्मन्द and कृशाश्व, in the sense 'enounced by him', the **तद्धित** is **इनि** — for the भिक्षु-sūtra and the नट-sūtra respectively.
4.3.112: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'lying in the same direction as that', the **तद्धित** is the one fixed by **प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण्** and the rules following it.
4.3.113: In the sense 'lying in the same direction as that', the **तद्धित** **तसि** is also added.
4.3.114: After उरस्, in the sense 'lying in the same direction as that', the **तद्धित**s are **यत्** and **तसि**.
4.3.115: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'discovered by him' (known without being taught), the **तद्धित** is the one already fixed by the earlier rules.
4.3.116: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'made by him', the **तद्धित** is the one already fixed — when the thing made is a book.
4.3.117: After a word in the third (instrumental) case, in the sense 'made by him', the **तद्धित** is the one already fixed — when the whole word is a name (**संज्ञा**).
4.3.118: After कुलाल and the rest, in the sense 'made by him', the **तद्धित** is **वुञ्** — when the whole word is a name (**संज्ञा**).
4.3.119: After क्षुद्रा, भ्रमर, वटर, पादप, in the sense 'made by him', the **तद्धित** is **अञ्** — when the whole word is a name (**संज्ञा**).
4.3.120: After a word in the sixth (genitive) case, in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is the one fixed by **प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण्** and the rules following it.
4.3.121: After रथ, in the sense 'this is his' (a part of the chariot), the **तद्धित** is **यत्**.
4.3.122: After रथ preceded by a word for a draught-animal (पत्र), in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **अञ्**.
4.3.123: After a word for a draught-animal (पत्र) and after अध्वर्यु and परिषद्, in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **अञ्**.
4.3.124: After हल and सीर, in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **ठक्**.
4.3.125: After a **द्वन्द्व** compound, in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **वुञ्** — when it names mutual enmity or a matrimonial bond.
4.3.126: After a word naming a **गोत्र** or a **चरण** (Vedic school, here its duties and tradition), in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **वुञ्**.
4.3.127: After a **गोत्र** word ending in **अञ्**, **यञ्**, or **इञ्**, in the sense 'this is his', the **तद्धित** is **अण्** — when the word names a congregation (**संघ**), a brand-mark (**अङ्क**), or a distinguishing mark (**लक्षण**).
4.3.128: After शाकल, in the senses congregation, brand-mark, mark (and hamlet), 'this is his', the **तद्धित** **अण्** comes optionally.
4.3.129: After छन्दोग, औक्थिक, याज्ञिक, बह्वृच, and नट, **ञ्य** marks the Law or Tradition belonging to them, blocking **अण्** and **वुञ्**.
4.3.130: **वुञ्** does not come after a family-name when it names a beginner pupil (**दण्डमाणव**) or a live-in pupil (**अन्तेवासिन्**).
4.3.131: After रैवतिक, स्वापिशि, and the rest, **छ** marks 'this is his', blocking **वुञ्**.
4.3.132: After कौपिञ्जल and हास्तिपद, **अण्** marks 'this is his', blocking **वुञ्**.
4.3.133: After आथर्वणिक, **अण्** marks 'this is his', and its penultimate **इक्** drops, blocking **वुञ्**.
4.3.134: In the sense 'a modification of it', an **अण्** (and the **प्रत्यय**s taught onward) comes after a word in the genitive; तस्य is repeated to stop the reach of शेषे, so the शेष-**प्रत्यय**s घ, ख and the like never carry this sense.
4.3.135: After a word naming an animal, a herb, or a tree, the **प्रत्यय** also marks 'this is a part of it', alongside 'a modification of it'.
4.3.136: After बिल्व, व्रीहि, and the rest, **अण्** marks its modification or part, blocking **अञ्** and **मयट्**.
4.3.137: After a word with क् as its penultimate, **अण्** marks its modification or part, blocking **अञ्**.
4.3.138: After त्रपु and जतु, **अण्** with the augment **षुक्** marks its modification, blocking **अञ्**.
4.3.139: After a word ending in उ, **अञ्** marks its modification or part, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.140: After a word with the अनुदात्त on its first syllable, **अञ्** marks its modification or part, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.141: After पलाश, खदिर, शिंशपा, and the rest, **अञ्** optionally marks its modification or part.
4.3.142: After शमी, **ट्लञ्** marks its modification or part, blocking **अञ्**.
4.3.143: In secular language, **मयट्** optionally marks the product or part of any base, except when food or clothing is meant; it also stands in for the special **प्रत्यय**s of these senses.
4.3.144: After **वृद्ध** words and after शर, दर्भ, and the rest, **मयट्** always marks the product or part in secular language, except when food or clothing is meant.
4.3.146: After पिष्ट, **मयट्** always marks its product or part, blocking **अण्**.
4.3.147: After पिष्ट, **कन्** marks the product when the whole word is a **संज्ञा**, blocking **मयट्**.
4.3.149: After तिल and यव, **मयट्** marks the product when the whole word is not a **संज्ञा**.
4.3.150: In the **छन्दस्**, after a two-syllable word **मयट्** marks its product or part.
4.3.151: In the **छन्दस्**, **मयट्** does not come after a two-syllable word containing short उ, nor after वर्ध्र and बिल्व.
4.3.152: After ताल, बार्हिण, इन्द्रालिश, and the rest, **अण्** marks its product or part, blocking **मयट्** and the others.
4.3.153: After a word for gold, **अण्** marks a weight or measure, blocking **मयट्** and the others.
4.3.154: After words naming living beings and after रजत, सीस, लोह, and the rest, **अञ्** marks its product or part, blocking **अण्** and the others.
4.3.155: After a word ending in a **प्रत्यय** marked with **ञ्** that itself meant product or part, **अञ्** again marks its product or part, blocking **मयट्**.
4.3.156: After a word denoting a measure, the **प्रत्यय** for 'its product or part' is the same one that means 'purchased', and behaves the same throughout.
4.3.157: After उष्ट्र, **वुञ्** marks its product or part, blocking **अञ्**.
4.3.158: After उमा and ऊर्णा, **वुञ्** optionally marks its product or part.
4.3.159: After feminine एणी, **ढञ्** optionally marks the product or part — the flesh of a female black deer. (For the masculine एण, only **अञ्** holds.)
4.3.160: After गो and पयस्, **यत्** marks the product or part.
4.3.161: After द्रु too, **यत्** marks the product or part, blocking **अञ्**.
4.3.162: After द्रु meaning a measure, **वय** marks the product, blocking **यत्**.
4.3.163: When the product or part is a fruit, the affix marking it drops by **लुक्**. (A fruit counts as both a product and a part of its tree.)
4.3.164: After प्लक्ष and the rest, **अण्** marks the product or part when it is a fruit, blocking **अञ्**. Because it is specifically taught here, it does not drop.
4.3.165: After जम्बु, **अण्** optionally marks a fruit, blocking **अञ्**. The **अण्** does not drop, but the **अञ्** still drops by [[4.3.163]].
4.3.166: After जम्बु, the fruit-marking affix also optionally drops by **लुप्** — and with **लुप्** the derivative keeps the gender and number of what it names.
4.3.167: After हरीतकी and the rest, the fruit-marking affix drops by **लुप्**, the derivative keeping the gender of what it names.
4.3.168: After कंसीय and परशव्य, **यञ्** and **अञ्** respectively mark the product, and the **छ** and **यत्** that built those words drop by **लुक्**: कंसीय→कांस्य, परशव्य→पारशव.
4.4.1: From here through [[4.4.76]], **ठक्** is the governing affix carried into the senses given in the rules that follow.
4.4.2: After a word in the third case, **ठक्** marks the senses he plays with it, he digs with it, he conquers with it, or it is conquered by it.
4.4.3: After a word in the third case, **ठक्** marks refined by it (made finer or tastier).
4.4.4: After कुलत्थ and after words with a penultimate क्, **अण्** marks refined by it, blocking **ठक्**.
4.4.5: After a word in the third case, **ठक्** marks he crosses the water by it.
4.4.6: After गोपुच्छ, **ठञ्** marks he crosses by it, blocking **ठक्** — the two differ only in accent.
4.4.7: After नौ and after two-syllable bases, **ठन्** marks he crosses by it, blocking **ठक्**.
4.4.8: After a word in the third case, **ठक्** marks he gets on by it (lives, feeds, travels by it).
4.4.9: After आकर्ष, **ष्ठल्** marks he gets on by it, blocking **ठक्**. The ल् sets the accent; the ष् takes the feminine **ङीष्**.
4.4.10: After पर्प and the rest, **ष्ठन्** marks he gets on by it, blocking **ठक्**. The न् sets the accent; the ष् takes the feminine **ङीष्**.
4.4.11: After श्वगण, **ठञ्** — and by च also **ष्ठन्** — marks he gets on by it, blocking **ठक्**.
4.4.12: After वेतन and the rest in the third case, **ठक्** marks he lives by it.
4.4.13: After वस्न, क्रय, and विक्रय in the third case, **ठन्** marks he lives by it, blocking **ठक्**.
4.4.14: After आयुध, **छ** — and by च also **ठन्** — marks he lives by it.
4.4.15: After उत्सङ्ग and the rest in the third case, **ठक्** marks he carries it (takes it to another place).
4.4.16: After भस्त्रा and the rest in the third case, **ष्ठन्** marks he carries by it. The ष् takes the feminine **ङीष्**.
4.4.17: After विवध and वीवध in the third case, **ष्ठन्** optionally marks he carries by it; otherwise the governing **ठक्** holds.
4.4.18: After कुटिलिका in the third case, **अण्** marks he carries by it.
4.4.19: After अक्षद्यूत and the rest in the third case, **ठक्** marks completed by it.
4.4.20: After a word ending in the affix **त्रि** (the **क्त्रि** of [[3.3.88]]), **मप्** always follows, in the sense completed by it: पक्त्रिम, उप्त्रिम, कृत्रिम. A **क्त्रि**-word never stands alone — **मप्** is fixed to it.
4.4.21: After अपमित्य and याचित, in the sense of completion, add **कक्** and **कन्** respectively (अपमित्य → आपमित्यकम्, याचित → याचितकम्).
4.4.22: After a third-case word, in the sense 'mixed with it', add **ठक्** (दध्ना संसृष्टम् → दाधिकम्).
4.4.23: After चूर्ण, in the sense 'mixed with it', add **इनि**, blocking **ठक्** (चूर्णिनः).
4.4.24: After लवण, the **ठक्** of 'mixed with it' drops by **लुक्** (लवणः सूपः). This holds when लवण names the substance, not when it qualifies.
4.4.25: After मुद्ग, in the sense 'mixed with it', add **अण्**, blocking **ठक्** (मौद्ग ओदनः).
4.4.26: After a third-case word naming a condiment, in the sense 'sprinkled with it', add **ठक्** (दध्ना उपसिक्तम् → दाधिकम्). A condiment word only — not उदकेन उपसिक्तम्.
4.4.27: After the third-case words ओजस्, सहस्, अम्भस्, in the sense 'lives by it', add **ठक्** (ओजसा वर्तते → औजसिकः).
4.4.28: After ईप, लोम, कूल preceded by प्रति or अनु, in the second case, in the sense 'lives by it', add **ठक्** (प्रतीपं वर्तते → प्रातीपिकः, अनुलोमं → आनुलोमिकः).
4.4.29: After परिमुख in the second case, in the sense 'lives by it', also add **ठक्** (परिमुखं वर्तते → पारिमुखिकः). The च extends it to other such words (पारिपार्श्विकः).
4.4.30: After a second-case word, in the sense 'gives it' from a mean motive, add **ठक्** (द्विगुणं प्रयच्छति → द्वैगुणिकः). Only when the motive is mean.
4.4.31: After कुसीद and दशैकादश, in the sense 'gives from a mean motive', add **ष्ठन्** and **ष्ठच्** respectively, blocking **ठक्** (कुसीदिकः, दशैकादशिकः). The two affixes differ only in accent.
4.4.32: After a second-case word, in the sense 'gleans it', add **ठक्** (बदराणि उञ्छति → बादरिकः).
4.4.33: After a second-case word, in the sense 'protects it', add **ठक्** (समाजं रक्षति → सामाजिकः).
4.4.34: After शब्द and दर्दुर in the second case, in the sense 'makes it', add **ठक्** (शब्दं करोति → शाब्दिकः, दर्दुरं → दार्दुरिकः).
4.4.35: After a second-case word naming a bird, fish, or wild beast, in the sense 'kills it', add **ठक्**. It reaches synonyms and species too (पक्षिणं हन्ति → पाक्षिकः, शाकुनिकः, मात्स्यिकः, मार्गिकः).
4.4.36: After परिपन्थ in the second case, in the sense 'waylays it', also add **ठक्** (परिपन्थं तिष्ठति → पारिपन्थिकः). The च carries over 'kills' from before too (परिपन्थं हन्ति → पारिपन्थिकः).
4.4.37: After a word ending in माथ, and after पदवी and अनुपद, in the sense 'runs along it', add **ठक्** (दण्डमाथं धावति → दाण्डमाथिकः, पादविकः, आनुपदिकः). माथ means a road.
4.4.38: After आक्रन्द in the second case, in the sense 'runs to it', add **ठञ्** and, by च, **ठक्** too (आक्रन्दं धावति → आक्रन्दिकः). The two differ only in accent.
4.4.39: After a word ending in पद, in the second case, in the sense 'takes it', add **ठक्** (पूर्वपदं गृह्णाति → पौर्वपदिकः, औत्तरपदिकः).
4.4.40: After प्रतिकण्ठा, अर्थ, and ललाम, in the second case, in the sense 'takes it', add **ठक्** (प्रतिकण्ठं गृह्णाति → प्रातिकण्ठिकः, आर्थिकः, लालामिकः).
4.4.41: After धर्म in the second case, in the sense 'practices it', add **ठक्** (धर्मं चरति → धार्मिकः).
4.4.42: After प्रतिपथ in the second case, in the sense 'goes along it', add **ठन्** and, by च, **ठक्** too (प्रतिपथमेति → प्रतिपथिकः, प्रातिपथिकः). The **ठक्** brings **वृद्धि**, the **ठन्** does not.
4.4.43: After a second-case word meaning a gathering, in the sense 'assembles there', add **ठक्**. The plural समवायान् extends it to synonyms (समवायान् समवैति → सामवायिकः, सामाजिकः, सामूहिकः).
4.4.44: After परिषद्, in the sense 'assembles there', add **ण्य**, blocking **ठक्** (परिषदं समवैति → पारिषद्यः).
4.4.45: After सेना, in the sense 'assembles there', optionally add **ण्य**, with **ठक्** otherwise (सेनां समवैति → सैन्यः or सैनिकः).
4.4.46: After ललाट and कुक्कुटी in the second case, in the sense 'watches it', add **ठक्** when the whole word is a name (ललाटं पश्यति → लालाटिकः, कौक्कुटिकः).
4.4.47: After a sixth-case word, in the sense 'its customary usage', add **ठक्** (शुल्कशालायाः धर्म्यम् → शौल्कशालिकम्, आकरिकम्, आपणिकम्).
4.4.48: After महिषी and the rest, in the sense 'its usage', add **अण्**, blocking **ठक्** (महिष्याः धर्म्यम् → माहिषम्, प्राजावतम्).
4.4.49: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in ऋ, in the sense 'its usage', add **अञ्**, blocking **ठक्** (पोतुः धर्म्यम् → पौत्रम्, औद्गात्रम्).
4.4.50: After a sixth-case word, in the sense 'the tax on it', add **ठक्** (शुल्कशालायाः अवक्रयः → शौल्कशालिकः, आकरिकः). अवक्रय is an exacted tax — distinct from धर्म्य, which is a lawful, religious due.
4.4.51: After a word naming a thing that is sold (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "this is whose **पण्य** (saleable goods)": अपूपाः पण्यमस्य -> आपूपिकः, a cake-seller.
4.4.52: After लवण, **ठञ्** adds in the sense "this is whose **पण्य**", blocking **ठक्**; the two differ only in accent. लवण -> लावणिकः, a salt-seller.
4.4.53: After किशर and the rest (names of perfumes), **ष्ठन्** adds in the sense "this is whose **पण्य**", blocking **ठक्**: किशराः पण्यमस्य -> किशरिकः.
4.4.54: After शलालु (a scent), **ष्ठन्** optionally adds in the sense "this is whose **पण्य**"; otherwise **ठक्** stays. शलालुकः or शालालुकः.
4.4.55: After a word naming a craft (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "this is whose **शिल्प** (craft)": मृदङ्गवादनं शिल्पमस्य -> मार्दङ्गिकः, a drummer.
4.4.56: After मड्डुक and झर्झर, **अण्** optionally adds in the sense "this is whose **शिल्प**", otherwise **ठक्** stays: माड्डुकः or माड्डुकिकः.
4.4.57: After a word naming a weapon (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "this is whose **प्रहरण** (weapon)": असिः प्रहरणमस्य -> आसिकः, a swordsman.
4.4.58: After परश्वध (an axe), both **ठञ्** and **ठक्** add in the sense "this is whose **प्रहरण**"; they differ only in accent. -> पारश्वधिकः.
4.4.59: After शक्ति and यष्टि, **ईकक्** adds in the sense "this is whose **प्रहरण**", blocking **ठक्**: शाक्तीकः, याष्टीकः.
4.4.60: After अस्ति, नास्ति, and दिष्ट (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "this is whose **मति** (belief)": आस्तिकः (believes the hereafter is), नास्तिकः (believes it is not), दैष्टिकः (believes in fate).
4.4.61: After a word (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "whose **शील** (habit) is this": अपूपभक्षणं शीलमस्य -> आपूपिकः, one whose habit is to eat cakes.
4.4.62: After छत्र and the rest, **ण** adds in the sense "whose **शील** is this", blocking **ठक्**: छत्रं शीलमस्य -> छात्रः, a pupil. (स्था in the list is taken with an उपसर्ग: आस्था, संस्था, अवस्था.)
4.4.63: After a word naming the act (first case) that is the **कर्म** done in recitation, **ठक्** adds in the sense "this is his act done in study": एकमन्यदध्ययने कर्म वृत्तमस्य -> ऐकान्यिकः, one who makes one mistake while reciting.
4.4.64: After a compound whose prior member has many vowels, **ठच्** adds in the sense "this is his act done in study", blocking **ठक्**: द्वादशान्यानि कर्माणि अध्ययने वृत्तानि अस्य -> द्वादशान्यिकः, one who makes twelve mistakes.
4.4.65: After a word naming food (first case), **ठक्** adds in the sense "this **भक्ष** (food) is wholesome for whom": अपूपभक्षणं हितमस्मै -> आपूपिकः, one for whom cakes are good food. (The sense takes the dative although अस्य is genitive.)
4.4.66: After a word naming the thing given (first case), **ठक्** adds in the dative sense "this is rightfully given to whom" (दीयते नियुक्तम् = given by fixed appointment): अग्रे भोजनमस्मै नियुक्तं दीयते -> आग्रभोजनिकः.
4.4.67: After श्राणा and मांसौदन, **टिठन्** adds in the sense "this is rightfully given to whom", blocking **ठक्**: श्राणिकः, मांसौदनिकः. (The ट् marks the feminine in ङीप्; the इ is just for pronouncing the affix.)
4.4.68: After भक्त, **अण्** optionally adds in the sense "this is rightfully given to whom", otherwise **ठक्** stays: भाक्तः or भाक्तिकः.
4.4.69: After a word in the locative (तत्र), **ठक्** adds in the sense "appointed there": शुल्कशालायां नियुक्तः -> शौल्कशालिकः, a customs-house officer.
4.4.70: After a word ending in अगार, **ठन्** adds in the sense "appointed there", blocking **ठक्**; they differ in accent and in the absence of **वृद्धि**. देवागारे नियुक्तः -> देवागारिकः.
4.4.71: After a locative word naming a forbidden place or time of study, **ठक्** adds in the sense "who studies there": श्मशानेऽधीते -> श्माशानिकः; चतुर्दश्यामधीते -> चातुर्दशिकः. Only forbidden place or time: not स्रुघ्नेऽधीते, पूर्वाह्णेऽधीते.
4.4.72: After a locative word ending in कठिन, and after प्रस्तार and संस्थान, **ठक्** adds in the sense "who carries on business there": वंशकठिने व्यवहरति -> वांशकठिनिकः; प्रास्तारिकः; सांस्थानिकः.
4.4.73: After the locative word निकट, **ठक्** adds in the sense "who dwells there": निकटे वसति -> नैकटिकः, an ascetic permitted to dwell near a village.
4.4.74: After the locative word आवसथ, **ष्ठल्** adds in the sense "who dwells there": आवसथे वसति -> आवसथिकः, a householder. (The ष् marks the feminine in ङीष्, the ल् is for accent.) This ends the run of **ठक्**.
4.4.75: From here forward to तस्मै हितम् [[5.1.5]], **यत्** is the governing affix carried into each rule.
4.4.76: After रथ, युग, and प्रासङ्ग (second case), **यत्** adds in the sense "what carries it": रथं वहति -> रथ्यः, a carriage-horse; युग्यः; प्रासङ्ग्यः.
4.4.77: After धुर् (second case), both **यत्** and **ढक्** add in the sense "what carries it": धुरं वहति -> धुर्यः or धौरेयः, a beast of burden.
4.4.78: After सर्वधुरा (second case), **ख** adds in the sense "what carries it": सर्वधुरां वहति -> सर्वधुरीणः.
4.4.79: After एकधुरा (second case), **ख** adds in the sense "what carries it", and it optionally drops: एकधुरां वहति -> एकधुरीणः or एकधुरः.
4.4.80: After शकट (second case), **अण्** adds in the sense "what carries it": शकटं वहति -> शाकटः, a draught-ox.
4.4.81: After हल and सीर (accusative), add **ठक्** in the sense "what carries it": हलं वहति → हालिकः, सैरिकः.
4.4.82: After जनी (accusative), add **यत्** in the sense "what carries it", when the whole word is a **संज्ञा**: जनीं वहति → जन्या.
4.4.83: After a word in the accusative, add **यत्** in the sense "what pierces it", provided the piercing is not done with a bow: पादौ विध्यन्ति → पद्याः.
4.4.84: After धन and गण (accusative), add **यत्** in the sense "who obtains it": धनं लब्धा → धन्यः, गण्यः.
4.4.85: After अन्न (accusative), add **ण** in the sense "who obtains it": अन्नं लब्धा → आन्नः.
4.4.86: After वश (accusative), add **यत्** in the sense "gone to": वशं गतः → वश्यः.
4.4.87: After पद (nominative), add **यत्** in the sense "in which it is visible": पदं दृश्यमस्मिन् → पद्यः कर्दमः.
4.4.88: After मूल (nominative), add **यत्** in the sense "whose root is uprooted": मूलमेषामाबर्हि → मूल्याः.
4.4.89: धेनुष्या is formed irregularly as a **संज्ञा**, taking the augment षुक् and the affix य after धेनु, with **उदात्त** on the final.
4.4.90: After गृहपति (instrumental), add **ञ्य** in the sense "joined with it", the whole being a **संज्ञा**: गृहपतिना संयुक्तः → गार्हपत्यः (the अग्नि).
4.4.91: After नौ, वयस्, धर्म, विष, मूल, मूल, सीता, तुला (instrumental), add **यत्** in the respective senses "to be crossed, like, attainable, to be killed, to be bent, equal to, joined with, equally measured": नाव्यम्, वयस्यः, धर्म्यम्, विष्यः, मूल्यम्, मूल्यः, ..., as **संज्ञा**.
4.4.92: After धर्म, पथिन्, अर्थ, न्याय (ablative), add **यत्** in the sense "not departing from it": धर्म्यम्, पथ्यम्, अर्थ्यम्, न्याय्यम्.
4.4.93: After छन्दस् (instrumental), add **यत्** in the sense "made by it", छन्दस् here meaning will or desire: छन्दसा निर्मितः → छन्दस्यः.
4.4.94: After उरस् (instrumental), add **अण्**, and by च also **यत्**, in the sense "made by it", as **संज्ञा**: उरसा निर्मितः → औरसः, उरस्यः (the son).
4.4.95: After हृदय (genitive), add **यत्** in the sense "dear to it", as **संज्ञा**: हृदयस्य प्रियः → हृद्यो देशः.
4.4.96: After हृदय (genitive), add **यत्** in the sense "a binding", when the word names an ऋषि (Vedic hymn): हृदयस्य बन्धनमृषिः → हृद्यः.
4.4.97: After मत, जन, हल (genitive), add **यत्** in the respective senses "means, gossip, drawing": मत्यम्, जन्यः, हल्यः.
4.4.98: After a word in the locative, add **यत्** in the sense "expert in it", साधु here meaning skilled or fit, not beneficial: सामसु साधुः → सामन्यः.
4.4.99: After प्रतिजन etc., add **खञ्** in the sense "expert in it", blocking **यत्**: प्रतिजने साधुः → प्रातिजनीनः.
4.4.100: After भक्त, add **ण** in the sense "good for it", blocking **यत्**: भक्ते साधुः → भाक्तः शालिः.
4.4.101: After परिषद्, add **ण्य** in the sense "expert in it", blocking **यत्**: परिषदि साधुः → पारिषद्यः (and **ण** gives पारिषदः).
4.4.102: After कथा etc., add **ठक्** in the sense "expert in it", blocking **यत्**: कथायां साधुः → काथिकः.
4.4.103: After गुड etc., add **ठञ्** in the sense "good for it", blocking **यत्**: गुडे साधुः → गौडिकः.
4.4.104: After पथिन्, अतिथि, वसति, स्वपति, add **ढञ्** in the sense "good for it", blocking **यत्**: पाथेयम्, आतिथेयम्, वासतेयम्, स्वापतेयम्.
4.4.105: After सभा, add **य** in the sense "fit for it", blocking **यत्** (the two differ only in accent): सभायां साधुः → सभ्यः.
4.4.106: After सभा, add **ढ** in the sense "fit for it" in the **छन्दस्**, blocking **य**: → सभेयः.
4.4.107: After समानतीर्थ (locative), add **यत्** in the sense "who dwells there", तीर्थ here meaning the teacher: समाने तीर्थे वासी → सतीर्थ्यः.
4.4.108: After समानोदर (locative), add **यत्** in the sense "who lies", and the **उदात्त** falls on the ओ: समानोदरे शयितः → समानोदर्यः.
4.4.109: After सोदर (locative), add **य** in the sense "who lies" (समान becomes स), the **उदात्त** falling on the य, not the ओ: → सोदर्यः.
4.4.110: After a word in the locative, add **यत्** in the sense "what occurs there" in the **छन्दस्**, blocking **अण्**, **घ** etc.: मेघ्यः, विद्युत्यः.
4.4.111: In the Vedas, **पाथस्** and **नदी** take **ड्यण्** for 'what stays there'; the **ड** drops their final अस्/ई (पाथसि भवः → पाथ्य, नद्यां भवः → नाद्य). This blocks **यत्**.
4.4.112: In the Vedas, **वेशन्त** and **हिमवत्** take **अण्** for 'what stays there', blocking **यत्**.
4.4.113: In the Vedas, **स्रोतस्** optionally takes **ड्यत्** or **ड्य** for 'what stays there'; the **ड** drops its अस् (स्रोतसि भवः → स्रोत्य). **यत्** stays available as the other option (स्रोतस्य); the two **ड्य** affixes differ only in accent.
4.4.114: **सगर्भ**, **सयूथ**, **सनुत** take **यन्** for 'what stays there', blocking **यत्**; the two differ only in accent.
4.4.115: In the Vedas, **तुग्र** takes **घन्** for 'what stays there', blocking **यत्**.
4.4.116: In the Vedas, **अग्र** takes **यत्** for 'what stays there'. (Stated separately so the next rule's **घच्** and **छ** don't block it.)
4.4.117: In the Vedas, **अग्र** also takes **घच्** and **छ** for 'what stays there'; the **च** carries down **घन्** from before. These differ only in accent.
4.4.118: In the Vedas, **समुद्र** and **अभ्र** take **घ** for 'what stays there', blocking **यत्**.
4.4.119: In the Vedas, after **बर्हिष्** in the locative, **यत्** comes for 'given' (बर्हिषि दत्तम् → बर्हिष्य). Here 'what stays there' no longer carries down.
4.4.120: In the Vedas, after **दूत** in the genitive, **यत्** comes for 'its share' or 'its work' (दूत्य).
4.4.121: In the Vedas, after **रक्षस्** and **यातु** in the genitive, **यत्** comes for 'killer of it' (रक्षस्य, यातव्य) — the thing by which it is killed.
4.4.122: In the Vedas, after **रेवती**, **जगती**, **हविष्य** in the genitive, **यत्** comes for 'praise of it' (रेवत्य, जगत्य, हविष्य).
4.4.123: In the Vedas, after **असुर** in the genitive, **यत्** comes for 'property' (असुर्य), blocking **अण्**.
4.4.124: In the Vedas, after **असुर** in the genitive, **अण्** comes for 'magic, glamour' (आसुर, fem. आसुरी), blocking **यत्**.
4.4.125: In the Vedas, a **मतुप्**-ending stem takes **यत्** when it names the **मन्त्र** with which these bricks are set down (तद्वान् ... उपधानो मन्त्रः), and the **मतुप्** then drops (वर्चस्वत् → वर्चस्य).
4.4.126: In the Vedas, **अश्विमत्** takes **अण्** to name bricks set down with a **मन्त्र** containing अश्विन्; the **मतुप्** drops (आश्विन), blocking **यत्**.
4.4.127: In the Vedas, to name bricks set down with a **मन्त्र** containing वयस्, **मूर्धन्** takes **मतुप्** (मूर्धन्वत्), blocking the **यत्** of 4.4.125 — only when the **मन्त्र** also carries वयस्.
4.4.128: In the Vedas, **यत्** comes with the force of **मतुप्** when the word formed names a month or a body (नभस्य, सहस्य, तपस्य, मधव्य; ओजस्या तनूः), blocking **मतुप्** and the other मत्वर्थ affixes.
4.4.129: In the Vedas, **मधु** takes **ष** (and, by च, **यत्**) with the force of **मतुप्** (माधव, मधव्य; the affix may also drop, giving मधु).
4.4.130: In the Vedas, **ओजस्** takes **यत्** and **ख** with the force of **मतुप्** when 'a day' is meant (ओजस्य, ओजसीन).
4.4.131: In the Vedas, a stem ending in **भग** and beginning with **वेशस्** or **यशस्** takes **थल्** with the force of **मतुप्** (वेशोभग्य, यशोभग्य); the **ल्** sets the accent on the vowel before the affix.
4.4.132: In the Vedas, **वेशोभग** and **यशोभग** also take **ख** with the force of **मतुप्** (वेशोभगीन, यशोभगीन); by च, **यत्** too.
4.4.133: After **पूर्व** ('the forefathers') in the instrumental, **इन्**, **य**, and (by च) **ख** come for 'made by them' (पूर्विन्, पूर्व्य, पूर्वीण).
4.4.134: In the Vedas, after **अपस्** (अद्भिस्) in the instrumental, **यत्** comes for 'sanctified' (अप्य).
4.4.135: In the Vedas, after **सहस्र** in the instrumental, **घ** comes for 'equal to it' (सहस्रिय).
4.4.136: In the Vedas, **सहस्र** takes **घ** with the force of **मतुप्** (सहस्रिय), blocking **विनि**, **इनि**, and the **अण्** of 5.2.102-103.
4.4.137: In the Vedas, after **सोम** in the accusative, **य** comes for 'who deserves it' (सौम्य); it differs from **घ** only in accent.
4.4.138: In the Vedas, **सोम** takes **य** with the force of **मयट्** (सोम्य = सोममय); the case in construction follows whichever sense of मयट् applies.
4.4.139: In the Vedas, **मधु** takes **यत्** with the force of **मयट्** (मधव्य = मधुमय).
4.4.140: In the Vedas, **वसु** takes **यत्** for 'a collection' (वसव्य = समूह), and by च also with the force of **मयट्**.
4.4.141: In the **छन्दस्**, **घ** attaches after नक्षत्र without changing its meaning; the **समूह** sense does not carry over here.
4.4.142: In the **छन्दस्**, **तातिल्** attaches after सर्व and देव without changing the meaning.
4.4.143: In the **छन्दस्**, **तातिल्** attaches after शिव, शम्, and अरिष्ट in the genitive when the sense is 'does' (कर).
4.4.144: In the **छन्दस्**, **तातिल्** also attaches after शिव, शम्, and अरिष्ट in the genitive when the sense is **भाव** (the state of being that thing).
5.1.1: From here up to तेन कृतम् [[5.1.37]], the senses being specified govern the affix **छ**.
5.1.2: **यत्** attaches after a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in उ (short or long) and after गो and the rest, in the **छ** senses; it blocks **छ**.
5.1.3: **यत्** attaches after कम्बल in the **छ** senses when a name is meant, blocking **छ**.
5.1.4: **यत्** attaches optionally after words for an offering (**हविस्**) and after the अपूप list, in the **छ** senses.
5.1.5: After a word in the fourth case, the affix attaches in the sense 'good for that' (तस्मै हितम्).
5.1.6: **यत्** attaches after a word for a part of the body in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**.
5.1.7: **यत्** attaches after खल, यव, माष, तिल, वृष, and ब्रह्मन् in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**; च extends it to a few others.
5.1.8: **थ्यन्** attaches after अज and अवि in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**.
5.1.9: **ख** attaches after आत्मन्, विश्वजन, and compounds ending in भोग, in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**.
5.1.10: **ण** attaches after सर्व and **ढञ्** after पुरुष, in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**.
5.1.11: **खञ्** attaches after माणव and चरक in the sense 'good for that', blocking **छ**.
5.1.12: After a word naming a product (विकृति), the affix attaches to mean the raw material (प्रकृति) that serves for making that product, and nothing else.
5.1.13: **ढञ्** attaches after छदिस्, उपधि, and बलि in the sense of the material serving for that product, blocking **छ**.
5.1.14: **ञ्य** attaches after ऋषभ and उपानह् in the sense of the material serving for that product, blocking **छ**.
5.1.15: **अञ्** attaches after a word naming a leather product, in the sense of the leather serving for that product, blocking **छ**.
5.1.16: After a word in the first case, the same affixes attach with genitive or locative force, in the senses 'this is enough for that' (तद् अस्य स्यात्) and 'this is enough to make in here' (तद् अस्मिन् स्यात्).
5.1.17: **ढञ्** attaches after परिखा in those 'enough for that / enough therein' senses, blocking **छ**; here the rule of **छ** and **यत्** ends.
5.1.18: From here up to [[5.1.115]] (excluding it), the senses being specified govern the affix **ठञ्**.
5.1.19: From here up to तदर्हति [[5.1.63]] inclusive, the affix is **ठक्** — except after गोपुच्छ, a **संख्या**, or a **परिमाण** (measure).
5.1.20: **ठक्** attaches after निष्क and the rest when they stand outside a compound, in the **ठक्** senses, blocking **ठञ्**.
5.1.21: **ठन्** and **यत्** attach after शत when it stands outside a compound and does not mean just 'a hundred', in the **ठक्** senses, blocking **कन्**.
5.1.22: **कन्** attaches after a **संख्या** that does not end in ति or शत्, in the **ठक्** senses, blocking **ठञ्**.
5.1.23: After a **संख्या** ending in वत्, **कन्** optionally takes the augment **इट्**.
5.1.24: **ड्वुन्** attaches after विंशति and त्रिंशत् when no name is meant, in the **ठक्** senses; the ति and अत् drop.
5.1.25: **टिठन्** attaches after कंस in the **ठक्** senses, blocking **ठञ्** (the टि gives the feminine **ङीप्**).
5.1.26: **अञ्** attaches optionally after शूर्प in the **ठक्** senses, with **ठञ्** as the alternative.
5.1.27: After शतमान, विंशतिक, सहस्र, and वसन, the senses through [[5.1.63]] take **अण्**, blocking ठञ्, ठक्, and कन्.
5.1.28: After a stem beginning with अध्यर्ध and after a **द्विगु**, the आर्हीय affix (the senses through [[5.1.63]]) drops by **लुक्**, except in a name.
5.1.29: After कार्षापण and सहस्र (preceded by अध्यर्ध or a numeral, forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय affix optionally drops by **लुक्**, where the previous rule made the dropping fixed.
5.1.30: After निष्क preceded by द्वि or त्रि (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय affix optionally drops by **लुक्**.
5.1.31: After बिस्त preceded by द्वि or त्रि (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय affix optionally drops by **लुक्**.
5.1.32: After विंशतिक preceded by अध्यर्ध or a numeral (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय senses take **ख** (ईन).
5.1.33: After खारी preceded by अध्यर्ध or a numeral (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय senses take **ईकन्**.
5.1.34: After पण, पाद, माष, and शत preceded by अध्यर्ध or a numeral (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय senses take **यत्**.
5.1.35: After शाण preceded by अध्यर्ध or a numeral (forming a **द्विगु**), the आर्हीय senses optionally take **यत्**, blocking ठञ्.
5.1.36: After शाण preceded by द्वि or त्रि, the आर्हीय senses take **अण्**, and by च also **यत्**.
5.1.37: The thirteen affixes of [[5.1.18]]–[[5.1.36]] mean 'bought for this price', added to a word in the third case.
5.1.38: Those same affixes also mean 'the occasion for it', added to a word in the sixth case, when the thing is a **संयोग** (a connection) or an **उत्पात** (a portent).
5.1.39: After गो and after a two-syllable stem—but not a numeral, a measure of capacity, or अश्व etc.—the sense 'occasion of a connection or portent' takes **यत्**, blocking ठञ्.
5.1.40: After पुत्र, the same sense takes **छ** (ईय) as well as **यत्**.
5.1.41: In the same sense of 'occasion of a connection or portent', सर्वभूमि takes **अण्** and पृथिवी takes **अञ्**, respectively, blocking ठक्.
5.1.42: सर्वभूमि takes **अण्** and पृथिवी takes **अञ्**, in the sense 'lord of it', the word being in the sixth case.
5.1.43: सर्वभूमि takes **अण्** and पृथिवी takes **अञ्**, in the sense 'known in it', the word being in the seventh case.
5.1.44: After लोक and सर्वलोक, in the seventh case, the sense 'known in it' takes **ठञ्**.
5.1.45: The above affixes also mean 'sown with this much' (a field), added to a word in the sixth case.
5.1.46: After पात्र, the sense 'sown with this much' takes **ष्ठन्** (इक), blocking ठञ्.
5.1.47: The above affixes also mean 'on this, an interest, rent, profit, tax, or bribe is given', added to a word in the first case, the affix carrying a locative sense.
5.1.48: After an ordinal and after अर्ध, that same sense takes **ठञ्**, blocking ठक् and टिठन्.
5.1.49: After भाग, that same sense takes **यत्**, and by च also ठन्, blocking ठञ्.
5.1.50: After भार preceded by वंश etc., in the second case, the above affixes mean 'who carries off, conveys, or brings it'.
5.1.51: After वसन and द्रव्य, in the second case, the senses 'who carries etc.' take **ठन्** (इक) and **कन्** (क), respectively.
5.1.52: The above affixes also mean 'what holds, takes away, or cooks this much', added to a word in the second case.
5.1.53: After आढक, आचित, and पात्र, that same sense optionally takes **ख** (ईन), blocking ठञ्.
5.1.54: After आढक, आचित, and पात्र final in a **द्विगु**, that sense optionally takes **ष्ठन्** (इक), and by च also **ख**; neither drops by [[5.1.28]].
5.1.55: After कुलिज final in a **द्विगु**, that sense optionally drops the affix by **लुक्** or takes **ख** (ईन), and by च also **ष्ठन्**.
5.1.56: The affixes taught from [[5.1.18]] also mean 'this is his share, price, or wages', added to a word in the first case, the affix carrying a sixth-case sense.
5.1.57: The affixes of प्राग्वतेष्ठञ् [[5.1.18]] onward also take the sense 'this is its measure'; the measuring word stands in the nominative.
5.1.58: After a numeral word, those affixes take the sense 'this is its measure' when the result names a **संज्ञा**, a **संघ**, a **सूत्र**, or a fixed course of study; in the **संज्ञा** sense the affix adds nothing to the meaning.
5.1.59: पङ्क्ति, विंशति, त्रिंशत्, चत्वारिंशत्, पञ्चाशत्, षष्टि, सप्तति, अशीति, नवति, शतम् are formed irregularly in the sense 'this is its measure'.
5.1.60: With वर्ग, पञ्चत् and दशत् are formed irregularly (with डति) in the sense 'this is its measure'; optionally कन् applies instead.
5.1.61: In the **छन्दस्**, सप्तन् takes अञ् in the sense 'this is its measure' when a वर्ग is meant.
5.1.62: त्रिंशत् and चत्वारिंशत् take डण् in the sense 'this is its measure' when the word names a ब्राह्मण-book.
5.1.63: The affixes of प्राग्वतेष्ठञ् [[5.1.18]] onward also take the sense 'who deserves that'; the deserved thing stands in the accusative.
5.1.64: After छेद and the rest, in the accusative, those affixes always take the sense 'who deserves that without exception'.
5.1.65: After शीर्षच्छेद in the accusative, यत् takes the sense 'who deserves that without exception', and so do the affixes above.
5.1.66: After दण्ड and the rest, in the accusative, य takes the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठक्.
5.1.67: In the **छन्दस्**, any **प्रातिपदिक** takes यत् in the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठञ् and the rest.
5.1.68: After पात्र, घञ् and यत् take the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठक् and ठञ्.
5.1.69: After कडङ्गर and दक्षिणा, छ and यत् take the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठक्.
5.1.70: After स्थालीबिल, छ and यत् take the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठक्.
5.1.71: यज्ञ takes घ and ऋत्विज् takes खञ्, respectively, in the sense 'who deserves that', blocking ठक्.
5.1.72: After पारायण, तुरायण, चान्द्रायण in the accusative, ठञ् takes the sense 'who performs this'.
5.1.73: After संशय in the accusative, ठञ् takes the sense 'fallen into this'.
5.1.74: After योजन in the accusative, ठञ् takes the sense 'who goes that far'.
5.1.75: After पथिन् in the accusative, ष्कन् takes the sense 'who travels it' (ष् brings the feminine ङीष्, न् sets the accent).
5.1.76: पथिन् becomes पन्थ and takes ण in the sense 'who always travels it'.
5.1.77: After उत्तरपथ in the instrumental, ठञ् takes the senses 'conveyed by that road' and 'who travels by it'.
5.1.78: Through the following rules (up to [[5.1.96]]), supply 'after a word for time'.
5.1.79: After a time-word in the instrumental, ठञ् takes the sense 'accomplished in that time'.
5.1.80: After a time-word in the accusative, the affixes above take the senses 'solicited (to serve unpaid) for that span', 'hired for it', 'lasting through it', and 'going to last through it'.
5.1.81: After मास, denoting age, यत् and खञ् apply, blocking ठञ् (supply 'lasting through it').
5.1.82: After a **द्विगु** ending in मास, denoting age, यप् applies.
5.1.83: After षण्मास, denoting age, ण्यत्, यप्, and ठञ् apply.
5.1.84: After षण्मास, when age is not meant, ठन् applies, and ण्यत् as well.
5.1.85: After समा, ख takes the senses 'solicited', 'hired', 'lasting', and 'going to last', blocking ठञ्.
5.1.86: After a **द्विगु** ending in समा, ख applies optionally in those senses; otherwise ठञ् applies.
5.1.87: After रात्री, अहन्, सम्वत्सर ending a **द्विगु**, the affix ख comes optionally in the senses from [[5.1.79]] onward; otherwise ठञ्.
5.1.88: After a **द्विगु** ending in वर्षा, ख and ठञ् come in those same senses, and either affix may also drop, giving three forms.
5.1.89: After a **द्विगु** ending in वर्षा, the affix drops obligatorily when the word refers to something endowed with reason.
5.1.90: षष्टिकाः is formed irregularly: कन् after षष्टिरात्रि (3rd case), with रात्रि dropping, in the sense 'what ripens in sixty nights' — a name for a kind of barley.
5.1.91: In the **छन्दस्**, after a stem ending in वत्सर, the affix छ comes in the fivefold senses from [[5.1.76]] onward, blocking ठञ्.
5.1.92: In the **छन्दस्**, after वत्सर preceded by सम् or परि, both ख and छ come in those fivefold senses.
5.1.93: After a time word (3rd case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'subdued, gained, accomplished, or easily accomplished in that time'.
5.1.94: After a time word, ठञ् comes in the sense 'an abstinence (**ब्रह्मचर्य**) lasting that long' — or 'who keeps abstinence that long'.
5.1.95: After a word naming a sacrifice (6th case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'the fee (दक्षिणा) for it'.
5.1.96: After a time word (7th case), the affixes that mean **भव** (from [[4.3.53]], [[4.3.11]]) also come in the sense 'given in that' and 'done in that'; वत् makes all the तत्रभवः rules apply here.
5.1.97: After व्युष्ट and the rest (7th case), अण् comes in the sense 'given therein or done therein'.
5.1.98: After यथाकथाच and हस्त (3rd case), ण and यत् come respectively, in the sense 'given or done in this way' — and यथासंख्य does not split दीयते and कार्य between them.
5.1.99: After a word (3rd case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'fit for that'.
5.1.100: After कर्म and वेष (3rd case), यत् comes in the sense 'fit for that', blocking ठञ्.
5.1.101: After संताप and the rest (4th case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'able to effect that'.
5.1.102: After योग, यत् also comes in the sense 'able to effect that', alongside ठञ्.
5.1.103: After कर्मन्, उकञ् comes in the sense 'able to effect that', blocking ठञ्.
5.1.104: After समय (1st case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'that for which it has arrived'.
5.1.105: After ऋतु (1st case), अण् comes in the sense 'that for which it has come'.
5.1.106: In the **छन्दस्**, after ऋतु, घस् comes in the sense 'that for which the season has come', blocking अण्.
5.1.107: After काल (1st case), यत् comes in the sense 'that for which the time has come'.
5.1.108: After काल (1st case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'long-standing'.
5.1.109: After a word (1st case), ठञ् comes in the sense 'that whose purpose is this'.
5.1.110: After विशाखा and आषाढ (1st case), अण् comes in the sense 'that whose purpose is this' — विशाखा paired with मन्थ, आषाढ with दण्ड.
5.1.111: After अनुप्रवचन and the rest, छ comes in the sense 'that whose purpose is this', blocking ठञ्.
5.1.112: After समापन with a word preceding it in compound, छ comes in the sense 'that whose purpose is this', blocking ठञ्.
5.1.113: ऐकागारिकट् is formed irregularly in the sense 'thief'; the ट् restricts it to ङीप् in the feminine.
5.1.114: आकालिकट् is formed irregularly in the sense 'what coincides with its beginning and end' — what lasts only an instant; आकाल replaces समानकाल.
5.1.115: After a word (3rd case), वति comes in the sense 'like that', when the likeness is one of action.
5.1.116: After a word in the 7th or 6th case, वति comes in the sense 'like what is therein' or 'like that of it'.
5.1.117: **वति** (वत्) attaches to a word in the accusative meaning "befitting that": राजानम् अर्हति → राजवत्.
5.1.118: In the **छन्दस्**, **वति** (वत्) attaches to an **उपसर्ग** standing for the sense of a verbal root.
5.1.119: **त्व** and **तल्** attach to a genitive word meaning "the nature of that": अश्वस्य भावः → अश्वत्वम् or अश्वता.
