5.1.120: From here through ब्रह्मणस्त्वः [5.1.136], **त्व** and **तल्** stay in force, so they apply alongside every later affix taught for "nature"; and the च adds them to mean **कर्म** as well (from [5.1.124]).
5.1.121: The "nature" affixes taught from here do not attach after a **तत्पुरुष** whose first member is **नञ्** — except after चतुर, संगत, लवण, वट, बुध, कत, रस, लस.
5.1.122: After पृथु, मृदु, महत्, पटु and the rest of the पृथु-group, **इमनिच्** (इमन्) optionally marks "the nature of that": पृथु → प्रथिमा (the option lets अण् etc. apply too).
5.1.123: After a word naming a colour, and after दृढ, वृढ, भृश and the rest of the दृढ-group, **ष्यञ्** marks "the nature of that" — and by the च, **इमनिच्** too: शुक्ल → शौक्ल्यम्, शुक्लिमा.
5.1.124: After a word naming a quality, and after ब्राह्मण, वाडव, माणव and the rest of the ब्राह्मण-group, **ष्यञ्** marks **कर्म** (the activity or occupation) — and by the च, "nature" too: जड → जाड्यम्.
5.1.125: After स्तेन, **यत्** (य) marks "the nature or activity of that," and the न drops: स्तेन → स्तेयम्.
5.1.126: After सखि, **य** marks "the nature or activity of that": सखि → सख्यम्.
5.1.127: After कपि and ज्ञाति, **ढक्** marks "the nature or activity of that": कपि → कापेयम्, ज्ञाति → ज्ञातेयम्.
5.1.128: After a compound ending in पति, and after पुरोहित and the rest of the पुरोहित-group, **यक्** marks "the nature or activity of that": सेनापति → सैनापत्यम्.
5.1.129: After a word naming a class of animals, after a word naming an age, and after उद्गातृ and the rest of the उद्गातृ-group, **अञ्** marks "the nature or activity of that": अश्व → आश्वम्, कुमार → कौमारम्.
5.1.130: After a compound ending in हायन, and after युवन्, स्थविर and the rest of the युवन्-group, **अण्** marks "the nature or activity of that": द्विहायन → द्वैहायनम्, युवन् → यौवनम्.
5.1.131: After a stem ending in an **इक्** vowel (इ, ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, ऌ) whose preceding syllable is prosodically light, **अण्** marks "the nature or activity of that": शुचि → शौचम्, पटु → पाटवम्.
5.1.132: After a stem of three or more syllables whose penultimate letter is य् and whose penultimate syllable is prosodically heavy, **वुञ्** marks "the nature or activity of that": रमणीय → रामणीयकम्.
5.1.133: After a **द्वन्द्व** compound, and after मनोज्ञ, कल्याण and the rest of the मनोज्ञ-group, **वुञ्** marks "the nature or activity of that": मनोज्ञ → मानोज्ञकम्.
5.1.134: After a **गोत्र** name or the name of a Vedic school, **वुञ्** marks "the nature or activity of that" when one boasts of it, shows contempt by it, or has attained or come to know it.
5.1.135: After a word naming a **होत्रा** priest, **छ** (ईय) marks "the nature or activity of that": अच्छावाक → अच्छावाकीयम्, पोतृ → पोत्रीयम्.
5.1.136: After ब्रह्मन् naming a kind of **होत्रा** priest, **त्व** marks "the nature or activity of that," blocking छ: ब्रह्मन् → ब्रह्मत्वम्.
5.2.1: After the name of a particular grain in the genitive, **खञ्** marks the field where it grows: मुद्ग → मौद्गीनम् क्षेत्रम्.
5.2.2: After व्रीहि and शालि, **ढक्** marks the field where they grow: व्रीहि → व्रैहेयम्, शालि → शालेयम्.
5.2.3: After यव, यवक, षष्टिक, **यत्** marks the field where they grow: यव → यव्यम्.
5.2.4: After तिल, माष, उमा, भङ्गा, अणु, **यत्** optionally marks the field where they grow (otherwise खञ्): तिल → तिल्यम् or तैलीनम्.
5.2.5: After सर्वचर्मन् (instrumental), **ख** (ईन) and **खञ्** mark "wholly made of that": सर्वचर्मन् → सर्वचर्मीणः or सार्वचर्मीणः.
5.2.6: After यथामुख and संमुख in the genitive, **ख** (ईन) marks a mirror — that in which the face is seen: यथामुख → यथामुखीनः, संमुख → संमुखीनः.
5.2.7: After पथिन्, अङ्ग, कर्मन्, पत्र, or पात्र preceded by सर्व (accusative), **ख** (ईन) marks "what pervades the whole of that": सर्वपथ → सर्वपथीनः, सर्वाङ्ग → सर्वाङ्गीणः.
5.2.8: After आप्रपद, **ख** (ईन) marks "reaching up to that": आप्रपद → आप्रपदीनः पटः, cloth reaching to the top of the feet.
5.2.9: After अनुपद, सर्वान्न, अयानय (accusative), **ख** (ईन) marks respectively "bound to that," "eating that," and "carried to that": अनुपद → अनुपदीना, सर्वान्न → सर्वान्नीनः, अयानय → अयानयीनः.
5.2.10: After परोवर, परम्पर, पुत्रपौत्र (accusative), **ख** (ईन) marks "who lives through that": परोवर → परोवरीणः, who lives to see high and low.
5.2.11: After अवारपार, अत्यन्त, अनुकाम (accusative), the **प्रत्यय** ख (ईन) marks "who means to go there": अवारपारीणः.
5.2.12: After समांसमाम् (accusative of time), the **प्रत्यय** ख (ईन) marks "who carries young year after year": समांसमीना गौः.
5.2.13: अद्यश्वीन is the irregular form for a female about to give birth today or tomorrow.
5.2.14: आगवीन is the irregular form for a day-laborer who works until the cows come back, taking ख after आ + गो.
5.2.15: After अनुगु (behind the cows), the **प्रत्यय** ख (ईन) marks "fit to follow": अनुगवीनः, a cowherd.
5.2.16: After अध्वन् (accusative), the **प्रत्यय**s यत् (य) and ख (ईन) mark "fit to travel it": अध्वन्यः, अध्वनीनः.
5.2.17: After अभ्यमित्र (accusative), the **प्रत्यय** छ (ईय) marks "fit to advance on the enemy", and the च adds यत् and ख too: अभ्यमित्रीयः, अभ्यमित्र्यः, अभ्यमित्रीणः.
5.2.18: After गोष्ठ (a cow-pen), the **प्रत्यय** खञ् marks "what used to be one": गौष्ठीनो देशः, a place that was formerly a cow-pen.
5.2.19: After अश्व (genitive), the **प्रत्यय** खञ् marks the distance covered in one day: आश्वीनः.
5.2.20: शालीन (modest) and कौपीन (a shameful act) are the irregular forms, from शाला and कूप, when they carry those senses.
5.2.21: After व्रात (instrumental) — a roving band that lives by bodily labor — the **प्रत्यय** खञ् marks "who lives by it": व्रातीनः.
5.2.22: साप्तपदीन is the irregular form for friendship, from सप्तपद.
5.2.23: हैयंगवीन is the irregular form, as a Name, for fresh butter made from yesterday's milk (ह्यः + गो).
5.2.24: After पील्वादि words (genitive) the **प्रत्यय** कुणप् (कुण) marks their fruiting-season, and after कर्णादि words the **प्रत्यय** जाहच् (जाह) marks their root: पीलुकुणः, कर्णजाहम्.
5.2.25: After पक्ष (genitive), the **प्रत्यय** ति marks its root — only मूल carries over from the previous rule, not पाक: पक्षतिः, the first day of a fortnight.
5.2.26: After a word (instrumental), the **प्रत्यय**s चुञ्चुप् (चुञ्चु) and चणप् (चण) mark "famed through it": विद्याचुञ्चुः, विद्याचणः.
5.2.27: In the sense "not together", the **प्रत्यय** ना follows वि and the **प्रत्यय** नाञ् follows नञ्: विना, नाना.
5.2.28: After वि, the **प्रत्यय**s शालच् (शाल) and शङ्कटच् (शङ्कट) follow without changing the sense: विशाल, विशङ्कट.
5.2.29: After सम्, प्र, उद् — and वि by the च — the **प्रत्यय** कटच् (कट) follows: संकटम्, प्रकटम्, उत्कटम्, विकटम्.
5.2.30: After अव, the **प्रत्यय** कुटारच् (कुटार) follows, and कटच् (कट) by the च: अवकुटारम्, अवकटम्.
5.2.31: After अव, the **प्रत्यय**s टीटच् (टीट), नाटच् (नाट), भ्रटच् (भ्रट) mark a sunken nose, as a Name: अवटीटम्, अवनाटम्, अवभ्रटम्.
5.2.32: After नि, the **प्रत्यय**s बिडच् (बिड) and बिरीसच् (बिरीस) mark a sunken nose, as a Name: निबिडम्, निबिरीसम्.
5.2.33: After नि, the **प्रत्यय**s इनच् (इन) and पिटच् (पिट) mark a sunken nose, and नि becomes चिक् before इनच् and चि before पिटच्: चिकिनः, चिपिटः.
5.2.34: The **प्रत्यय** त्यकन् (त्यक) follows उप in the sense "nearby" and अधि in the sense "risen above", forming Names: उपत्यका, the land at a mountain's foot; अधित्यका, its tableland.
5.2.35: After कर्म (locative), the **प्रत्यय** अठच् (अठ) marks "who throws himself into it": कर्मठः पुरुषः.
5.2.36: After तारकादि words (nominative), the **प्रत्यय** इतच् (इत) marks "that on which this has appeared": तारकितं नभः, a starry sky; पुष्पितो वृक्षः. The तारकादि class is an **आकृतिगण**.
5.2.37: After a word (nominative) naming a height, the **प्रत्यय**s द्वयसच् (द्वयस), दघ्नच् (दघ्न), मात्रच् (मात्र) mark "that whose measure is this": ऊरुद्वयसम्, ऊरुदघ्नम्, ऊरुमात्रम्, reaching as high as the thigh.
5.2.38: After पुरुष and हस्ति (nominative), the **प्रत्यय** अण् marks "that whose measure is this", and the द्वयसच् series too by the च: पौरुषम्, पुरुषद्वयसम्, पुरुषदघ्नम्, पुरुषमात्रम्; हास्तिनम्.
5.2.39: After यद्, तद्, एतद् (nominative), the **प्रत्यय** वतुप् (वत्) marks "that whose volume is this": यावान्, तावान्, एतावान्.
5.2.40: After किम् and इदम्, the घ (इय्) replaces the व् of वतुप्: कियान्, इयान्.
5.2.41: After **किम्** (first case), in the sense of 'how many in number', add **डति** (which is अति, with इम् dropped) and, by च, **वतुप्** — whose व् becomes घ् (giving इयत्).
5.2.42: After a **संख्या**, in the sense 'whose parts are this many', add **तयप्**: पञ्च + तयप् = पञ्चतयम् 'having five parts'.
5.2.43: After द्वि and त्रि, **अयच्** optionally replaces **तयप्**: द्वितयम् or द्वयम्, त्रितयम् or त्रयम्.
5.2.44: After उभ, **अयच्** always replaces **तयप्**, with the **उदात्त** on its first syllable: उभयः, उभये, उभयोः.
5.2.45: After a numeral ending in दशन् (first case), in the sense 'this much is surplus in it', add **ड** (अ, with the stem's अन् dropped): एकादश + शत = एकादशं शतम् 'hundred-and-eleven'. Both numbers must count the same kind of thing, and the it-word must be शत or सहस्र.
5.2.46: In the same 'surplus in it' sense, add **ड** after a numeral ending in शत् and after विंशति (dropping अत् / अति): त्रिंशं शतम्, विंशं शतम् — and, by a वार्त्तिक, after a compound ending in विंशति: एकविंशं शतम्. This holds only for pure numbers.
5.2.47: After a numeral (first case), with genitive force, in the sense that so many **गुण** (parts) of one thing are the निमान (price) of one part of another, add **मयट्** (फेम. **ङीप्**): यवानां द्विमयम् उदश्वित् 'curd-water worth two parts of barley per part'.
5.2.48: After a numeral (genitive), in the sense 'the one that completes this count', add **डट्** (अ, dropping the final vowel and what follows it): एकादशानां पूरणः = एकादशः 'eleventh'. This builds ordinals.
5.2.49: Before **डट्**, a numeral that ends in न् and is not preceded by another numeral takes the augment **मट्**: पञ्चमः 'fifth', सप्तमः.
5.2.50: In the **छन्दस्**, the same न्-ending numeral takes the augment **थट्** before **डट्**, and by च the augment **मट्** as well: पञ्चथः or पञ्चमः, सप्तथः.
5.2.51: Before **डट्**, षट्, कति, कतिपय, and चतुर् take the augment **थुक्**: षष्ठः 'sixth', कतिथः, कतिपयथः, चतुर्थः. (कतिपय is not itself a numeral; this rule gives it **डट्**.)
5.2.52: Before **डट्**, बहु, पूग, गण, and सङ्घ take the augment **तिथुक्**: बहुतिथः, पूगतिथः, गणतिथः, सङ्घतिथः.
5.2.53: Before **डट्**, a stem ending in **वतु** takes the augment **इथुक्**: यावतिथः, तावतिथः, एतावतिथः.
5.2.54: After द्वि, in the 'completer thereof' sense, add **तीय** (blocking **डट्**): द्वितीयः 'second'.
5.2.55: After त्रि, in the same sense, add **तीय** (blocking **डट्**), with **सम्प्रसारण** of the stem: त्रि → तृ, giving तृतीयः 'third'.
5.2.56: After विंशति and the like, **डट्** optionally takes the augment **तमट्** (फेम. **ङीप्**): विंशतितमः or विंशः 'twentieth', एकविंशतितमः or एकविंशः.
5.2.57: After शत and the like, and after मास, अर्धमास, and संवत्सर, **डट्** always takes the augment **तमट्** (फेम. **ङीप्**): शततमः 'hundredth', सहस्रतमः, मासतमः, अर्धमासतमः, संवत्सरतमः.
5.2.58: After षष्टि and the like when no other numeral precedes, **डट्** always takes the augment **तमट्**: षष्टितमः, सप्ततितमः. (With a preceding numeral it is optional by 5.2.56: एकषष्टः or एकषष्टितमः.)
5.2.59: In the sense of **मतुप्** (तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्), when naming a सूक्त or साम्न्, add **छ** (ईय) to a **प्रातिपदिक**: अच्छावाकीयं सूक्तम्, यज्ञायज्ञीयं साम.
5.2.60: When naming an अध्याय or अनुवाक, the **छ** (ईय) carrying **मतुप्** sense undergoes **लुक्** (drops): गर्दभाण्डोऽध्यायः (or, optionally, गर्दभाण्डीयः).
5.2.61: In **मतुप्** sense, when naming an अध्याय or अनुवाक, add **अण्** after विमुक्त and the rest: वैमुक्तोऽध्यायः, दैवासुरः.
5.2.62: In **मतुप्** sense, when naming an अध्याय or अनुवाक, add **वुन्** after गोषद and the rest: गोषदकोऽध्यायः, इषेत्वकः, मातरिश्वकः.
5.2.63: After पथिन् (seventh case), in the sense 'skilled therein', add **वुन्**: पथि कुशलः = पथकः.
5.2.64: After the **प्रातिपदिक** आकर्ष and the rest (seventh case), in the sense 'skilled therein', add **कन्**: आकर्षकः, त्सरुकः.
5.2.65: After धन and हिरण्य (seventh case), in the sense 'a craving for it', add **कन्**: धनको देवदत्तस्य, हिरण्यको देवदत्तस्य.
5.2.66: After a word for a part of one's own body (seventh case), in the sense 'absorbed in tending it', add **कन्**: केशेषु प्रसितः = केशकः. The plural स्वाङ्गेभ्यः lets it follow a compound of such words too: दन्तौष्ठकः, केशनखकः.
5.2.67: After उदर (seventh case, in the 'absorbed therein' sense), when the word means 'voracious', add **ठक्**: उदरे प्रसितः = औदरिकः. Only in the 'voracious' sense — not उदरकः 'abdominal'.
5.2.68: After सस्य 'fine quality' (third case), in the sense 'richly endowed with it', add **कन्**: सस्येन परिजातः = सस्यकः शालिः 'flawless rice', सस्यको मणिः.
5.2.69: After अंश 'a share' (accusative), in the sense 'who must take it', add **कन्**: अंशं हारी = अंशकः 'an heir'.
5.2.70: After तन्त्र 'a loom' (ablative), in the sense 'taken off it not long ago', add **कन्**: तन्त्रादचिरापहृतः = तन्त्रकः पटः 'a fresh, unbleached cloth'.
5.2.71: ब्राह्मण and उष्णिक, both with **कन्**, are irregular as a **संज्ञा**: ब्राह्मणक is a place where weapon-bearing Brahmanas live, उष्णिका is thin gruel.
5.2.72: After शीत and उष्ण, **कन्** marks one who goes about a task that way: शीतक is a sluggard, उष्णक is brisk and able.
5.2.73: अधिक, meaning 'more', is the irregular **कन्** form of अध्यारूढ with its second member dropped.
5.2.74: अनुक, अभिक, अभीक, all with **कन्**, are irregular forms meaning one free to do or fond of doing (from कम्); अभीक also irregularly lengthens its vowel.
5.2.75: After पार्श्व ('a crooked trick'), **कन्** marks one who pursues his ends by it: पार्श्वक is a trickster, a deceiver.
5.2.76: After अयःशूल and दण्डाजिन, **ठक्** and **ठञ्** respectively mark one who pursues his ends by that: आयःशूलिक is a man of violence, दाण्डाजिनिक is a hypocrite.
5.2.77: After an ordinal, **कन्** marks mastery gained on that attempt, and the ordinal **प्रत्यय** optionally drops: द्विक or द्वितीयक ग्रहण, त्रिक or तृतीयक. (For the person who masters it on that attempt, the ordinal drop is fixed: षट्क देवदत्त.)
5.2.78: After a word in the nominative standing for the genitive, **कन्** marks 'he is their leader': देवदत्तक are those whose ग्रामणी is Devadatta.
5.2.79: After शृङ्खल ('a wooden clog'), **कन्** marks 'the clog is its fetter', when the whole word means a young camel: शृङ्खलक.
5.2.80: उत्क, the irregular **कन्** form of उद्, means longing, yearning: उत्क देवदत्त is the man whose mind reaches out (उन्मनस्).
5.2.81: After a word for the time, cause, or effect of an illness, **कन्** names the illness: द्वितीयक ज्वर strikes on the second day, विषपुष्पक is caused by poison-flowers, उष्णक produces heat.
5.2.82: After a word for food in the nominative, **कन्** marks 'this is the chief food on that occasion', when the whole is a **संज्ञा**: गुडापूपिका पौर्णमासी is the full-moon day whose main fare is sugar-cakes. (वटक takes **इनि**: वटकिनी.)
5.2.83: After कुल्माष, **अञ्** marks 'this is the chief food on that occasion', when the whole is a **संज्ञा**: कौल्माषी पौर्णमासी. The ञ् triggers **वृद्धि** and accent.
5.2.84: श्रोत्रिय, ending in irregular **घन्** (with न् for accent), means one who has studied the **छन्दस्**: श्रोत्रिय ब्राह्मण.
5.2.85: After श्राद्ध, **इनि** and **ठन्** mark 'eaten by him' that very day: श्राद्धी or श्राद्धिक is one who has eaten the funeral meal.
5.2.86: After पूर्व, **इनि** marks 'done by him before' (supply any verb): पूर्वी is one who went, ate, or drank before.
5.2.87: **इनि** for 'done by him before' also comes after पूर्व when another word precedes it: कृतपूर्वी कटम् is one who made the mat before, भुक्तपूर्वी ओदनम्.
5.2.88: After इष्ट and the rest of its list, **इनि** marks 'done by him': इष्टी is one who has sacrificed, पूर्ती one who has given alms.
5.2.89: In the **छन्दस्**, परिपन्थिन् and परिपरिन् are irregular **इनि** forms meaning an adversary, one who stands against you.
5.2.90: अनुपदिन्, an irregular **इनि** form, means one who goes after, who tracks: अनुपदी गवाम् tracks the cows.
5.2.91: After साक्षात्, **इनि** marks an eyewitness, when the whole is a **संज्ञा**: साक्षिन्. The **संज्ञा** restricts it to the onlooker, not the giver or taker who also see the deed.
5.2.92: क्षेत्रिय, the irregular **घच्** form of परक्षेत्र with पर dropped, means curable only in another body: क्षेत्रिय व्याधि is an incurable disease.
5.2.93: इन्द्रिय, with acute on the last syllable, is the irregular **घच्** form for an organ of sense, taken as इन्द्र's mark, or seen, created, enjoyed, or given by इन्द्र.
5.2.94: After a word in the nominative, **मतुप्** marks 'it is his' or 'it is in him': गोमत् (गोमान्) has cows, वृक्षवत् (वृक्षवान्) has trees.
5.2.95: **मतुप्** also comes after रस and the rest of its list: रसवत्, रूपवत्, गन्धवत्. This blocks the other **मतुप्**-sense affixes for these words.
5.2.96: After a stem ending in आ that names something found only in a living being, **लच्** optionally replaces **मतुप्**: चूडाल or चूडावान्, कर्णिकाल or कर्णिकावान्.
5.2.97: After सिध्म and the rest of its list, **लच्** comes in the sense of **मतुप्**, with **मतुप्** as the alternative: सिध्मल or सिध्मवान्, गडुल or गडुवान्.
5.2.98: After वत्स and अंस, **लच्** comes in the senses of love and strength respectively: वत्सल is tender, अंसल is strong.
5.2.99: After फेन, **इलच्** and **लच्** come in the sense of **मतुप्**, with **मतुप्** as the alternative: फेनिल, फेनल, फेनवान्.
5.2.100: In the sense of **मतुप्**, **श** comes after लोमादि words, **न** after पामादि, and **इलच्** after पिच्छादि, with **मतुप्** as the alternative: लोमश or लोमवान्, पामन or पामवान्, पिच्छिल or पिच्छवान्.
5.2.101: प्रज्ञा, श्रद्धा, अर्चा, वृत्ति take **ण्** in the sense of **मतुप्** (and **मतुप्** itself also comes).
5.2.102: तपस् takes **विनि** and सहस्र takes **इनि**, both in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.104: सिकता and शर्करा take **अण्** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.105: When the sense is a locality, सिकता and शर्करा drop the **मतुप्**-sense affix by **लुप्** (keeping the base word's gender and number), or take **इलच्**, **अण्**, or **मतुप्**.
5.2.106: दन्त takes **उरच्** in the sense of having projecting teeth.
5.2.107: ऊष, सुषि, मुष्क, मधु take **र** in the sense of **मतुप्** (forming fixed names of things).
5.2.108: द्यु and द्रु take **म** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.109: केश optionally takes **व** in the sense of **मतुप्** (and **इनि**, **ठन्**, **मतुप्** also come).
5.2.110: गाण्डी and अजग take **व** in the sense of **मतुप्** when forming a name.
5.2.111: काण्ड takes **ईरन्** and अण्ड takes **ईरच्**, both in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.112: रजस्, कृषि, आसुति, परिषद् take **वलच्** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.113: दन्त and शिखा take **वलच्** in the sense of **मतुप्** when forming a name.
5.2.114: ज्योत्स्ना, तमिस्रा, शृङ्गिण, ऊर्जस्विन्, ऊर्जस्वल, गोमिन्, मलिन, मलीमस are irregularly formed in the sense of **मतुप्** as names.
5.2.115: A **प्रातिपदिक** ending in short अ takes **इनि** and **ठन्** in the sense of **मतुप्** (and **मतुप्** also comes).
5.2.116: व्रीहि and the rest take **इनि** and **ठन्** in the sense of **मतुप्** (and **मतुप्** also comes).
5.2.117: तुन्द and the rest also take **इलच्** in the sense of **मतुप्** (and **इनि**, **ठन्**, **मतुप्** also come).
5.2.118: A stem preceded in compound by एक or गो always takes **ठञ्** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.119: A stem ending in शत or सहस्र takes **ठञ्** in the sense of **मतुप्** when that शत or सहस्र follows निष्क.
5.2.120: रूप takes **यप्** in the sense of **मतुप्** when stamping or praise is denoted.
5.2.121: A stem ending in अस्, and माया, मेधा, स्रज्, take **विनि** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.122: In the **छन्दस्** **विनि** comes variously in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.123: ऊर्णा takes **युस्** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.124: वाच् takes **ग्मिनि** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.125: वाच् takes **आलच्** and **आटच्** in the sense of **मतुप्** when a talkative person is denoted.
5.2.126: स्वामिन् is irregularly formed (स्व plus **आमिन्**) when lordship is denoted.
5.2.127: अर्श and the rest take **अच्** in the sense of **मतुप्**.
5.2.128: A **द्वन्द्व** compound, a disease name, or anything denoting a fault takes **इनि** in the sense of **मतुप्** when the thing sits in a living being.
5.2.129: After वात and अतिसार, the augment **कुक्** is added before **इनि**.
5.2.130: An ordinal numeral takes **इनि** in the sense of **मतुप्** when age is denoted.
5.2.131: After सुख, दुःख and the rest of the सुखादि list, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्**, blocking the other possessive affixes; after माला, **इनि** comes when censure is meant.
5.2.132: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in धर्म, शील or वर्ण, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्**, blocking the others.
5.2.133: After हस्त, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** when the whole word names a **जाति** (species), as हस्तिन्.
5.2.134: After वर्ण, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** when the word means a **ब्रह्मचारिन्**.
5.2.135: After पुष्कर, पद्म and the rest of the पुष्करादि list, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** when the word names a locality, as पुष्करिणी.
5.2.136: After बल, उत्साह and the rest of the बलादि list, **मतुप्** is the affix, with **इनि** as the alternative — बलवान् or बलिन्.
5.2.137: After a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in मन् or म, **इनि** (इन्) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** when the whole word is a name, as प्रथिमिन्, होमिन्.
5.2.138: After कम् (water, happiness) and शम् (happiness), the seven affixes ब, भ, युस्, ति, तु, त, यस् come in the sense of **मतुप्** — कम्बः, कम्भः, कंयुः, कन्तिः, कन्तुः, कन्तः, कंयः, and likewise from शम्.
5.2.139: After तुन्दि, वलि and वटि, भ is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** — तुन्दिभः, वलिभः, वटिभः.
5.2.140: After अहम् and the indeclinable शुभम्, युस् (यु) is the affix in the sense of **मतुप्** — अहंयुः, शुभंयुः.
5.3.1: From here up to (but not including) 5.3.27, the affixes specified are **विभक्ति**.
5.3.2: These **प्राग्दिशीय** affixes come after किम्, after a **सर्वनाम**, and after बहु — but not after द्वि and the rest.
5.3.3: इदम् becomes इश् before a **प्राग्दिशीय** affix.
5.3.4: इदम् becomes एत before a **प्राग्दिशीय** affix beginning with र, and इत before one beginning with थ — एतर्हि, इत्थम्.
5.3.5: एतद् becomes अश् before a **प्राग्दिशीय** affix — अतः, अत्र.
5.3.6: सर्व optionally becomes स before a **प्राग्दिशीय** **विभक्ति** beginning with द — सर्वदा or सदा.
5.3.7: After किम्, a **सर्वनाम** or बहु in the ablative, तसिल् (तस्) is the affix — कुतः, यतः, ततः, बहुतः.
5.3.8: तसिल् (तस्) replaces the affix तस् after किम्, a **सर्वनाम** or बहु.
5.3.9: तसिल् (तस्) also comes after परि (meaning 'all') and अभि (meaning 'both') — परितः, अभितः.
5.3.10: After किम्, a **सर्वनाम** or बहु in the locative, त्रल् is the affix — कुत्र, तत्र, बहुत्र.
5.3.11: After इदम् in the locative, ह is the affix, blocking त्रल् — इह.
5.3.12: After किम् in the locative, अत् (अ) is the affix, blocking त्रल् — क्व.
5.3.13: In the **छन्दस्**, ह optionally comes after किम् in the locative, alongside the other affixes — कुह, क्व, कुत्र.
5.3.14: तसिल्, त्रल्, ह and the rest are seen after किम्, a **सर्वनाम** and बहु in cases other than the ablative and locative too — ततो भवान् or तत्र भवान् for स भवान्.
5.3.15: After सर्व, एक, अन्य, किम्, यद् and तद् in the locative, दा is the affix when time is meant, blocking त्रल् — सर्वदा, एकदा, अन्यदा, कदा, यदा, तदा.
5.3.16: After इदम् in the locative denoting time, र्हिल् is the affix, blocking ह — एतर्हि.
5.3.17: अधुना ('at this time') is irregular: इदम् becomes अश् and the affix धुन is added.
5.3.18: दानीम् also comes after इदम् in the locative denoting time — इदानीम्.
5.3.19: After तद् in the locative denoting time, दा and दानीम् are the affixes — तदा, तदानीम्.
5.3.20: In the **छन्दस्**, दा comes after इदम् and र्हि after तद्, alongside the other affixes — इदा, तर्हि, इदानीम्, तदानीम्.
5.3.21: After **किम्**, the **सर्वनाम**, and बहु etc. (the words of [[5.3.2]]) in the locative naming a time not of the current day, the **प्रत्यय** र्हिल् is added optionally: कर्हि or कदा, यर्हि or यदा, तर्हि or तदा. (The छन्दसि of earlier rules is not carried in; this holds generally.)
5.3.22: These fourteen forms are irregular: सद्यः, परुत्, परारि, ऐषमस्, परेद्यवि, अद्य, पूर्वेद्युस्, अन्येद्युस्, अन्यतरेद्युस्, इतरेद्युस्, अपरेद्युस्, अधरेद्युस्, उभयेद्युस्, उत्तरेद्युस्. The base, the **आदेश**, the **प्रत्यय**, and the particular time are all fixed by this listing — e.g. समान becomes स and takes द्यस् for 'the same day' (सद्यः); पूर्व/पूर्वतर become पर and take उत्/आरि for a year (परुत्, परारि).
5.3.23: After **किम्**, the **सर्वनाम**, and बहु etc. (the words of [[5.3.2]]), the **प्रत्यय** थाल् is added when you name a kind or manner: तथा, यथा, सर्वथा. (प्रकार is the differentiating quality that marks off a species within a genus.)
5.3.24: After इदम्, naming a kind or manner, the **प्रत्यय** थमु (थम्) is added: इत्थम्. This blocks थाल्. (The उ keeps the म् from becoming an **इत्**.)
5.3.25: After **किम्** too, naming a kind or manner, the **प्रत्यय** थमु is added: कथम्.
5.3.26: In the **छन्दस्**, after **किम्** the **प्रत्यय** था is added naming a cause, and (by च) naming a kind or manner: कथा 'why' (cause), कथा 'how' (manner).
5.3.27: After a word of direction in the locative, ablative, or nominative — when it names a direction, a place, or a time — the **प्रत्यय** अस्ताति (अस्तात्) is added without changing the sense: पुरस्तात्, अधस्तात् (each covering 'eastward', 'from the east', 'previously').
5.3.28: After दक्षिण and उत्तर in the locative, ablative, or nominative, naming a direction, place, or time, the **प्रत्यय** अतसुच् (अतस्) is added: दक्षिणतः, उत्तरतः. This blocks अस्ताति. (दक्षिणा never names a time, so for it only direction and place apply.)
5.3.29: After पर and अवर the **प्रत्यय** अतसुच् is added optionally in the sense of अस्ताति: परतः or परस्तात्, अवरतः or अवरस्तात्.
5.3.30: After a word of direction ending in **अञ्च्**, the **प्रत्यय** अस्ताति drops by **लुक्**: प्राक्, प्रत्यक्. (The feminine **प्रत्यय** of प्राची drops too, by [[1.2.49]].)
5.3.31: उपरि and उपरिष्टात् are irregular forms in the sense of अस्ताति: from ऊर्ध्व, which becomes उप and takes रिल् and रिष्टातिल्. So उपरि वसति, उपरिष्टाद् वसति.
5.3.32: पश्चात् is an irregular form in the sense of अस्ताति: अपर becomes पश्च and takes आति. So अपरस्यां दिशि = पश्चात्. (अपर likewise becomes पश्च after a preceding direction-word — दक्षिणपश्चात् — and before अर्ध — पश्चार्धः.)
5.3.33: In the **छन्दस्**, पश्च and पश्चा are irregular forms in the sense of अस्ताति, and (by च) पश्चात् as well: पश्च, पश्चा, or पश्चात् सिंहः.
5.3.34: After उत्तर and दक्षिण the **प्रत्यय** आति is added in the sense of अस्ताति: उत्तरात्, दक्षिणात् (and अधरात्).
5.3.35: After उत्तर, अधर, and दक्षिण the **प्रत्यय** एनप् (एन) is added optionally in the sense of अस्ताति, when the limit is nearby and the force is not ablative: उत्तरेण, अधरेण, दक्षिणेन वसति. (It carries locative and nominative force, not ablative. From here on, अपञ्चम्याः — 'not ablative' — governs the following rules.)
5.3.36: After दक्षिण the **प्रत्यय** आच् (आ) is added in the sense of अस्ताति, but not with ablative force: दक्षिणा वसति, दक्षिणा रमणीयम् — but दक्षिणत आगतः for 'from the south'.
5.3.37: After दक्षिण the **प्रत्यय** आहि is added in the sense of अस्ताति, and (by च) आच् as well, when the limit is distant: दक्षिणाहि or दक्षिणा वसति. (Not ablative: दक्षिणत आगतः.)
5.3.38: After उत्तर too the **प्रत्यय**s आच् (आ) and आहि are added in the sense of अस्ताति when the limit is distant: उत्तरा or उत्तराहि वसति. (Not ablative: उत्तरादागतः.)
5.3.39: After पूर्व, अधर, and अवर the **प्रत्यय** असि (अस्) is added in the sense of अस्ताति, and alongside it these become पुर्, अध्, and अव् respectively: पुरः, अधः, अवः. (अपञ्चम्याः does not govern here.)
5.3.40: The same substitution — पूर्व→पुर्, अधर→अध्, अवर→अव् — happens before the **प्रत्यय** अस्ताति: पुरस्तात्, अधस्तात्, अवस्तात्. (This shows अस्ताति still applies after these words and is not blocked by असि.)
5.3.41: Before अस्ताति the substitution of अव् for अवर is optional: अवस्तात् or अवरस्तात् वसति.
5.3.42: After a **प्रातिपदिक** naming a number, the **प्रत्यय** धा is added when it names the manner of an action: एकधा, द्विधा, त्रिधा, चतुर्धा, पञ्चधा. (विधा is प्रकार, applying to action of every kind.)
5.3.43: After a number the **प्रत्यय** धा is also added when the sense is a change in how a substance is apportioned — making one into many or many into one: एकं राशिं पञ्चधा कुरु, अनेकमेकधा कुरु. (अधिकरण is the substance, विचाल the change in number.)
5.3.44: After एक the substitute ध्यमुञ् optionally replaces धा: एकधा or ऐकध्यं कुरु. (धा is repeated in the rule so this covers both the विधा sense and the अधिकरणविचाल sense.)
5.3.45: After द्वि and त्रि the substitute धमुञ् optionally replaces धा: द्विधा or द्वैधम्, त्रिधा or त्रैधम्. (Both the विधा and अधिकरणविचाल senses.)
5.3.46: After द्वि and त्रि the substitute एधाच् (एधा) optionally replaces धा: द्वेधा, द्वैधम्, or द्विधा; त्रेधा, त्रैधम्, or त्रिधा.
5.3.47: The **प्रत्यय** पाशप् marks something as contemptible or trifling: वैयाकरणपाशः 'a wretched grammarian', याज्ञिकपाशः. (याप्य is 'contemptible'.)
5.3.48: After a **प्रातिपदिक** that is an ordinal ending in तीय, the **प्रत्यय** अन् is added — the word keeping its meaning — when a part is meant: द्वितीयो भागः, तृतीयः. (This only shifts the accent: द्विती꣡यः becomes द्वि꣡तीयः.)
5.3.49: After an ordinal below eleven, the **प्रत्यय** अन् is added — the word keeping its meaning — when a part is meant, but not in the **छन्दस्**: च꣡तुर्थः, प꣡ञ्चमः, स꣡प्तमः, न꣡वमः, द꣡शमः. (This only shifts the accent; एकादश and above are excluded.)
5.3.50: After षष्ठ and अष्टम, when a part is meant and not in the **छन्दस्**, the **प्रत्यय** ञ (अ) is added, and (by च) अन् too: षाष्ठः or षष्ठः, आष्टमः or अष्टमः.
5.3.51: After **षष्ठ**, add **कन्** (क) when a fraction of a **मान** (a grain measure) is meant; after **अष्टम**, **लुक्**-drop the affix when a part of an animal's body is meant. By च the ordinary forms stand too: **षाष्ठ**/**षष्ठ**, **आष्टम**/**अष्टम**.
5.3.52: After **एक** meaning 'alone' (not the numeral 'one'), add **आकिनिच्** (आकिन्) in the same sense; by च, **कन्** and **लुक्** also apply, the **लुक्** dropping **कन्** or **आकिनिच्**. So **एकाकिन्**, **एकक**, **एक**.
5.3.53: **चरट्** (चर, feminine in **ङीप्**) follows a **प्रातिपदिक** in its own sense when the meaning is 'this had been so before': **आढ्यचर** 'once rich'.
5.3.54: After a genitive **प्रातिपदिक**, add **रूप्य**, and by च also **चरट्**, when the meaning is 'this formerly belonged to him': **देवदत्तरूप्य**, **देवदत्तचर** 'the cow that once belonged to Devadatta'.
5.3.55: For surpassing, **तमप्** (तम) and **इष्ठन्** (इष्ठ) follow a **प्रातिपदिक** in its own sense — the superlative: **आढ्यतम**, **पटिष्ठ**, **गरिष्ठ**.
5.3.56: **तमप्** (तम) also follows a finite verb when surpassing is meant: **पचतितमाम्** 'cooks more than all the rest'. (**इक्ष्ठन्** never follows a verb.)
5.3.57: **तरप्** (तर) and **ईयसुन्** (ईयस्) follow a **प्रातिपदिक** or finite verb, for surpassing, when two things are compared or when the item is set off from another — the comparative: **आढ्यतर**, **पटीयस्**, **पचतितराम्**. They block **तमप्** and **इष्ठन्**.
5.3.58: The vowel-initial affixes **ईयसुन्** and **इष्ठन्** follow only words denoting a quality (a **गुणवचन**): **पटीयस्**, **पटिष्ठ** — but **पाचकतर**, **पाचकतम**, never *पाचीयस्*.
5.3.59: In the **छन्दस्**, the vowel-initial **इष्ठन्** and **ईयसुन्** follow a **प्रातिपदिक** ending in तृ (**तृन्** or **तृच्**): **करिष्ठ**, **दोहीयस्**.
5.3.62: Before **इष्ठन्** and **ईयसुन्**, **ज्य** also replaces **वृद्ध**: **ज्येष्ठ**, **ज्यायस्** (and, by another rule, **वर्षिष्ठ**, **वर्षीयस्**).
5.3.65: Before **इष्ठन्** and **ईयसुन्**, the affixes **विन्** and **मतुप्** are **लुक्**-dropped: **स्रजिष्ठ**, **स्रजीयस्** (from **स्रग्विन्**); **त्वचिष्ठ**, **त्वचीयस्** (from **त्वग्वत्**).
5.3.66: **रूपप्** follows a **प्रातिपदिक** or finite verb in its own sense when praise is meant: **वैयाकरणरूप** 'a celebrated grammarian', **चोररूप** 'a notorious thief'.
5.3.67: **कल्पप्** (कल्प), **देश्य**, and **देशीयर्** (देशीय) follow a **प्रातिपदिक** or finite verb that means slight incompleteness: **पटुकल्प**, **पटुदेश्य**, **पटुदेशीय** 'almost clever', **पचतिकल्पम्**.
5.3.68: For slight incompleteness, **बहुच्** (बहु) optionally follows a declined noun — but it stands before the word, not after: **बहुपटु** 'tolerably skillful', **बहुमृदु**. (By 'optionally', **कल्प** etc. also apply.)
5.3.69: **जातीयर्** (जातीय) follows a declined noun that expresses a kind or sort (**प्रकार**): **पटुजातीय** 'of the clever sort', **मृदुजातीय**.
5.3.70: The affix **क** governs every rule from here down to **इवे प्रतिकृतौ** (5.3.96).
5.3.71: **अकच्** (अक्) is inserted into an **अव्यय** or a **सर्वनाम** before its last vowel, in the senses of the **क**-section: **उच्चकैः**, **नीचकैः**, **सर्वके**, **विश्वके**. It blocks **क**.
5.3.72: **द** replaces the final क् of an **अव्यय** when **अकच्** is inserted: **धकित्** (from धिक्), **हिरकुत्** (from हिरुक्), **पृथकत्** (from पृथक्).
5.3.73: **क** and **अकच्** follow a noun or verb when the thing spoken of is unknown — unknown in its relation, not in itself: **अश्वक** 'whose horse?', **सर्वके**, **पचतकि**.
5.3.74: **क** and **अकच्** follow when the thing is spoken of as contemptible: **अश्वक** 'a sorry horse', **पचतकि** 'cooks wretchedly'.
5.3.75: **कन्** (क) follows in that same contemptible sense when the whole word is a **संज्ञा** (a name): **शूद्रक**, **धारक**, **चूर्णक**. It blocks **क**.
5.3.76: These affixes follow when **अनुकम्पा** (tender pity, endearment) is meant: **पुत्रक** 'poor little child', **वत्सक**, **स्वपितकि**.
5.3.77: They also follow, for courteous **नीति** (kindly policy), the word naming what is offered to the one pitied: **हन्त ते धानकाः** 'here, some barley for you', **एहकि**.
5.3.78: **ठच्** optionally follows a human name of more than two syllables, for pity or for courtesy joined with pity (otherwise **कन्**): **देविक**/**देवदत्तक**, **यज्ञिक**/**यज्ञदत्तक**.
5.3.79: **घन्** and **इलच्** also follow a human name of more than two syllables in that sense (and by च, **कन्** too): **देविय**, **देविल**, **देविक**, **देवदत्तक**.
5.3.80: For the Eastern grammarians, **अडच्** and **वुच्** also follow such a human name beginning with **उप** (and by च the earlier affixes too): **उपड**, **उपक**, **उपिय**, **उपिल**, **उपिक**, **उपेन्द्रदत्तक**.
5.3.81: After a species-name (व्याघ्र, सिंह...) used as a man's name, add **कन्** for affection or courtesy.
5.3.82: After a man's name ending in अजिन, add **कन्** for affection, and the second member drops before it.
5.3.83: Before ठ or any vowel-initial affix just taught, drop everything after the second vowel of the man's name.
5.3.84: For a man's name starting with शेवल, सुपरि, विशाल, वरुण, or आर्यमन्, drop everything after the third vowel before those same affixes.
5.3.85: The affixes from **क** onward come for a small amount or small number.
5.3.86: The affixes from **क** onward come for shortness of length.
5.3.87: When the short thing is a name, add **कन्** (blocking **क**).
5.3.88: After कुटी, शमी, and शुण्डा, add **र** for shortness.
5.3.89: After कुतू, add **डुपच्** (उप) for diminution; the final ऊ drops.
5.3.90: After कासू and गोणी, add **ष्टरच्** (तर, feminine in ङीष्) for diminution.
5.3.91: After वत्स, उक्षन्, अश्व, and ऋषभ, add **ष्टरच्** for slenderness.
5.3.92: After किम्, यद्, तद्, in singling out one of two, add **डतरच्** (अतर, dropping the final इम्/अद्).
5.3.93: After किम्, यद्, तद्, in singling out one of many by a question of caste, optionally add **डतमच्** (अतम, dropping the final syllable).
5.3.94: For the Eastern grammarians, after एक add **डतरच्** (one of two) and **डतमच्** (one of many) in these same senses.
5.3.96: For an imitation of a thing, add **कन्** in the sense 'like this' (अश्व → अश्वकः, a model horse).
5.3.97: Add **कन्** in the sense 'like this' when the whole word formed is a name.
5.3.98: When such a name denotes a man, the affix drops by **लुप्**, the word keeping its number and gender (चञ्चा, a straw man).
5.3.99: **कन्** likewise drops when the figure is a means of livelihood and not for sale (वासुदेवः, the idol).
5.3.100: After देवपथ and the rest, **कन्** (from इवे प्रतिकृतौ and संज्ञायां च) likewise drops.
5.3.101: After वस्ति, add **ढञ्** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.102: After शिला, add **ढ** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.103: After शाखा and the rest, add **यत्** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.104: द्रव्य (from द्रु + **यत्**) is irregularly formed and means 'fine, excellent'.
5.3.105: After कुशाग्र, add **छ** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.106: After a compound that already holds the sense 'like this', add **छ** for a further 'like this' (काकतालीयम्).
5.3.107: After शर्करा and the rest, add **अण्** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.108: After अङ्गुली and the rest, add **ठक्** in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.109: After एकशाला, optionally add **ठच्** in the sense 'like this' (otherwise **ठक्**).
5.3.110: After कर्क and लोहित, add **ईकक्** (ईक) in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.111: In the **छन्दस्**, **थाल्** comes after प्रत्न, पूर्व, विश्व, and इम (इदम्) in the sense 'like this'.
5.3.112: A word for a **पूग** (a mixed crowd of men of no fixed livelihood, banded together to make a living) takes **ञ्य** with no change of sense, unless the word begins with the band's leader's name.
5.3.113: A word for a **व्रात** (a violent band of mixed castes living by force), or one ending in च्फञ्, takes **ञ्य** with no change of sense, but not in the feminine.
5.3.114: Among the वाहीक, a word for a band living by arms takes **ञ्यट्** with no change of sense, but not when the word names a ब्राह्मण nor when the word is राजन्य. (The ट् gives the feminine ङीप्.)
5.3.115: वृक, naming a band living by arms, takes **टेण्यण्** with no change of sense. (The ट् gives the feminine ङीप्, the ण् gives वृद्धि.)
5.3.116: दामनि and the rest, and the six त्रिगर्तषष्ठ warrior-stocks, take **छ** (ईय) with no change of sense when they name a band living by arms.
5.3.117: पर्शु and the rest take **अण्**, and यौधेय and the rest take **अञ्**, with no change of sense, when they name a band living by arms.
5.3.118: After अभिजित्, बिदभृत्, शालावत्, शिखावत्, शामीवत्, ऊर्णावत्, and श्रुमत् ending in the patronymic **अण्**, comes **यञ्** with no change of sense.
5.3.119: **ञ्य** and the affixes following it (from 5.3.112 on) are **तद्राज**.
5.4.1: A word ending in पाद or शत and beginning with a numeral takes **वुन्** in a distributive sense, and the stem's final drops. (The drop is stated here, not caused by the affix, so it is not स्थानिवत् and पाद् does not become पद्.)
5.4.2: Also when the sense is a fine (दण्ड) or a gift (व्यवसर्ग). (Here there is no distributive sense.)
5.4.3: After स्थूल and the rest, **कन्** comes in the sense 'of that kind'. (This blocks जातीयर्.)
5.4.4: After a **क्त** participle, **कन्** comes when the act is not wholly finished.
5.4.5: Not when सामि (or a word meaning 'half') precedes the participle. (This blocks the स्वार्थिक **कन्**, not the **कन्** of incompleteness.)
5.4.6: बृहति takes **कन्** with no change of sense when it means an article of dress.
5.4.7: After अषडक्ष, आशितङ्गु, अलंकर्म, अलम्पुरुष, and a stem ending in अधि, comes **ख** with no change of sense.
5.4.8: A stem ending in अञ्च् optionally takes **ख** with no change of sense, except for a direction word in the feminine.
5.4.9: A stem ending in जाति takes **छ** (ईय) with no change of sense in the sense 'fitting for'.
5.4.10: A stem ending in स्थान optionally takes **छ** (ईय) when it is compounded with सस्थान, that is, 'of equal standing'.
5.4.11: To **तर**/**तम** (घ) coming after किम्, after a word ending in ए, after a finite verb, or after an indeclinable, **आम्** is added, but not when the excess belongs to a substance.
5.4.12: In the **छन्दस्**, **अम्** is also added in the same case (and, by च, **आम्** as well).
5.4.13: अनुगादिन् takes **ठक्** with no change of sense.
5.4.14: After a word ending in **णच्**, **अञ्** comes with no change of sense when the word is feminine.
5.4.15: After a stem ending in **इनुण्**, **अण्** comes with no change of sense.
5.4.16: विसारिन् takes **अण्** when the word means a fish.
5.4.17: A numeral takes **कृत्वसुच्** when the repetition of an action is being counted.
5.4.18: द्वि, त्रि, and चतुर् take **सुच्** in the sense of counting an action's repetition. (This blocks कृत्वसुच्.)
5.4.19: सकृत् replaces एक before **सुच्** when an action is counted. (This blocks कृत्वसुच्.)
5.4.20: बहु optionally takes **धा** when counting an action's repetition within a short span of time. (This blocks कृत्वसुच्, which stays as the alternative.)
5.4.21: After a word in the nominative, **मयट्** comes in the sense 'made of that' or 'abounding in that'. (The ट् gives the feminine ङीप्.)
5.4.22: When the base is a multitude, the **समूह** affixes (**तस्य समूहः** etc.) also mark 'made of it' or 'in which it occurs'; the च brings in **मयट्** too.
5.4.23: **ञ्य** comes after अनन्ता, आवसथ, इतिह, भेषजा without changing the sense.
5.4.24: **यत्** comes after a stem ending in देवता in the dative, meaning 'meant for it'.
5.4.25: **यत्** comes after पाद and अर्घ in the dative, meaning 'meant for it'; the च adds further words seen in the **छन्दस्**.
5.4.26: **ञ्य** comes after अतिथि in the dative, meaning 'meant for it'.
5.4.27: **तल्** comes after देव without changing the sense (देव → देवता).
5.4.28: **क** comes after अवि without changing the sense (अवि → अविक).
5.4.29: **कन्** comes after याव, मणि, अस्थि, ... without changing the sense.
5.4.30: **कन्** comes after लोहित when it means a gem, without changing the sense.
5.4.31: **कन्** comes after लोहित when it means a passing, impermanent color.
5.4.32: **कन्** comes after लोहित when it means something dyed red.
5.4.33: **कन्** comes after काल when it means a passing color or something dyed.
5.4.34: **ठक्** comes after विनय, समय, ... without changing the sense.
5.4.35: **ठक्** comes after वाच् when it means a message someone else spoke that is now being relayed.
5.4.36: **अण्** comes after कर्मन् when the act is one carried out on such a relayed message.
5.4.37: **अण्** comes after ओषधि when it does not mean a species.
5.4.38: **अण्** comes after प्रज्ञ, वणिज्, उशिज्, ... without changing the sense.
5.4.39: **तिकन्** comes after मृद् without changing the sense (मृद् → मृत्तिका).
5.4.40: **स** and **स्न** come after मृद् when it means excellence, blocking **रूपप्** (मृत्सा, मृत्स्ना).
5.4.41: In the **छन्दस्**, **तिल्** and **तातिल्** come after वृक and ज्येष्ठ respectively when excellence is meant, blocking **रूपप्**.
5.4.42: **शस्** optionally comes after a word meaning much or little when it is a **कारक** (बहुशस्, अल्पशस्).
5.4.43: **शस्** optionally comes after a number-word or a singular coin-word when the sense is distributive and the word is a **कारक** (द्विशस्, कार्षापणशस्).
5.4.44: **तसि** comes after the ablative that arises from joining the **कर्मप्रवचनीय** प्रति (वासुदेवतः प्रति).
5.4.45: **तसि** also comes after an **अपादान** ablative, except when that **अपादान** arises with the verbs हीय (passive of हा) or रुह् (ग्रामतः आगच्छति).
5.4.46: **तसि** comes after a non-agent instrumental governed by a verb meaning to surpass, to stand unshaken, or to blame (वृत्ततः अतिगृह्यते).
5.4.47: **तसि** comes optionally after a non-agent instrumental joined to हीय or to पाप, where no blame is meant (वृत्ततः हीयते, वृत्ततः पापः).
5.4.48: **तसि** comes optionally after a genitive when the sense is taking a side (अर्जुनतः अभवन्).
5.4.49: **तसि** comes optionally after a genitive disease-word when its curing is meant (प्रवाहिकातः कुरु).
5.4.50: **च्वि** comes after a word, joined to कृ, भू, or अस्, when the **सम्पद्यकर्तृ** takes on a state it was not in before (शुक्ली करोति, शुक्ली भवति).
5.4.51: **च्वि** comes after अरुस्, मनस्, चक्षुस्, चेतस्, रहस्, रजस्, and their final consonant drops (अरू करोति, उन्मनी भवति).
5.4.52: In the **च्वि** sense, when the thing turns into something else in its entirety (**कार्त्स्न्य**), **साति** is added optionally.
5.4.53: In the **च्वि** sense, when everything of a kind turns into something else even partially (**अभिविधि**), **साति** is added with **सम्पद्**, and also with **कृ**, **भू**, **अस्**.
5.4.54: After a word for a master, in the sense of 'under that one's control', **साति** is added with **कृ**, **भू**, **अस्**, **सम्पद्**.
5.4.55: In the sense of 'to be given to that one's keeping', **त्रा** is added, and also **साति**, with **कृ**, **भू**, **अस्**, **सम्पद्**.
5.4.56: After देव, मनुष्य, पुरुष, पुरु, मर्त्य in the accusative or locative, **त्रा** is variously added, carrying that same accusative or locative force.
5.4.57: After an imitation of an inarticulate sound (**अव्यक्तानुकरण**) whose doubled half is at least two syllables, when इति does not follow, **डाच्** is added (and the word reduplicates).
5.4.58: After द्वितीय, तृतीय, शम्ब, बीज, in the sense of ploughing, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.59: After a numeral ending in गुण, in the sense of ploughing that many times, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.60: After समय, in the sense of letting the time slip by, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.61: After सपत्त्र and निष्पत्त्र, in the sense of piercing through with violent pain, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.62: After निष्कुल, in the sense of scooping the insides out, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.63: After सुख and प्रिय, in the sense of going with the grain (pleasing another), **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.64: After दुःख, in the sense of going against the grain (paining another), **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.65: After शूल, in the sense of roasting, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.66: After सत्य, when it does not mean swearing an oath, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.67: After मद्र, in the sense of shaving the head, **डाच्** is added with **कृ**.
5.4.68: The affixes taught from here on are **समासान्त**: they attach at the end of a compound without changing its meaning.
5.4.69: No **समासान्त** is added when the first member is a word of praise (सु or अति).
5.4.70: No **समासान्त** is added after किम् used in reproach.
5.4.71: No **समासान्त** is added to a **तत्पुरुष** of राजन् and the like when नञ् precedes.
5.4.72: After पथिन् in a **तत्पुरुष** with नञ्, the **समासान्त** is optionally dropped.
5.4.73: In a **बहुव्रीहि** denoting a number, **डच्** is added, except when the last term is बहु or गण.
5.4.74: After a compound ending in ऋक्, पुर्, अप्, धुर्, पथिन्, the **समासान्त** अ is added, but not when धुर् pairs with अक्ष.
5.4.75: After सामन् and लोमन् preceded by प्रति, अनु, अव, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.76: After अक्षि when it does not mean the eye, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.77: These words take the **समासान्त** अच् irregularly: अचतुर, विचतुर, सुचतुर, स्त्रीपुंस, धेन्वनडुह, ऋक्साम, वाङ्मनस, अक्षिभ्रुव, दारगव, ऊर्वष्ठीव, पदष्ठीव, नक्तंदिव, रात्रिंदिव, अहर्दिव, सरजस, निःश्रेयस, पुरुषायुष, द्व्यायुष, त्र्यायुष, ऋग्यजुष, जातोक्ष, महोक्ष, वृद्धोक्ष, उपशुन, गोष्ठश्व.
5.4.78: After वर्चस् preceded by ब्रह्म or हस्ति, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.79: After तमस् preceded by अव, सम्, अन्ध, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.80: After वसीयस् and श्रेयस् following श्वस्, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.81: After रहस् following अनु, अव, तप्त, the **समासान्त** अच् is added.
5.4.82: **उरस्** at the end of a compound with **प्रति** before it, in the sense of the locative (in the chest), takes **अच्**: प्रत्युरसम्.
5.4.83: अनुगव is the irregular form, with **अच्**, meaning 'matching the length of the cows'.
5.4.84: द्विस्तावा and त्रिस्तावा are the irregular forms (with **अच्** and **टि**-**लोप**) when the word names a **वेदि** (altar).
5.4.85: अध्वन् at the end of a compound with an **उपसर्ग** before it takes **अच्**: प्राध्वः, निरध्वम्, प्रत्यध्वम्.
5.4.86: A **तत्पुरुष** ending in अङ्गुलि takes **अच्** when a **संख्या** or an **अव्यय** begins it: द्व्यङ्गुलम्, निरङ्गुलम्.
5.4.87: रात्रि at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** takes **अच्** after अहन्, सर्व, a word for a part of the night, संख्यात, or पुण्य — and also after a **संख्या** or an **अव्यय**: अहोरात्रः, पूर्वरात्रः, संख्यातरात्रः, द्विरात्रः.
5.4.88: Before the **टच्** of [[5.4.91]], अहन् becomes अह्न after these same words (the **संख्या**s, **अव्यय**s, सर्व, संख्यात, and the part-of-night words): द्व्यह्नः, अत्यह्नः, पूर्वाह्णः.
5.4.89: After a **संख्या** this अह्न substitution does not apply when the **तत्पुरुष** is a **समाहार** (the days counted as one whole): द्व्यहः, त्र्यहः.
5.4.90: After उत्तम (the last word of the list, पुण्य) and after एक the अह्न substitution also does not apply: पुण्याहः, एकाहः.
5.4.91: राजन्, अहन्, and सखि at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** take **टच्**: महाराजः, परमाहः, राजसखः.
5.4.92: गो at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** takes **टच्** when no **तद्धित** has been dropped in forming the compound: परमगवः, पञ्चगवम् (but पञ्चगुः, where a **तद्धित** is dropped).
5.4.93: उरस् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** takes **टच्** when it means 'the finest of its kind': अश्वोरसम्, हस्त्युरसम्.
5.4.94: अनस्, अश्मन्, अयस्, and सरस् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** take **टच्** when the compound is a **जाति** or a **संज्ञा**: उपानसम्, महानसम्, कालायसम्, मण्डूकसरसम्.
5.4.95: तक्षन् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** with ग्राम or कौट before it takes **टच्**: ग्रामतक्षः, कौटतक्षः.
5.4.96: श्वन् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** with अति before it takes **टच्**: अतिश्वः.
5.4.97: श्वन् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष**, used as the standard of comparison for something non-living, takes **टच्**: आकर्षश्वः, फलकश्वः.
5.4.98: सक्थि at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** with उत्तर, मृग, or पूर्व before it — and also as the standard of comparison — takes **टच्**: उत्तरसक्थम्, फलकसक्थम्.
5.4.99: नौ at the end of a **द्विगु** takes **टच्**: द्विनावम्, त्रिनावम्.
5.4.100: नौ at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** with अर्ध before it takes **टच्**: अर्धनावम्.
5.4.101: खारी at the end of a **द्विगु**, and खारी with अर्ध before it, optionally take **टच्** for the Eastern grammarians: द्विखारम् or द्विखारि, अर्धखारम् or अर्धखारी.
5.4.102: अञ्जलि at the end of a **द्विगु** with द्वि or त्रि before it takes **टच्**: द्व्यञ्जलम्, त्र्यञ्जलम्.
5.4.103: In the **छन्दस्**, a neuter **तत्पुरुष** ending in अन् or अस् takes **टच्** (optionally): हस्तिचर्मम्, देवच्छन्दसम्.
5.4.104: ब्रह्मन् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** takes **टच्** when the compound names a person of a particular country: सुराष्ट्रब्रह्मः, अवन्तिब्रह्मः.
5.4.105: ब्रह्मन् at the end of a **तत्पुरुष** with कु or महत् before it optionally takes **टच्**: कुब्रह्मः or कुब्रह्मा, महाब्रह्मः or महाब्रह्मा.
5.4.106: A **समाहार** **द्वन्द्व** ending in a palatal, द्, ष्, or ह् takes **टच्**: वाक्त्वचम्, समिद्दृषदम्, वाग्विप्रुषम्, छत्रोपानहम्.
5.4.107: शरत् and the rest take **टच्** when forming an **अव्ययीभाव**: उपशरदम्, प्रतिविपाशम्.
5.4.108: An **अव्ययीभाव** ending in अन् takes **टच्**: उपराजम्, अध्यात्मम्.
5.4.109: An **अव्ययीभाव** ending in a neuter word whose last syllable is अन् optionally takes **टच्**: प्रतिचर्मम् or प्रतिचर्म.
5.4.110: An **अव्ययीभाव** ending in नदी, पौर्णमासी, or आग्रहायणी optionally takes **टच्**: उपनदम् or उपनदि, उपपौर्णमासम् or उपपौर्णमासि.
5.4.111: An **अव्ययीभाव** ending in a **झय्** consonant (any mute) optionally takes **टच्**: उपसमिधम् or उपसमित्.
5.4.112: By सेनक's view, an **अव्ययीभाव** ending in गिरि optionally takes **टच्** (अन्तर्गिरम् / अन्तर्गिरि); naming सेनक is a mark of respect, since the option already carries over.
5.4.113: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in सक्थि or अक्षि, when it names a part of the body, takes the **समासान्त** **षच्**.
5.4.114: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in अङ्गुलि takes **षच्** when the compound means a piece of wood (द्व्यङ्गुलं दारु).
5.4.115: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in मूर्धन् after द्वि or त्रि takes **ष** (द्विमूर्धः, त्रिमूर्धः).
5.4.116: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in a feminine ordinal or in प्रमाणी takes **अप्** (कल्याणीपञ्चमा रात्रयः, स्त्रीप्रमाणाः).
5.4.117: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in लोमन् after अन्तर् or बहिस् takes **अप्** (अन्तर्लोमः, बहिर्लोमः).
5.4.118: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in नासिका, when it is a name, takes **अच्** and नासिका becomes नस् — but not when स्थूल precedes (द्रुणसः; not स्थूलनासिकः).
5.4.119: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in नासिका after an **उपसर्ग** takes **अच्** and नासिका becomes नस् (उन्नसः, प्रणसः) — here without the name condition.
5.4.120: सुप्रात, सुश्व, सुदिव, शारिकुक्ष, चतुरश्र, एणीपद, अजपद, प्रोष्ठपद are irregular **बहुव्रीहि**-s formed with **अच्**.
5.4.121: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in हलि or सक्थि after नञ्, दुस्, or सु optionally takes **अच्** (अहलः / अहलिः, सुसक्थः / सुसक्थिः).
5.4.122: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in प्रजा or मेधा after नञ्, दुस्, or सु always takes **असिच्** (अप्रजाः, सुमेधाः) — the option drops here.
5.4.123: बहुप्रजास् is the valid form in the Vedas (बहुप्रजा), against secular बहुप्रजः.
5.4.124: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in धर्म takes **अनिच्** when धर्म stands alone as the final member, its first member a single word (कल्याणधर्मा); not परमस्वधर्मः.
5.4.125: After सु, हरित, तृण, सोम in a **बहुव्रीहि**, the final word is जम्भन् (with **समासान्त** अम्), meaning food or tooth (सुजम्भा, सोमजम्भा).
5.4.126: दक्षिणेर्मन् is an irregular **बहुव्रीहि** used of a stag wounded on the right by a hunter (दक्षिणेर्मा मृगः).
5.4.127: A **बहुव्रीहि** denoting reciprocal action takes **इच्** (केशाकेशि, दण्डादण्डि).
5.4.128: द्विदण्डि and the rest are valid forms ending in **इच्** (द्विदण्डि प्रहरति).
5.4.129: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, जानु becomes ज्ञु after प्र and सम् (प्रज्ञुः, संज्ञुः).
5.4.130: After ऊर्ध्व, जानु optionally becomes ज्ञु (ऊर्ध्वजानुः / ऊर्ध्वज्ञुः).
5.4.131: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in ऊधस् takes **अनङ्** for its final (कुण्डोध्नी, घटोध्नी).
5.4.132: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in धनुस् takes **अनङ्** for its final (शार्ङ्गधन्वा, पुष्पधन्वा).
5.4.133: When the **बहुव्रीहि** is a name, this **अनङ्** is optional (शतधनुः / शतधन्वा).
5.4.134: A **बहुव्रीहि** ending in जाया takes **निङ्** for its final (युवजानिः, वृद्धजानिः).
5.4.135: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, the अ of गन्ध becomes इ after उत्, पूति, सु, सुरभि (उद्गन्धिः, सुगन्धिः); not तीव्रगन्धः.
5.4.136: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, the अ of गन्ध becomes इ when गन्ध means a little (सूपगन्धि भोजनम्).
5.4.137: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, the अ of गन्ध becomes इ after a word of comparison (पद्मगन्धिः, उत्पलगन्धिः).
5.4.138: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, the अ of पाद drops after a word of comparison (व्याघ्रपात्, सिंहपात्); but not after हस्ति and the rest.
5.4.139: कुम्भपदी and the rest are formed by the same dropping of पाद's अ, with पद् before the feminine ई (कुम्भपदी, शतपदी).
5.4.140: In a **बहुव्रीहि**, the अ of पाद drops after a numeral or सु (द्विपात्, त्रिपात्, सुपात्).
5.4.141: In a **बहुव्रीहि** after a numeral or सु, दन्त becomes दत् when the word states an age (द्विदन्, सुदन् कुमारः); not द्विदन्तः कुञ्जरः.
5.4.142: In the **छन्दस्**, **दन्त** final in a **बहुव्रीहि** becomes **दत्**.
5.4.143: **दन्त** final in a **बहुव्रीहि** becomes **दत्** when the compound is feminine and a **संज्ञा**.
5.4.144: After श्याव or अरोक, **दन्त** final in a **बहुव्रीहि** optionally becomes **दत्**.
5.4.145: After a word ending in अग्र, or after शुद्ध, शुभ्र, वृष, वराह, **दन्त** final in a **बहुव्रीहि** optionally becomes **दत्**; the च extends this option to unlisted cases too.
5.4.146: The final of ककुद drops in a **बहुव्रीहि** that marks an animal's age or condition.
5.4.147: त्रिककुद्, with the final of ककुद dropped in a **बहुव्रीहि**, is the name of a mountain.
5.4.148: After उत् and वि, the final of काकुद drops in a **बहुव्रीहि**.
5.4.149: After पूर्ण, the final of काकुद optionally drops in a **बहुव्रीहि**.
5.4.150: सुहृद् and दुर्हृद्, irregular **बहुव्रीहि** forms with हृदय reduced to हृद्, are 'friend' and 'foe' respectively.
5.4.151: The **प्रत्यय** कप् comes after उरस् and the rest final in a **बहुव्रीहि**.
5.4.152: कप् comes after a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in इन् when the compound is feminine.
5.4.153: कप् comes after a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in a feminine **नदी** word (final long ई or ऊ) or ending in short ऋ.
5.4.154: After any other **बहुव्रीहि** the foregoing rules don't cover, कप् is added optionally.
5.4.155: कप् does not come after a **बहुव्रीहि** that is a **संज्ञा**.
5.4.156: कप् does not come after a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in the **प्रत्यय** ईयस्.
5.4.157: कप् does not come after a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in भ्रातृ when it means 'praised'.
5.4.158: In the **छन्दस्**, कप् does not come after a **बहुव्रीहि** ending in short ऋ.
5.4.159: कप् does not come after the words नाडी and तन्त्री final in a **बहुव्रीहि** when they mean body parts.
5.4.160: निष्प्रवाणि is irregular: no कप् is added, though प्रवाणी is a **नदी** word.
6.1.1: Two stand in place of the first single-vowel portion (the first syllable is reduplicated). This heading carries एकाचः, द्वे, प्रथमस्य through the following rules up to 6.1.12.
6.1.2: When the root begins with a vowel, the two stand in place of the second single-vowel portion instead of the first.
6.1.3: When न्, द्, र् begin a conjunct consonant in that second portion, they are not reduplicated.
6.1.4: The first of the two is the **अभ्यास**.
6.1.6: जक्षि and the six roots after it are also **अभ्यस्त**.
6.1.7: A short vowel of the **अभ्यास** of तुज् and the like becomes long.
6.1.8: Before the **लिट्**, a root not already reduplicated is reduplicated.
6.1.9: A root not already reduplicated and ending in सन् or यङ् is reduplicated.
6.1.10: Before श्लु, a root not already reduplicated is reduplicated.
6.1.11: Before चङ्, a root not already reduplicated is reduplicated.
6.1.12: दाश्वान्, साह्वान्, and मीढ्वान् (from दाश्, सह्, मिह् with **क्वसु**) form without reduplication and without the **इट्** augment; साह्वान् and मीढ्वान् also lengthen the penult, and मीढ्वान् changes ह to ड.
6.1.13: Before पुत्र or पति in a **तत्पुरुष**, the य् of the affix **ष्यङ्** vocalizes to इ (**सम्प्रसारण**).
6.1.14: Before बन्धु in a **बहुव्रीहि**, the य् of **ष्यङ्** vocalizes to इ (**सम्प्रसारण**).
6.1.15: The semi-vowels of वच्, स्वप्, and the यजादि roots (यज्, वप्, वह्, वस्, वे, व्ये, ह्वे, वद्, श्वि) vocalize (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **कित्** affix.
6.1.16: The semi-vowels of ग्रह्, ज्या, वे, व्यध्, वश्, व्यच्, व्रश्च्, प्रच्छ्, and भ्रस्ज् vocalize (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **ङित्** affix, and by च before a **कित्** one too.
6.1.17: Before **लिट्** affixes, the **अभ्यास** of both the वच्-group [[6.1.15]] and the ग्रह्-group [[6.1.16]] vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**).
6.1.18: The semi-vowel of causative स्वापि vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) before **चङ्** of the reduplicated aorist.
6.1.19: The semi-vowels of स्वप्, स्यम्, and व्ये vocalize (**सम्प्रसारण**) before **यङ्** of the intensive.
6.1.21: की replaces चाय् before **यङ्** of the intensive.
6.1.22: स्फी replaces स्फाय् before the **निष्ठा** affixes.
6.1.23: स्त्या (स्त्यै, ष्ठ्यै), preceded by प्र, vocalizes its semi-vowel (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **निष्ठा** affix.
6.1.24: श्या vocalizes its semi-vowel (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **निष्ठा** affix when the sense is hardening of a fluid or cold to the touch.
6.1.25: श्या preceded by प्रति vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **निष्ठा** affix.
6.1.26: श्या preceded by अभि or अव optionally vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) before a **निष्ठा** affix.
6.1.27: श्रा optionally becomes शृ before the **निष्ठा** affix क्त in the sense of cooked.
6.1.28: पी optionally replaces प्याय् before the **निष्ठा** affixes.
6.1.29: पी replaces प्याय् before **लिट्** and **यङ्** affixes.
6.1.30: श्वि optionally vocalizes its semi-vowel (**सम्प्रसारण**) before **लिट्** and **यङ्** affixes.
6.1.31: In the causative of श्वि, the semi-vowel optionally vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) before the desiderative **सन्** and the aorist **चङ्**.
6.1.32: In the causative of ह्वे, the semi-vowel vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) before the desiderative **सन्** and the aorist **चङ्**.
6.1.33: ह्वा also vocalizes (**सम्प्रसारण**) in the **अभ्यस्त** (the reduplicated form).
6.1.35: की replaces चाय् variously in the **छन्दस्**.
6.1.36: In the **छन्दस्** these forms stand as given: अपस्पृधेथाम्, आनृचुः, आनृहुः, चिच्युषे, तित्याज, श्राताः, श्रितम्, आशीः, आशीर्ताः.
6.1.37: When one semi-vowel has vocalized, an earlier semi-vowel in the same word does not also vocalize (no **सम्प्रसारण** before a **सम्प्रसारण**).
6.1.38: In the substitute root वय् [[2.4.41]], the य् does not vocalize before **लिट्**.
6.1.39: Before a **कित्** **लिट्** affix, the य् of वय् optionally becomes व्.
6.1.41: वे does not vocalize before **ल्यप्** either.
6.1.42: The semivowel of ज्या does not undergo **संप्रसारणं** before **ल्यप्**.
6.1.43: The semivowel of व्या (व्ये) does not undergo **संप्रसारणं** before **ल्यप्**.
6.1.44: After परि, व्ये optionally undergoes **संप्रसारणं** before **ल्यप्**.
6.1.45: A root that ends in एच् (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ) in its **उपदेश** form takes आ for that एच्, but not before a **शित्** **प्रत्यय**.
6.1.46: व्ये does not take आ for its एच् before the **लिट्**.
6.1.47: स्फुर् and स्फुल् take आ for their एच् before **घञ्**.
6.1.48: क्री, इ, and जि take आ for their एच् before the **णि** of the causative.
6.1.49: सिध् takes आ for its एच् before the causative **णि** when it does not mean the next world.
6.1.50: मी, मि, and दी take आ for their final before **ल्यप्**, and also before any **प्रत्यय** that would otherwise call for the आ-for-एच् substitution.
6.1.51: ली optionally takes आ for its final before **ल्यप्** and before any **प्रत्यय** that would otherwise call for the आ-for-एच् substitution.
6.1.52: In the **छन्दस्**, खिद् optionally takes आ for its एच्.
6.1.53: After अप, गुर् optionally takes आ for its एच् before **णमुल्**.
6.1.54: चि and स्फुर् optionally take आ for their एच् before the causative **णि**.
6.1.55: वी optionally takes आ for its एच् before the causative **णि** when it means to conceive an embryo.
6.1.56: भी optionally takes आ for its एच् before the causative **णि** when the causer is itself the direct source of the fear.
6.1.57: स्मि always takes आ for its एच् before the causative **णि** when the causer is itself the direct source of the astonishment.
6.1.58: सृज् and दृश् take the augment अम् (अ) before an affix beginning with a **झल्** consonant that has no indicatory क्.
6.1.59: A root marked **अनुदात्त** in its **उपदेश** form, ending in a consonant with ऋ before it, optionally takes the augment अम् (अ) before an affix beginning with a **झल्** consonant that has no indicatory क्.
6.1.60: शीर्षन् for head occurs in the **छन्दस्**.
6.1.61: शीर्षन् replaces शिरस् before a **तद्धित** affix beginning with य्.
6.1.62: शीर्ष replaces शिरस् before a **तद्धित** affix beginning with a vowel.
6.1.63: In the weak cases (from the accusative plural on), these stems replace their fuller forms: पद् for पाद, दत् for दन्त, नस् for नासिका, मास् for मास, हृद् for हृदय, निश् for निशा, असन् for असृज्, यूषन् for यूष, दोषन् for दोष, यकन् for यकृत्, शकन् for शकृत्, उदन् for उदक, आसन् for आस्य।
6.1.64: An initial ष् of a root in the **धातुपाठ** becomes स्.
6.1.65: An initial ण् of a root in the **धातुपाठ** becomes न्.
6.1.66: व् and य् drop (**लोप**) before a **वल्** consonant (any consonant except य्).
6.1.67: The affix वि drops (**लोप**) when it is reduced to the single consonant व्.
6.1.68: The single-consonant affix (the स् of सु, and the त्, स् of ति, सि) drops after a consonant; and सु's स् drops after the long ई of ङी and the long आ of आप्.
6.1.69: After a stem ending in ए, ओ, or a short vowel, the consonant of the **सम्बुद्धि** (vocative singular) affix drops.
6.1.70: In the **छन्दस्**, the affix शि (the इ of the neuter nominative and accusative plural) variously drops.
6.1.71: A root ending in a short vowel takes the augment त् (तुक्) before a **कृत्** affix with an indicatory प्.
6.1.72: In every rule from here through [[6.1.157]], supply **संहितायाम्** (in continuous, unbroken speech).
6.1.73: Before छ, a preceding short vowel takes the augment **तुक्** (त्). The augment attaches to the short vowel itself, not to the word that ends in it.
6.1.74: Before छ, the particle आ (as a **गति**) and the prohibitive मा (as आङ् and माङ्) take the augment **तुक्** (त्).
6.1.75: Before छ, a preceding long vowel takes the augment **तुक्** (त्). The augment attaches to the long vowel itself.
6.1.76: Before छ, a long vowel at the end of a **पद** optionally takes the augment **तुक्** (त्).
6.1.77: Before any vowel, the **इक्** vowels (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ) become the corresponding **यण्**: इ→य्, उ→व्, ऋ→र्, ऌ→ल्.
6.1.78: Before a vowel, ए, ऐ, ओ, औ become अय्, आय्, अव्, आव् respectively.
6.1.79: Before a **प्रत्यय** beginning with य्, ओ becomes अव् and औ becomes आव्.
6.1.80: A root's final ओ or औ becomes अव् or आव् before a य्-initial **प्रत्यय** only when that same **प्रत्यय** produced the ओ or औ in the first place.
6.1.81: In क्षय्य and जय्य the ए becomes अय् only when the sense is "possible to do" (क्षि, जि with यत्).
6.1.82: In क्रय्य the ए becomes अय् only when the sense is "put out for sale" (क्री with यत्).
6.1.83: In the **छन्दस्**, भी and प्र+वी with यत् give the forms भय्य and प्रवय्य (ए becomes अय्).
6.1.84: In every rule from here through [[6.1.111]], supply: one substitute replaces both the preceding and the following sound (एकादेश).
6.1.85: This single substitute counts as the final of the preceding form and the initial of the following form.
6.1.86: For ष्-substitution (स्→ष्) and for the **तुक्** augment, treat the single substitute (एकादेश) as if it had not happened (it blocks operations that depend on it).
6.1.87: Before a vowel, a preceding अ or आ together with that vowel becomes the corresponding **गुण** (अ/आ + vowel → **गुण**).
6.1.88: Before a diphthong (एच्: ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), a preceding अ or आ together with it becomes the corresponding **वृद्धि** (अ/आ + diphthong → **वृद्धि**).
6.1.89: A preceding अ or आ becomes **वृद्धि** with the ए of एति (root इ) and एधति (root एध्), and with the ऊ of ऊठ् (the substitute for वा in वाह्).
6.1.90: Before any vowel, the augment आट् together with that vowel becomes **वृद्धि**.
6.1.91: When an **उपसर्ग** ending in अ or आ is followed by a root beginning with short ऋ, the two become **वृद्धि**.
6.1.92: By आपिशलि's view, when an **उपसर्ग** ending in अ or आ is followed by a denominative verb beginning with ऋ, the two optionally become **वृद्धि**.
6.1.93: The ओ of a nominal stem together with the अ of the accusative endings अम् and शस् becomes आ (गो + अम् → गाम्).
6.1.94: When an **उपसर्ग** ending in अ or आ is followed by a root beginning with ए or ओ, the two become the second vowel (पररूप).
6.1.95: A preceding अ or आ together with the ओ of ओम् or the आ of the **उपसर्ग** आङ् becomes the second vowel (पररूप).
6.1.96: A preceding अ or आ (not at the end of a **पद**) together with the उ of the ending उस् becomes the second vowel (पररूप).
6.1.97: A short अ (not at the end of a **पद**) together with a following **गुण** vowel becomes that following **गुण** (पररूप).
6.1.98: In a word imitating an inarticulate sound, its final अत् together with the इ of इति becomes इ (पटत् + इति → पटिति).
6.1.99: When the sound-imitation word is doubled, this merger does not apply automatically; for the final त् of the doubled part with the इ of इति, the इ is the substitute only optionally.
6.1.100: When such a doubled sound-imitation word takes the affix डाच्, the final त् of the first member together with the initial consonant of the second member always becomes that following consonant (पररूप).
6.1.101: Before a homogeneous (सवर्ण) vowel, an **अक्** vowel (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ, अ and their long forms) together with it becomes the corresponding long vowel (दधि + इन्द्रः → दधीन्द्रः).
6.1.102: When a stem's simple vowel meets the vowel of a Nominative or Accusative ending (any number), both become a single long vowel homogeneous with the first.
6.1.103: After that long vowel homogeneous with the first, the स् of the Accusative ending **शस्** becomes न् in the masculine.
6.1.104: That single long vowel does not form when अ or आ meets a Nominative or Accusative ending beginning with a vowel other than अ.
6.1.105: That single long vowel does not form when a long vowel meets the Nominative plural **जस्** or a Nominative/Accusative ending beginning with a vowel other than अ.
6.1.106: In the **छन्दस्**, after a long vowel before **जस्** or such a vowel, the single long vowel optionally forms.
6.1.107: When a simple vowel meets the अ of the ending **अम्**, both become the first vowel.
6.1.108: When a **सम्प्रसारण** vowel (a semivowel turned back into its vowel) meets a following vowel, both become the first vowel.
6.1.109: When ए or ओ ending a **पद** meets a following short अ, both become that ए or ओ.
6.1.110: When ए or ओ meets the अ of the Ablative/Genitive singular ending **अस्** (**ङसि**, **ङस्**), both become that ए or ओ.
6.1.111: When ऋ meets the अ of the Ablative/Genitive singular ending **अस्** (**ङसि**, **ङस्**), both become short उ.
6.1.112: After सखि and पति, once their इ has become य्, the अ of the Ablative/Genitive singular **ङसि**/**ङस्** becomes उ.
6.1.113: When **रु** (the र् that replaces a final स्) stands between two short अ, neither प्लुत, it and the preceding अ become उ.
6.1.114: When **रु** follows a short अ that is not प्लुत and a soft consonant (**हश्**) follows, the अ and **रु** become उ.
6.1.115: Inside a **पाद** of a Vedic verse, a final ए or ओ and the following अ each keep their own form, unless व् or य् follows that अ.
6.1.116: Inside a **पाद**, ए or ओ and the following अ keep their forms before अव्यात्, अवद्यात्, अवक्रमुः, अव्रत, अयम्, अवन्तु, अवस्यु, even though व् or य् follows.
6.1.117: In the **यजुर्वेद**, उरस् ending in ओ and the following short अ each keep their form.
6.1.118: In the **यजुर्वेद**, the following अ keeps its form after आपो, जुषाणो, वृष्णो, वर्षिष्ठे, and after अम्बे or अम्बाले standing before अम्बिके.
6.1.119: In the **यजुर्वेद**, when अङ्गे is followed by अङ्गे, the ए and the following short अ each keep their form.
6.1.120: In the **यजुर्वेद**, when an **अनुदात्त** अ followed by a guttural (**कु**) or ध follows ए or ओ, the ए or ओ and that अ each keep their form.
6.1.121: In the **यजुर्वेद**, when the **अनुदात्त** अ of अवपथास् follows ए or ओ, both keep their form.
6.1.122: Everywhere, in **छन्दस्** and in ordinary speech, ए or ओ of गो and a following अ optionally keep their forms.
6.1.123: By स्फोटायन, the ओ of गो becomes **अवङ्** before any vowel.
6.1.124: The ओ of गो becomes अव् before a vowel of the word इन्द्र.
6.1.125: **प्लुत** and **प्रगृह्य** vowels keep their form before a vowel, blocking any change that vowel would trigger.
6.1.126: In **छन्दस्**, the particle आङ् becomes nasalized आँ before a vowel and keeps that form.
6.1.127: By शाकल्य, an **इक्** vowel (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ) before a non-homogeneous vowel keeps its form, and if long it shortens.
6.1.128: By शाकल्य, a simple vowel (**अक्**) before ऋ keeps its form, and if long it shortens.
6.1.129: Before इति in the **पदपाठ**, a **प्लुत** vowel is treated as if it were ordinary (**अप्लुत**), so it undergoes sandhi.
6.1.130: By चाक्रवर्मण, the **प्लुत** ई३ before a vowel is treated as if it were ordinary.
6.1.131: The final व् of the stem दिव् becomes उ when दिव् is a **पद**.
6.1.132: After एतद् and तद्, the nominative singular स् drops before a consonant, when the word has no **क** ([[5.3.71]]) in it and no negative particle compounded with it.
6.1.133: In the **छन्दस्**, the nominative singular स् variously drops after स्य (meaning 'he') before a consonant.
6.1.134: The nominative singular of स (meaning 'he') drops before a vowel, if dropping it completes the metrical foot.
6.1.135: Adhikara through [[6.1.157]]: in each following rule supply 'the augment **सुट्** (स्) is added before क'.
6.1.136: The **सुट्** still goes before क even when the augment **अट्** ([[6.4.71]]) or the reduplicate stands between the preverb and कृ.
6.1.137: कृ takes **सुट्** before its क after सम्, परि, उप when the sense is adorning.
6.1.138: कृ also takes **सुट्** before its क after सम्, परि, उप when the sense is bringing together.
6.1.139: कृ takes **सुट्** before its क after उप when the sense is taking pains over something, altering by preparing, or supplying what a sentence leaves unsaid.
6.1.140: कृ (किरति) takes **सुट्** before its क after उप when the sense is cutting or reaping.
6.1.141: किरति takes **सुट्** before its क after उप and प्रति when the sense is causing harm.
6.1.142: किरति takes **सुट्** before its क after अप when the sense is four-footed animals or birds scratching at the ground.
6.1.144: अपरस्पर, formed with **सुट्**, is used when the sense is unbroken, continuous action.
6.1.145: गोष्पद, formed with **सुट्**, is used for ground that cows visit or do not visit, or for a measure of quantity.
6.1.146: आस्पद, formed with **सुट्**, is a settled place or standing.
6.1.147: आश्चर्य, formed with **सुट्**, is what is unusual, a marvel.
6.1.149: अपस्कर, formed with **सुट्**, is a part of a chariot.
6.1.150: विष्किर, formed optionally with **सुट्**, is a kind of bird; the other form is विकिर.
6.1.151: In a **मन्त्र**, चन्द्र takes **सुट्** as the second member of a compound after a short vowel.
6.1.152: The root कश् takes **सुट्** after प्रति, giving प्रतिष्कश (an emissary).
6.1.153: प्रस्कण्व and हरिश्चन्द्र, formed with **सुट्**, are the two Rishis of those names.
6.1.154: मस्कर (formed with **सुट्**) is a bamboo, and मस्करिन् is a wandering mendicant.
6.1.155: कास्तीर and अजस्तुन्द, formed with **सुट्**, are names of cities.
6.1.156: कारस्कर, formed with **सुट्**, is a tree.
6.1.157: पारस्कर and the rest, formed with **सुट्**, are proper names.
6.1.158: A **पद**, except for one syllable, is **अनुदात्त** (every syllable carries no accent except the single one some rule marks).
6.1.159: A stem ending in the **कृत्** affix **घञ्** has its **उदात्त** on the last syllable if it comes from कृष् (कर्षति) or contains a long आ.
6.1.160: उञ्छ and the rest carry the **उदात्त** on their last syllable.
6.1.161: An **अनुदात्त** vowel becomes **उदात्त** when a preceding **उदात्त** drops on its account.
6.1.162: A **धातु** has **उदात्त** on its last syllable.
6.1.163: A stem formed by an affix marked with indicatory च् takes **उदात्त** on its last syllable — the stem and affix counting as one whole.
6.1.164: A stem formed by a **तद्धित** affix marked with indicatory च् takes **उदात्त** on its last syllable; this च्-accent blocks a competing ञ्-accent.
6.1.165: A stem formed by a **तद्धित** affix marked with indicatory क् takes **उदात्त** on its last syllable.
6.1.166: The nominative plural जस् of तिसृ takes **उदात्त** on its last syllable.
6.1.167: चतुर् before the accusative plural शस् takes **उदात्त** on its last syllable.
6.1.168: When the stem before the locative-plural सु is monosyllabic, the case-endings from the instrumental onward take **उदात्त**.
6.1.169: When that monosyllabic end-**उदात्त** word stands at the end of a non-fixed compound, those same case-endings optionally take **उदात्त**.
6.1.170: In the **छन्दस्**, after a stem ending in अञ्च्, the non-**सर्वनामस्थान** case-endings — including शस् — take **उदात्त**.
6.1.171: The non-**सर्वनामस्थान** case-endings take **उदात्त** after a stem ending in ऊठ् (the substitute for the वा of वाह्), and after इदम्, after पद् etc. (through [[6.1.63]]), after अप्, पुंस्, रै, and दिव्.
6.1.172: After अष्टन् in its long form अष्टा, the non-**सर्वनामस्थान** case-endings take **उदात्त**.
6.1.173: After an end-**उदात्त** शतृ participle that lacks the नुम् augment, the feminine ई (**नदी**) and the vowel-initial non-**सर्वनामस्थान** case-endings take **उदात्त**.
6.1.174: When a **यण्** preceded by a consonant replaces an **उदात्त** final vowel of the stem, those **नदी** and vowel-initial non-**सर्वनामस्थान** endings take **उदात्त**.
6.1.175: But not when that **यण्** replaces the feminine ऊङ् or the final vowel of a **धातु**.
6.1.176: मतुप् (मत्/वत्) takes **उदात्त** after an end-**उदात्त** stem ending in a light vowel, or when it carries the नुट् augment.
6.1.177: The genitive plural नाम् optionally takes **उदात्त** after an end-**उदात्त** stem that ends in a light vowel (counting the vowel as light as it stands before मतुप्).
6.1.178: In the **छन्दस्**, नाम् variously takes **उदात्त** after the feminine ई (ङी).
6.1.179: Consonant-initial case-endings take **उदात्त** after the **षट्** numerals and after त्रि and चतुर्.
6.1.180: When त्रि, चतुर्, or a **षट्** numeral takes a झल्-initial ending and the resulting word has three or more syllables, **उदात्त** falls on its penultimate syllable.
6.1.181: In ordinary speech that penultimate **उदात्त** is optional.
6.1.182: The rules from [[6.1.168]] on do not apply after गो, after श्वन् (or stems ending in them), after a stem showing अ or आ before the nominative-singular सु, after राज्, after a stem ending in अञ्च्, or after कुञ्च् and कृत्.
6.1.183: After दिव्, a झल्-initial case-ending stays unaccented.
6.1.184: After नृ, a झल्-initial case-ending is optionally unaccented.
6.1.185: An affix marked with indicatory त् is **स्वरित**.
6.1.186: A **सार्वधातुक** personal ending is unaccented after the तासि of the periphrastic future, after a **धातु** marked in the **धातुपाठ** with an unaccented vowel or with indicatory ङ् (except ह्नुङ् and इङ्), and after a root taught with final अ in **उपदेश**.
6.1.187: An aorist formed with सिच् optionally takes **उदात्त** on its first syllable.
6.1.188: After स्वप् etc. and after हिंस्, a vowel-initial **सार्वधातुक** ending — the vowel not being the इट् augment — optionally puts **उदात्त** on the first syllable.
6.1.189: A reduplicated stem takes **उदात्त** on its first syllable before a vowel-initial **सार्वधातुक** ending whose vowel is not नुट्.
6.1.190: A reduplicated stem also takes **उदात्त** on its first syllable before an unaccented ending (तिप्, सिप्, मिप्).
6.1.191: सर्व takes **उदात्त** on its first syllable before a **सुप्** ending.
6.1.192: In भी, ह्री, भृ, हु, मद्, जन्, धन्, दरिद्रा, जागृ and their reduplicated stems, the syllable just before the affix takes the acute when a **पित्** **सार्वधातुक** singular ending follows.
6.1.193: Before an affix marked with **इत्** ल्, the syllable just before the affix takes the acute.
6.1.194: Before the absolutive affix णमुल्, the first syllable optionally takes the acute.
6.1.195: A root that ends in a vowel in its **उपदेश** form optionally takes the acute on its first syllable before the यक् of the passive when the agent acts on itself (**कर्तृ**).
6.1.196: Before the perfect 2nd singular ending थल् carrying the augment इट्, the acute falls optionally on the first syllable, on the इट्, or on the ending.
6.1.197: A form built with an affix marked with **इत्** ञ् or न् always takes the acute on its first syllable.
6.1.198: A vocative (**आमन्त्रित**) takes the acute on its first syllable.
6.1.199: पथिन् and मथिन् take the acute on their first syllable before a **सर्वनामस्थान** ending.
6.1.200: An infinitive in तवै takes the acute on its first syllable and its last syllable at once.
6.1.201: क्षय, meaning a dwelling, takes the acute on its first syllable and its last syllable at once.
6.1.202: जय, in the sense of the means by which one wins, takes the acute on its first syllable.
6.1.203: वृष and the rest take the acute on their first syllable.
6.1.204: A word naming the standard of comparison (**उपमान**) takes the acute on its first syllable when it serves as a name (**संज्ञा**).
6.1.205: A disyllabic **निष्ठा** participle in त takes the acute on its first syllable when it is a name (**संज्ञा**), unless that first syllable holds आ.
6.1.206: शुष्क and धृष्ट take the acute on their first syllable.
6.1.207: आशित, meaning the one who has eaten (the agent), takes the acute on its first syllable.
6.1.208: रिक्त optionally takes the acute on its first syllable.
6.1.209: In the **छन्दस्**, जुष्ट and अर्पित optionally take the acute on their first syllable.
6.1.210: In a **मन्त्र**, जुष्ट and अर्पित always take the acute on their first syllable.
